Title, purpose, and authority
Section 1.1
TITLE, PURPOSE, AND 
AUTHORITY
1.1.1 Title
This Ordinance shall be known and may be 
cited as the “Zoning Ordinance of the City of 
Manchester, New Hampshire” referred to herein as 
“this Ordinance.” References to “this Ordinance” 
may include all documents incorporated herein by 
reference, including, but not limited to, the Official 
Zoning Maps for the City of Manchester.
1.1.2 Purpose
This Ordinance is designed and adopted to protect 
and promote the public safety, convenience, 
comfort, aesthetics, prosperity, health, and general 
welfare of the inhabitants of the City of Manchester, 
New Hampshire and to implement the policy goals 
of the Manchester Master Plan, as they relate to 
land use. It does so in the following ways:
A. Physical Development
Regulating the physical development of land 
according to the:
1. Height, number of stories, and size of structures; 
2. Lot sizes, the percentages of lots that may be 
occupied, and the sizes of yards, courts, and other 
open spaces; 
3. Density of population; and
4. Location, uses, and appearance of buildings, 
structures, and land for business, industrial, 
residential, or other purposes;
B. Safety
Securing safety from fires, panic, explosion, noxious 
fumes, and other such hazards and dangers, and to 
control nuisance-producing uses of land;
C. Light, Air, Privacy and Access
Promoting adequate light, air, privacy, and 
convenience of access to property;
D. Prevent Overcrowding
Preventing undue concentration of population, 
overcrowding of land, and undue congestion in the 
streets;
E. Resources
Assuring the proper use of natural resources to 
prevent pollution of air and water, to protect property 
from flooding and accelerated erosion, to protect 
historic and archaeological resources, to protect 
wetlands, and to conserve natural beauty and open 
space;
F. Property Values
Conserving property values by preventing the 
harmful encroachment of incompatible uses, and 
by providing for the elimination of those uses that 
adversely affect the neighborhood character, 
development, and value of property, and by ensuring 
that any proposed development is compatible in use, 
scale, and building design within the neighborhood 
in which the development is proposed;
G. Land Use and Growth
Encouraging the most appropriate use of land, and 
allowing for planned, orderly, and beneficial growth; 
and
H. Economic Development
Promoting economic development and the expansion 
of the city’s tax base.
1.1.3 Authority
This Ordinance is adopted pursuant to the authority 
conferred by the New Hampshire Revised Statutes 
Annotated, Title LXIV, Planning and Zoning, as 
most recently amended. Authority for this Ordinance 
includes the power to adopt innovative land use 
controls pursuant to RSA 674:16, including but not 
limited to the specific methods of innovative land 
use controls contained in RSA 674:21.

CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 3
General Provisions
ARTICLE 1
Section 1.2
GENERAL PROVISIONS
1.2.1 Jurisdiction
This Ordinance shall be effective within the 
corporate boundaries of the City of Manchester, 
New Hampshire.
1.2.2 Effective Date
The Zoning Ordinance was originally adopted and 
became effective on January 18, 1927. After 1927, 
the City adopted entirely new zoning ordinances 
in 1965 and 2001, while making additional 
amendments to those ordinance. This Ordinance, 
which represents a comprehensive amendment of 
the Zoning Ordinance, shall take effect on March 
1st, 2026. Any complete application for a permit to 
construct, alter, use, or occupy any land or building 
that was filed with the Planning and Community 
Development Department prior to the effective date 
of this Ordinance shall be subject to the provisions 
that were in effect as of the date of the application’s 
submission.
1.2.3 Applicability
A. General
No person may use or occupy any land or buildings, 
or authorize or permit the use or occupancy of 
land or buildings under their control, except in 
accordance with all of the applicable provisions of 
this Ordinance. For the purposes of this Section, the 
“use” or “occupancy” of a building or land relates to 
anything and everything that is done in, on, or to that 
building or land.
B. Exemptions 
This Ordinance shall not apply to any land, building, 
or structure that is:
1. Owned or occupied by the United States, 
the State of New Hampshire, the County of 
Hillsborough, the City of Manchester, or an agent 
thereof; and 
2. Is used for a public purpose that is statutorily or 
traditionally governmental in nature.
1.2.4 Relationship to Existing
Zoning Ordinance
To the extent that the provisions of this Ordinance 
are the same in substance as the previously 
adopted provisions that they replace in the 
Zoning Ordinance, they shall be considered as 
continuations thereof and not as a new enactment, 
unless otherwise specifically provided. Any violation 
of the previously adopted provisions shall continue 
to be a violation under this Ordinance, unless the 
provisions changed to no longer prohibit the use, 
occupancy, or structure. 
1.2.5 Relationship to Other
Ordinances and Regulations
Wherever the provisions of this Ordinance conflict 
with any other ordinance, statute, law, or duly 
promulgated rule or regulation, the most restrictive 
or the higher standards shall apply. 
1.2.6 Relationship to the Master
Plan
It is intended that this Ordinance implement the 
planning policies and goals expressed in the Master 
Plan of the City of Manchester, New Hampshire, as 
amended.
1.2.7 Relationship to Private
Covenants and Restrictions
The provisions of this Ordinance shall not be 
construed to impair, interfere with, abrogate, annul, 
or enforce (except in the case of a condition of 
approval pursuant to Section 10.3.1.B. Enforcement 
of Approvals, of this Ordinance) the provisions of 
private restrictions placed on property by covenant, 
easement, deed, or agreement, provided that where 
this Ordinance imposes a greater restriction or a 
higher standard, the provisions of this Ordinance 
shall govern.

ARTICLE 2: DEFINITIONS
Section 2.1
WORD USAGE
The following shall be applicable to certain words
used in this Ordinance and the interpretation of this
Ordinance. Unless the context or natural construction
of the wording clearly indicates otherwise:
1. All words used in the present tense include the
future tense; all words in the plural number include
the singular number and all words in the singular
number include the plural number.
2. The words “must” and “shall” are mandatory.
3. The word “may” is permissive.
4. The particular shall control the general.
5. The words “used” or “occupied” include the words
“intended”, “designed”, “maintained”, or “arranged”
to be used or occupied.
6. The words “building,” “structure,” “lot,” “land,” or
“premise” shall be construed as though followed by
the words “or any portion thereof.
7. In the case of any difference of meaning or
implication between the text of this Ordinance and
any caption or illustration, the text shall control.
Where in conflict, numerical metrics shall take
precedence over graphical metrics.
8. The word “permitted” or words “permitted by
right,” whether or not capitalized, means permitted
without needing to meet the requirements for a
Conditional Use Permit or Special Exception.
9. The word “applicant” includes any authorized
agent of the applicant.
10. Unless expressly provided otherwise, all public
officials, bodies, and agencies to which reference is
made are those of the City.
Section 2.2
UNDEFINED TERMS
Terms and words not defined herein but defined in
the Building Code shall have meanings given therein
unless a contrary intention clearly appears. Words
not defined in either place shall have their common
meaning unless otherwise stated.
WORD USAGE
Section 2.3
DEFINED TERMS
General terms used throughout this Ordinance are
defined within this Section. Terms pertaining mostly to
specific sections of this Ordinance are defined within
that section. For instance, definitions associated with
principal, accessory, and temporary uses are defined
within Section 4.4, Section 4.6, and Section 4.7,
respectively. All defined terms shall have the meanings
set forth in their definitions, unless the context clearly
indicates or requires a different meaning.
A
Abandonment: The visible or otherwise apparent intention
of an owner to discontinue the use of a building, or structure,
or premises, or the removal of the characteristic equipment
or furnishings used in the performance of the use without its
replacement by similar equipment or furnishings.
Access: As a noun, a legal and physical means of entering
premises, whether by adjacency, easement, or otherwise;
as a verb, the act of entering premises.
Accessory Dwelling Unit: See Section 4.6.1 Accessory to
Residential Uses.
Accessory Structure: Any structure that is customarily and
clearly incidental and subordinate in size, area, height, and
intensity to a principal structure or use and is located on the
same lot as the principal structure or use. Where a structure
is attached to a principal structure, it shall be considered a
part thereof, and not an accessory structure. See Section
5.6, Accessory Structures.
Accessory Use: A use that exists on the same lot as the
principal use of the property to which it is related and that is
customarily incidental and subordinate to the principal use.
See Section 4.5, Accessory Uses .
Addition: An extension or increase in floor area, volume, or
height of a building or structure.
Airport: That area of land or water, whether constructed
or not, which has been approved by the New Hampshire
Commissioner of Transportation for Manchester-Boston
Regional Airport as a site for the landing and taking off of
aircraft, utilized or to be utilized by the public as a point of
arrival or departure by air.
Airport Approach Zone: An overlay district of this Ordinance
which represents the airspace of Manchester-Boston
Regional Airport, as most recently defined in accordance

ARTICLE 2: DEFINITIONS
Board of Adjustment: The Zoning Board of Adjustment of
the City.
Buildable Lot Area: The contiguous area of a lot or
other parcel of land excluding wetlands, land with slopes
over 25 percent, water bodies, regulatory floodways, and
land restricted from development by existing or proposed
easements, covenants or other legal restriction. The lot size
requirements within Article 5: Building and Lot Standards,
represent the minimum buildable lot area required by this
Ordinance.
Building: Any structure used for, or intended for, supporting
or sheltering any use or occupancy.
Building Code: The current Building Code of the City of
Manchester, as most recently adopted by the Board of
Mayor and Aldermen, pursuant to RSA 674:51.
C
Caliper: The diameter of a tree trunk, measured in inches,
at six inches above the ground.
Canopy: A roofed structure constructed of fabric or other
material supported by a building or by supports extending
directly to the ground under the canopy, placed so as to
extend outward from the building, providing a protective
shield for doors, windows, and other openings.
Cellar: See “Basement”.
Certificate of Occupancy / Occupancy Letter: The final
permission required from the Planning and Community
Development Department prior to the occupancy or
change of occupancy of the entirety or portion of a building,
structure, or lot, and which reflects the conclusion of the
work allowed by any applicable building permit. A building
or structure shall not be used or occupied, and a change of
occupancy of a building or structure or portion thereof shall
not be made, until the Department has issued a certificate
of occupancy therefor as provided herein. Issuance of
a certificate of occupancy shall not be construed as an
approval of a violation of the provisions of this Ordinance or
of other city ordinances and regulations.
City: The City of Manchester, New Hampshire.
Community Center: A building or structure, operated by
a non-profit organization for use devoted primarily to the
advancement of educational, recreational, welfare, or civic
pursuits and social activities, excluding facilities in which
liquor is served. See Assembly, Neighborhood or Assembly,
General in Section 4.3, Principal Uses .
DEFINED TERMS
Conditional Use: A land use that may be approved by the
Planning Board in districts where such use is specifically
authorized by this Ordinance and where the Planning Board
finds that such use can be developed in accordance with the
provisions of Section 10.1, Conditional Use Permits .
Condominium: A building, group of buildings, or portion
thereof, in which units are owned individually, and the
structure, common areas, or facilities are owned by all the
owners on a proportional, undivided basis, as further defined
in RSA 356-B, as amended.
Construction: The act of adding an addition to an existing
structure or the erection of a new structure.
Curb Cut: A legally designated vehicular point of access
from a street to a driveway.
D
Day-Night Sound Level (Ldn): A cumulative aircraft noise
index which estimates the exposure to aircraft noise and
relates the estimated exposure to an unexpected community
response. The Day-Night Sound Level noise metric assesses

DEFINED TERMS
Direct Access: The configuration of a parking space on a
lot such that it is immediately adjacent to a street or alley
and can access that street or alley without the need to use
a drive aisle or other intermediate space. A tandem parking
space, where permitted, shall be considered to have direct
access to a street or alley where the space directly in front
of or behind it has direct access.
Director: The Director of the Planning and Community
Development Department of the City of Manchester, New
Hampshire.
Dormer: Any structure whose framing projects out from a
sloping roof to form a vertical wall designed to accommodate
a window or other opening.
Drive-Through: A structure, or portion of a structure, that
is designed to provide products or services directly to
customers in a motor vehicle. See Section 4.5, Accessory
Uses .
Driveway: That portion of a lot designed and intended for
access to an off-street parking or loading area, accessory
garage, parking lot, or parking structure.
Dwelling: A building or portion thereof used exclusively for
residential occupancy, including single family, two-family
and multifamily dwellings, but not including a Residential
Care Facility, a Rooming House, or those uses listed under
Section 4.3-A.2 - Lodging in the Table of Principal Uses.
Dwelling Unit: A single unit providing complete,
independent living facilities for one or more persons,
including permanent provisions for sleeping, cooking, and
sanitation. In accordance with RSA 674:16, the maximum
number of people aged 18 years or more who may live in
a dwelling unit is equal to no more than two per bedroom.
E
Easement: A nonpossessory right of use over the real
property of another, such as for access, utility, or the flowage
of water.
Eave: The part of a roof that meets or overhangs the walls
of a building.
Elevation : (1) An exterior wall of a building, which need not
be a Faç ade, as defined herein; or (2) the height of land or
a structure above a given level, most often sea level. See
also “Façade.”

2
E
L
An architectural feature that is a C
Expression Line:
I
decorative, three-dimensional, linear element, horizontal or T
vertical, protruding or indented at least two inches from the R
exterior façade of a building and with a minimum width or A
height of one-and-one-half (1 1/2) inches, typically utilized
to delineate floors or stories of a building.
F
Façade: The exterior wall of a building that is set along any
front or street lot line. See also “ Elevation”.
[IMAGE]
Façade, Primary: The elevation of a building facing onto
the front lot line that contains the primary entrance(s), being
those customarily providing entry to a living room, main
entry, lobby, waiting room or foyer.
Façade, Secondary: For buildings located on corner or
through lots, the elevation facing onto any street lot line that
is not the front lot line.
Fence: A constructed barrier of any material or combination
of materials erected for the purpose of enclosing or
separating all or a portion of a lot, and may also provide
screening. That portion of a wall which is above grade on
only one side shall not constitute a fence. See Section 8.2,
Fences and Walls .
Fenestration: The openings in a structure, including
windows and doors, but not including loading berths and
entries for parking. Fenestration includes frames, mullions,
muntins, vents, and other elements integral to a window or
door unit.
Flag: Any fabric or other flexible material attached to or
designed to be flown from a flagpole or similar device. See
Section 5.6 . 5.F. Flag Pole , for flagpoles, and Section 9.2.4
Flags for flags as signs.

Floodplain: See Section 6.4.4.R. Definitions.

a legally accessible and accepted public street, as classified
by RSA 229:5. Corner lots and through lots have two
frontages: a principal frontage and a secondary frontage.
[IMAGE]
G
Garage: An enclosed, detached building, or an enclosed
extension of a principal building, used for the storage of one
or more motor vehicles on a lot.
Grade: The lowest point of elevation of the existing surface
of the ground within the area between a building and a line
six feet from the building.
Grade Plane: A reference plane representing the average
of finished ground level adjoining the building at exterior
walls. Where the finished ground level slopes away from the
exterior walls, the reference plane shall be established by
the lowest points within the area between the building and
the lot line or, where the lot line is more than six feet from
the building, between the building and a point six feet from
the building.
Grading: Any excavating, grubbing, filling, including
hydraulic fill, or stockpiling of earth materials or any
combination thereof, including land in its excavated or filled
condition.
Greenhouse: A freestanding structure, usually enclosed in
glass, in which the temperature and humidity is maintained
within a desired range, used for cultivating tender plants or
growing plants out of season. See Section 5.6 , Accessory
Structures .
Gross Floor Area: The sum of the areas of the several
floors of a building, including horizontal areas used for
human occupancy in basements, attics, and penthouses,
DEFINED TERMS
as measured from the exterior faces of the walls. It does
not include unenclosed porches, attics not used for human
occupancy, or any such floor space intended and designed
for accessory heating and ventilation equipment. For
non-residential facilities, it also does not include arcades,
porticoes, and similar open areas that are accessible to the
general public, and that are not designed or used as sales,
display, storage, service, or production areas.
Groundwater: Subsurface water that occurs beneath the
water table in soils and geologic formations.
Groundwater Management Zone (GMZ): Designated by
the State through the permit process as a component of the
remediation of contaminated groundwater. The State shall
issue permits or other similar controls for such zones that
establish a time period and process for the remediation of
the groundwater.
H
High Tunnel or Hoop House: A large, detached, internally-
framed structure of polyethylene, plastic, or fabric used to
cover plants to extend the growing season. See Section 5.6 ,
Accessory Structures .
Historic Structure: Any structure that: (1) is listed
individually in the National Register of Historic Places, such
listing as maintained by the U.S. Department of Interior;
(2) has a preliminary determination by the Secretary of the
Interior as meeting the requirements for individual listing in
the National Register; (3) is a contributing structure within a
local Historic District; or (4) is a local historic landmark as
designated by the Heritage Commission.
Horizontal Articulation: The horizontal design elements of
a building that establish character and visual interest, such
as windows, cornices, belt lines, and string courses.
I
Impervious Surface: The surface within a lot that does not
absorb rain, which includes all buildings, streets, sidewalks,
parking areas, and any area paved with bricks, concrete, or
asphalt.
Internal Drive: A curbed pedestrian and vehicular access
way that may include parallel parking, landscaped area,
and public lighting within a lot that connects to a street, and
provides access and circulation to or through such lot and
the building(s) and parking accommodations thereon.

of Ordinances.

street lot lines, or in case of a curved street the extended lot

a narrow corridor or panhandle.

ARTICLE 2: DEFINITIONS
Lot Line: A line of record constituting a boundary that
separates one lot from another or from a public or private
street or any other public space.
Lot Line, Front: The lot line separating a lot from the public
street right-of-way on which it has frontage. Where a lot
has only one lot line on a public street, or where a street
line faces the primary façade of a building, that line shall be
considered the front lot line. In the case of an unimproved
corner lot or through lot, the front lot line may be defined by
the owner, so long as the designated front lot line has the
minimum frontage for that district and the primary façade of
the building faces thereon.
Lot Line, Interior: Any side or rear lot line that only lies
adjacent to another lot line and not a street or alley.
Lot Line, Rear: The lot line opposite the front lot line.
Lot Line, Side: Any lot line other than the front or rear lot
line.
Lot Line, Street: A property line boundary between a lot
and an adjoining street.
Lot of Record: A lot described by deed, survey, or
subdivision plan and so recorded with the Hillsborough
County Registry of Deeds.
Lot Width: The horizontal distance between the side lot
lines. The required minimum lot width shall be measured at
the principal frontage line and shall extend into the lot for a
minimum depth of 100 feet. See Section 5.4.3.A. Minimum/
Maximum Lot Width for additional information.
M
Manufactured Housing or Manufactured Home: Any
structure, transportable in one or more sections that, in the
traveling mode, is eight body feet or more in width and 40
body feet or more in length, or, when erected on site, is 320
square feet or more, and that is built on a permanent chassis
and is designed to be used as a dwelling with or without
a permanent foundation when connected to the required
utilities, which include plumbing, heating, and electrical
heating systems contained therein. “Manufactured housing”
as defined in this Section shall not include pre-site-built
housing. For floodplain-management purposes, the terms
“manufactured housing” and “manufactured home” include
park trailers, travel trailers, and similar vehicles placed on a
site for greater than 180 days.
DEFINED TERMS
Manufactured Housing Park: The subdivision of a tract of
land into sites, lots, or other leaseholds that provide for the
longterm placement of manufactured housing, supported
by private, centrally managed improvements, services, and
facilities for the residents therein.
Manufactured Housing Subdivision: A subdivision of land
to create individually owned lots reserved exclusively for
manufactured homes.
Mixed-Use: A building, lot, or zoning district containing both
residential and non-residential uses.
Motor Vehicle: As defined by RSA 259:60, namely, any self-
propelled vehicle not operated exclusively upon stationary
tracks, including ski area vehicles.
Museum: A use characterized by the display, preservation,
collection, curation, or exhibition of objects of community
and cultural interest in one or more of the arts and sciences.
See Section 4.4.4.F. Cultural Facility
N
Nursing Home: A facility which provides basic domiciliary
services (room, board, and laundry) for two or more persons
and 24-hour nursing care with medical supervision provided
by licensed medical and nursing practitioners. See Section
4.4.1.G. Residential Care Facility .
O
Owner: Any person, group of persons, firm or firms,
corporation or corporations, or other legal entity having title
to, or sufficient proprietary interest in, land sought to be
subdivided or developed.
P
Parapet: A low wall or protective barrier that extends
vertically above the roof surface of a building or other
structure.
Parking, Accessory: An improved area that is designed for
the parking of motor vehicles and that serves, and is located
on the same lot as, a principal use. Accessory parking may
serve any principal use. See Section 4.5 , Accessory Uses .
Parking, Principal: An improved area that is designed
for the parking of motor vehicles and either exclusively
occupies a lot or reserves parking spaces on the lot of
another principal use for a fee. See Section 4.4, Principal
Use Definitions and Use-Specific Conditions .

DEFINED TERMS
Parking, Tandem: A parking arrangement in which one
parking space is blocked by another from egress. The
tandem parking space is the one that is blocked.
[IMAGE]
Party Wall: A wall shared between two residential or non-
residential units, extending from the foundation to the roof
of a building.
Planned Development: Any development involving the
construction or creation of two or more principal buildings
on a single lot.
Planning Board: The Planning Board of the City of
Manchester, New Hampshire.
Plot Plan: A plan of a lot, building, and other improvements
on such lot, prepared and submitted pursuant to this
Ordinance with a building permit application, which
evidences compliance of such lot, building, and other
improvements with this Ordinance.
Principal Building: The building on a lot in which the
principal use is conducted.
[IMAGE]
Principal Entrance (Main Entrance): The main point of
access into a building.
Principal Frontage: On corner lots and through lots bearing
two frontages, the frontage designated to bear the address
and principal entrance to the building, and the measure of
minimum lot width. See “Frontage”.
Principal Use: The main, predominant, or primary purpose
or purposes for which a structure, building, or lot is designed,
arranged, or intended, or for which they may be used,
occupied, or maintained, and as listed within Table 4.3-A ,
Principal Uses .
ARTICLE 2: DEFINITIONS
R
Recreational Vehicle: A vehicle which is (1) built on a single
chassis; (2) designed to be self-propelled or permanently
towable by a truck; and (3) designed primarily not for use as
2
a permanent dwelling, but as temporary living quarters for
E
recreational, camping, or travel purposes.
L
C
Religious Institution (Place of Worship): A facility used
I
by a non-profit group or institution for organized r eligious T
R
services, meetings, assembly, practice, activities, and
A
supporting uses. See Assembly, Neighborhood and
Assembly, General in Section 4.3 , Principal Uses .
Repair: The reconstruction or renewal of any part of an
existing building for the purpose of its maintenance or to
correct damage.
Residential: Premises available for long-term, non-transient
human habitation.
Retail: Uses characterized by selling, renting, or leasing new
or used goods in person, on-line, or by mail-in transactions
dealing directly with the consumer of such goods.
Right-of-Way: A legal right of public travel over a strip of
land accepted or acquired by a government entity. A right-of-
way may be occupied by a street, alley, sidewalk, trail, water
line, sanitary sewer, and/or other public utilities or facilities.
Rooming Unit: A room rented for occupancy without in-
unit facilities for sanitation or cooking within a Congregate
Housing Facility, Residential Care Facility, or a Rooming
House, as defined in Section 4.4, Principal Use Definitions
and Use-Specific Conditions.
S
Screen/Screening: The method by which a view is shielded,
concealed, or hidden by techniques such as vegetative
buffers, hedges, berms, walls, fences, or other landscaping
treatments.
Secondary Frontage: On corner lots or through lots, the
frontage that is not the principal frontage.
Setback: The minimum linear distance between a structure
or use and the nearest lot line that is required by this
Ordinance. (See also definitions relating to “Yard”).
Sexually Oriented Business: Any place of business
at which any of the following activities is conducted. See
Section 4.4.6.T. Sexually Oriented Business for use-specific
conditions.

ARTICLE 2: DEFINITIONS
(1) Adult Bookstore or Adult Video Store: A business
that devotes more than 15 percent of the total display, shelf,
rack, table, stand or floor area, utilized for the display and
sale of the following: 1. Books, magazines, periodicals, or
other printed matter, or photographs, films, motion pictures,
video cassettes, slides, tapes, records, CD-ROMs or other
forms of visual or audio representations which meet the
definition of “harmful to minors” and/or “sexual conduct” as
set forth in NH RSA 571-B:1; or 2. Instruments, devices
or paraphernalia which are designed for use in connection
with “sexual conduct” as defined by NH RSA 571-B:1, other
than birth control devices. An Adult Bookstore or Adult
Video Store does not include an establishment that sells
books or periodicals as an incidental or accessory part of
its principal stock and trade and does not devote more than
15 percent of the total floor area of the establishments to
the sale of books and periodicals.
(2) Adult Cabaret: A nightclub, bar, restaurant, or similar
establishment which during a substantial portion of the
total presentation time features live performances which
meet the definition of “harmful to minors” and/or “sexual
conduct” as set forth in NH RSA 571-B:1, and/or feature
films, motion pictures, video cassettes, slides or other
photographic reproductions, a substantial portion of the
total presentation time of which is devoted to showing of
material which meets the definition of “harmful to minors”
and/or “sexual conduct” as set forth in NH RSA 571-B:1.
(3) Adult Drive-In Theater: An open lot or part thereof, with
appurtenant facilities, devoted primarily to the presentation
of motion pictures, films, theatrical productions and other
forms of visual productions, for any form of consideration
to persons in motor vehicles or on outdoor seats, in which
a substantial portion of the total presentation time being
presented for observation by patrons is devoted to the
showing of material which meets the definition of “harmful
to minors” and/or “sexual conduct” as set forth in NH RSA
571-B:1.
(4) Adult Motel: A motel or similar establishment offering
public accommodations for any form of consideration
which provides patrons with closed circuit television
transmissions, films, motion pictures, video cassettes,
slides or other photographic reproductions, a substantial
portion of the total presentation time of which are
distinguished or characterized by an emphasis upon
the depiction or description of materials which meet the
definition of “harmful to minors” and/or “sexual conduct” as
set forth in NH RSA 571-B:1.
(5) Adult Motion Picture Arcade: Any place to which the
public is permitted or invited wherein coin or slug-operated
or electronically, electrically or mechanically controlled still
or motion picture machines, projectors, or other image-
producing devices are maintained to show images to five
DEFINED TERMS
or fewer persons per machine at any one time, in which
a substantial portion of the total presentation time of the
images so displayed is devoted to the showing of material
which meets the definition of “harmful to minors” and/or
“sexual conduct” as set forth in NH RSA 571-B:1.
(6) Adult Motion Picture Theater: An establishment with
a capacity of five or more persons, where for any form
of consideration, films, motion pictures, video cassettes,
slides or similar photographic reproductions are shown,
and in which a substantial portion of the total presentation
time is devoted to the showing of material which meets the
definition of “harmful to minors” and/or “sexual conduct” as
set forth in NH RSA 571-B:1, for observation by patrons.
For subsections C,D,E,F and G a “substantial portion of the
total presentation time” shall mean the presentation of films
or shows described above for viewing on more than seven
days within any 56 consecutive day period.
(7) Adult Theater: A theater, concert hall, auditorium or
similar establishment either indoor or outdoor in nature,
which, for any form of consideration, regularly features live
performances, a substantial portion of the total presentation
time of which are distinguished or characterized by an
emphasis on activities which meet the definition of “harmful
to minors” and/or “sexual conduct” as set forth in NH RSA
571-B:1.
(8) Nude Model Studio: A place where a person appears
in a state of nudity or displays male genitals in a state of
sexual arousal and/or the vulva or more intimate parts of
the female genitals and is observed, sketched, drawn,
painted, sculpted, photographed, or similarly depicted by
other persons who pay money or any form of consideration
and such display is characterized by an emphasis on
activities which meet the definition of “harmful to minors”
and/or “sexual conduct” as set forth in NH RSA 571-B:1.
(9) Sexual Encounter Center: A business or commercial
enterprise that as one of its primary business purposes,
offers for any form of consideration: (A) physical contact in
the form of wrestling or tumbling between persons of the
opposite and/or persons of the same sex; or (B) activities
between male and female persons and/or persons of the
same sex when one or more persons is in the state of
nudity; or where the activities in (A) or (B) is characterized
by an emphasis on activities which meet the definition of
“harmful to minors” and/or “sexual conduct” as set forth in
NH RSA 571-B:1.
Sign: Any writing (including letters, words, or numerals),
pictorial representation (including illustrations or decorations),
emblem (including devices, symbols, or trademarks), or any
other figure of similar character, used for visual communication
intended to be visible to or attract the attention of persons on
a right-of-way or on another property.

Regulations.

approved by the Zoning Board of Adjustment in accordance
with the provisions of Article 10 .
Story: That portion of a building included between the upper
surface of a floor and the upper surface of the floor or roof
next above.
Story, First: The lowermost story which is entirely above the
grade plane, except that a basement shall be considered a
story above grade where the finished surface of the floor
above the basement is: a) more than six feet above the
grade plane; b) more than 12 feet above the finished ground
level at any point.

situated under a sloping roof, the floor area of which does
not exceed two-thirds of the floor area immediately below it.

access to an abutting lot.

U
Use: A specific function, activity, or purpose accommodated
by or intended to be accommodated by land, a lot or
structure, or for which land, lot or structure is designed,

DEFINED TERMS
Wholesale: A use primarily providing the storage, transfer,
sale, or resale of goods not for direct consumption by the
buyer.
Y
Yard: The entire open space that lies between the principal
building or buildings and the lot or street lines. Refer to
Figure 2.3.Y-1, Yards . Also see definition for “Setbacks”.
Yard, Front: The area of a lot extending for the full width of
the lot between the primary façade of the building and the
front lot line.
Yard, Rear: The area of a lot extending for the full width of
the lot between the rear line of the building wall and the rear
lot line.
Yard, Side: The area of a lot extending for the full length
of a building between the building wall and the side lot line.

the street lot line.

of a building, such as columns, pilasters, and bays, that
establish character, rhythm, hierarchy, and visual interest.
Visible Basement: A story that is partially below grade
and partially exposed above with required transparency on
street facing façades.
W
Wetland Scientist: A person licensed by the State of New
Hampshire as a certified wetland scientist who is qualified to
delineate wetlands and practice wetland science.
Wetlands: As defined in RSA 482-A:2, as amended, a
wetland is an area that is inundated or saturated by surface
water or groundwater at a frequency and duration sufficient

a prevalence of vegetation typically adapted for life in
saturated soil conditions. Wetlands generally include, but
are not limited to, swamps, marshes, bogs, and similar
areas.

ARTICLE 3: ZONING MAP AND DISTRICTS
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 19
Official Zoning Maps
ARTICLE 3
City, as determined by the Manchester Conservation 
Commission. Areas surrounding the designated 
wetlands have more stringent regulations requiring 
setbacks and non-disturbance buffers. The Highest 
Priority Wetlands regulations are considered City￾wide regulations, as they apply to anywhere within 
the City limits that happens to fall within the wetland 
and wetland buffer areas. The map serves as an 
interpretation of the boundary lines of the wetlands, 
but official boundaries are subject to a determination 
by a wetlands scientist. The Highest Priority 
Wetlands Map is included as Appendix D within this 
Ordinance; and
D. Flood Map
The Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM), as published 
by the Federal Emergency Management Agency 
(FEMA), on September 25, 2009, displays the 
boundaries of and special limits within the floodplain, 
subject to the Floodplain Management Ordinance. 
The Ordinance identifies areas in which certain uses 
are either prohibited or subject to more stringent 
regulations requiring floodproofing. The Floodplain 
Management Ordinance is considered a city-wide 
regulation, as it applies to anywhere within the City 
limits that happens to fall within the floodplain.
3.2.3 District Boundaries
A. Establishment of Boundaries
The boundaries of each of the Districts identified in 
Section 3.3 are hereby established as shown on the 
duly adopted Zoning Map. Additionally, the Airport 
Navigational Hazards Overlay District is established 
as including the entire City.
B. Interpretation of District 
Boundaries
The location of district boundaries shall be as shown 
on the zoning maps or as otherwise described in 
this Ordinance. Where any uncertainty exists with 
respect to the boundary of any district as shown on 
an official zoning base district or overlay map, the 
following rules of interpretation shall be applied:
1. Where a boundary is indicated as a highway, 
street, alley, railroad, watercourse, or City boundary, 
it shall be construed to be the centerline thereof;
2. Where a boundary is indicated as approximately 
parallel to a street, alley, railroad, watercourse, 
or City boundary, it shall be construed as parallel 
thereto at such distance from the centerline thereof 
as shown on the official Zoning Map(s);
3. If no dimension is given on the official Zoning 
Map(s), the location of any boundary shall be 
determined by the use of the scale shown on the 
official Zoning Map(s);
4. Where a district boundary lies within 10 feet or 
less of a lot or the parcel line, the boundary shall be 
construed to be such line;
5. Boundaries indicated as following shore lines 
shall be construed to follow such shore lines, and 
in the event of change in the shore line shall be 
construed as moving with the actual shore line; 
boundaries indicated as approximately following 
the center lines of streams, rivers, canals, lakes, or 
other bodies of water shall be construed to follow 
such center lines;
C. Appeal to Zoning Board of 
Adjustment
In the case of uncertainty as to the true location of 
a District boundary line, an appeal of the Director’s 
determination may be taken to the Zoning Board of 
Adjustment, as provided in Article 10: Administration, 
Procedures, and Enforcement.
D. Lot or Parcel in More than One 
Jurisdiction
If any lot or other parcel of land is situated partially 
within the City and partially within one or more other 
jurisdictions, the portion of such lot or other parcel 
situated within the City shall comply with the City 
standards and requirements for the applicable City 
District.

District,” or “commercially-zoned” is used in this

such portion of any district used or available for 
commercial use.

construed to include such portion of any district used 
or available for industrial use.

Where the phrase “Conservation District” is used 
in this Ordinance, the phrase shall be construed to 
include such portion of any district used or available 
for conservation or open space uses.

allows for mixed-use development including a variety of

mixture of block sizes and buildings with active building 
frontages set at or close to the sidewalk.

vitality and residential capacity of the downtown core. 
It allows for Manchester’s downtown to continue to be 
the center of New Hampshire’s economy. Development 
may occur at maximum densities and building heights, 
including high-rise buildings. Blocks contain large-scale 
buildings with active frontages that are set up to sidewalks.

mixed-use district. This district has extra standards in 
place to ensure consistency of newer buildings with the 
area’s historic character.

24 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE
Establishment of Districts
3.3.3 Overlay Districts
Certain lands within the City are hereby included in 
the following Overlay Districts for the purposes so 
stated, as described below and as depicted on the 
Official Zoning Overlay District Maps. The Overlay 
Districts are superimposed upon the Base Districts, 
and the provisions of each of the Overlay District 
shall be in addition to the provisions of the Base 
District.
Land encumbered by requirements of a Base 
District and one or more Overlay Districts shall be 
used only if and to the extent that the proposed 
use is permitted both in the Base District and in the 
applicable Overlay District or Districts. Wherever 
the regulations differ between the Base District and 
an Overlay District, those that impose the more 
restrictive provisions or the higher standard shall 
control. 
The following Overlay Districts are hereby 
established for the public purposes stated, each 
of which shall be subject to the standards and 
regulations referenced below:
A. Airport Navigational Hazard 
Overlay
Reasonable visibility and navigational control 
is essential to public safety in the vicinity of the 
Manchester-Boston Regional Airport. The purpose of 
this Overlay District is to preclude the establishment 
of uses, structures, or other activities that would 
obstruct or impair the aerial approach to the airport 
by creating electrical impulses or disturbances which 
interfere with radio aids, communications and lights 
that may result in glare in the vision of pilots of 
aircraft or be confused with airport lights.
B. Airport Approach Overlay
The purpose of this Overlay District is to prevent the 
penetration of buildings, structures, trees or other 
intrusions into airspace reserved for use of aircraft 
landing and taking off at the Manchester-Boston 
Regional Airport. The primary function of this Overlay 
District is to provide a review and approval procedure 
which places supplemental controls on the height 
of structures or natural growth along an imaginary 
inclined surface. The Airport Approach Overlay 
District boundaries are based on the orientation of 
runways at Manchester-Boston Regional Airport. 
C. Airport Noise Overlay
The purpose of this Overlay District is to avoid 
the establishment of land uses in the vicinity of 
the Manchester-Boston Regional Airport that are 
incompatible with the noise levels generated by the 
take off and landing of aircraft, and to allow other 
uses to be established which may be compatible if 
soundproofing standards are integrated into new 
building construction. The establishment of the 
Overlay District is also intended to reduce future 
public costs to acquire property or otherwise mitigate 
the noise impacts of planned airport expansion. The 
primary intent of this Overlay District is to identify and 
preclude the establishment of incompatible uses, 
and to require soundproofing for compatible new 
development that may be affected by airport noise. 
D. Amoskeag Corporation 
Housing (ACH) Historic District 
Overlay
The Amoskeag Corporation Housing Historic 
Overlay District protects an area of unique character 
and architecture which contributes significantly to the 
attractiveness and vitality of downtown Manchester.
The creation of this Overlay District recognizes 
that the character and nature of the area depends 
on the unity of design of a complex of buildings 
that represents a value greater than the sum of 
the individual contributions of each structure. The 
character and value of the area within the overlay 
is recognized as a fundamental component of the 
City’s early development. The continuity of rich 
architectural expression, quality and integrity in 
closely related styles, materials, scale and detail 
of individual buildings is an integral component of 
long range development goals for the downtown. 
The opportunities that the area offers include, 
retention of the architectural and historic values and 
characteristics in this complex, and the presence 
of valuable resources for present and future 
housing and office needs. Through coordinated 
landscaping, development of pedestrian ways, and 
improvements to private and public open spaces 
adjoining the buildings, a rich, attractive and vital 
urban environment can be created and preserved for 
future generations. This Overlay District is intended 
to regulate the exterior appearance of existing and 
proposed structures, and to restrict those activities 
that could alter the use and appearance of the 
exterior spaces adjoining these buildings, while 
encouraging the rehabilitation and improvement of 
this area.

Millyard is preserved. Preventing the irretrievable loss 
of historic or architecturally significant buildings and 
their unique character is important to the economic 
well-being of the City, which will be strengthened by:
1. Preserving the Millyard’s architectural and historic 
setting;
2. Conserving the property values in the district;
3. Promoting Manchester’s unique character;
4. Strengthening the local economy; and 
5. Promoting the use of the historic district for the 
education, pleasure, and welfare of the citizens of 
Manchester and visitors to the City.
F. Gaslight Historic District (GHD) 
Overlay
The purpose of this Overlay District is to develop an 
area that is compatible with and complementary to the 
city center, and to protect an area of unique character 
and history which can contribute significantly to the 
attractiveness and vitality of downtown Manchester. 
The character and value of the area within the Overlay 
District is recognized as a fundamental component 
of the City’s early development in local commerce. 
The creation of this Overlay District recognizes that 
the character and nature of the area depends on the 
preservation of the remaining core buildings, and 
reinforcing the independent identity within the City. 
The continuity of architecture, quality and integrity in 
closely related styles, materials, scale and detail of 
individual buildings is an integral component of long 
range development goals for the downtown. This 
Overlay District is intended to regulate the exterior 
appearance of existing and proposed structures, 
and to restrict those activities that could alter the 
use and appearance of the exterior spaces adjoining 
these buildings, while encouraging the rehabilitation 
and improvement of this area.
G. Lake Massabesic Protection 
Overlay District (LMPOD).
The purpose of this Overlay District is to protect the 
Lake Massabesic drinking water supply to the City.
H. Manchester Landfill 
Groundwater Management Zone 
(ML-GMZ) Overlay
The purpose of this Overlay District is to protect 
public health by restricting groundwater use. 
The groundwater quality is being monitored under 
a permit issued by the New Hampshire Department 
of Environmental Services (NHDES). Pumping of 
groundwater from any well, trench or other structure 
for residential, irrigation, agricultural or industrial 
purpose is prohibited, unless it is for the specific 
purpose of pumping groundwater out of a sump 
to keep a cellar from flooding. The extent of the 
district shall be referenced by NHDES Permit as 
the Manchester Landfill Groundwater Management 
Zone.

ARTICLE 4: USES
Section 4.1
INTRODUCTORY
PROVISIONS
4.1.1 Applicability
All uses of structures and buildings shall comply
with the requirements of this Article, except for non-
conforming uses or structures that were legally
established prior to the adoption of this Ordinance,
pursuant to Article 12: Non-Conforming Lots, Uses,
and Structures .
4.1.2 General Provisions
The following general provisions apply to the uses
outlined in this section.
A. Principal Uses
Multiple principal uses may be established on a
single lot to the extent that such uses are authorized
within the Table of Principal Uses for the district in
which the lot is located. Such uses shall be contained
within the same structure, except for planned
developments as further specified in Section 4.1.5
Multiple Structures on a Single Lot .
B. Permitted Building Types
Each use shall be located within a permitted building
type (refer to Article 5: Building and Lot Standards ),
unless otherwise specified.
C. Location
Each use shall be located indoors (within a building),
unless otherwise expressly stated.
D. Measure of Distance
Some uses will have limitations imposed that specify
minimum distances from other types of residential or
civic uses or other zoning districts. The distancing
requirements shall always be measured in a straight
line, without regard to intervening structures, from
the closest point on the property line of any site listed
for which the distancing limitations are imposed to
the nearest property line or zoning district line.
INTRODUCTORY PROVISIONS
4.1.3 Administrative
Classification of Uses Not
Specified or Change in Use
A. Interpretation
In the event that a proposed use is not identified
within Table 4.3-A , Principal Uses , Table 4.5-A ,
Accessory Uses , or Section 4.7 Temporary Uses , or
where a change in a use permitted by right to another
use is proposed, the Director is authorized to render
a decision on the administrative classification of said
use.
B. Criteria for Decision
In reaching a decision on the classification of a
use, the Director may consider such factors as the
similarity of the proposed use to others included
in the principal, accessory, and temporary uses as
contained in this Article; and substantive changes
in the function, utility, or the intensity of the use
with respect to parking, loading, customer traffic, or
other impacts. The Director may also consider the
similarity of the proposed use to the hierarchy of non-
residential uses as identified in the “North American
Industry Classification System”, and the relationship
of the classification to the uses contained in this
Article.
C. Administrative Decision on
Classification
On the basis of these considerations, the Director
shall render a decision which indicates an
administrative classification of the proposed use or
change in use, and a determination that:
1. The use is permitted by right; or
2. The use requires a Special Exception, Conditional
Use permit, or other approval; or
3. The use is not permitted under the Ordinance.
D. Appeal of Decision on
Classification
Appeals of any decision by the Director shall require
an appeal of an administrative decision to the
Zoning Board of Adjustment, in accordance with the
procedures set forth in Article 10: Administration,
Procedures, and Enforcement .

INTRODUCTORY PROVISIONS
E. Non-Conforming Change of Use
A change in use from a non-conforming use to
another use not permitted shall require a Special
Exception from the Board of Adjustment, subject to
the review criteria established in Article 12: Non-
Conforming Lots, Uses, and Structures .
4.1.4 Overlay District Provisions
In addition to the use regulations which pertain to
the base districts designated within Table 4.3-A and
Table 4.5-A , certain regulations and procedures for
base districts and overlay districts are set forth in
Article 6: Special District-Wide Regulations . Uses
which are authorized within Table 4.3-A and Table
4.5-A may be further restricted or prohibited if they
are also located within one or more overlay districts.
Wherever there is a conflict between the provisions
of an overlay district and a base district, the provision
which imposes the greater restriction or the higher
standard shall control.
4.1.5 Multiple Structures on a
Single Lot
No more than one principal structure shall occupy
a single lot of record, unless the development is
approved by the Planning Board as and meets the
provisions of Section 8.7, Planned Developments.
All planned developments are subject to Planning
Board review. Planned developments shall comply
with all other requirements of this Ordinance,
including the standards of the chosen building types
within the planned development. Buildings shall be
considered separate and unattached if connected
by ancillary features such as, but not limited to,
fences, breezeways, carports, enclosed corridors,
porches, porch roofs, or similar minor connections.

District Provisions for Lodging,

Uses
Any uses as defined in 4.4.2.A. Bed and Breakfast
or 4.4.5.C. Professional Office, or listed within 4.4.6
Retail and Service Uses have additional standards
within the Mixed-Use (MX) Zoning Districts. See
6.2.2 Mixed-Use (MX) Districts for more information.

CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 29
Introductory provisions
ARTICLE 4
E. Non-Conforming Change of Use
A change in use from a non-conforming use to 
another use not permitted shall require a Special 
Exception from the Board of Adjustment, subject to 
the review criteria established in Article 12: Non￾Conforming Lots, Uses, and Structures.
4.1.4 Overlay District Provisions
In addition to the use regulations which pertain to 
the base districts designated within Table 4.3-A and 
Table 4.5-A, certain regulations and procedures for 
base districts and overlay districts are set forth in 
Article 6: Special District-Wide Regulations. Uses 
which are authorized within Table 4.3-A and Table 
4.5-A may be further restricted or prohibited if they 
are also located within one or more overlay districts. 
Wherever there is a conflict between the provisions 
of an overlay district and a base district, the provision 
which imposes the greater restriction or the higher 
standard shall control.
4.1.5 Multiple Structures on a
Single Lot
No more than one principal structure shall occupy 
a single lot of record, unless the development is 
approved by the Planning Board as and meets the 
provisions of Section 8.7, Planned Developments. 
All planned developments are subject to Planning 
Board review. Planned developments shall comply 
with all other requirements of this Ordinance, 
including the standards of the chosen building types 
within the planned development. Buildings shall be 
considered separate and unattached if connected 
by ancillary features such as, but not limited to, 
fences, breezeways, carports, enclosed corridors, 
porches, porch roofs, or similar minor connections. 
4.1.6 Additional Mixed-Use (MX)
District Provisions for Lodging,
Office, and Retail and Service
Uses
Any uses as defined in 4.4.2.A. Bed and Breakfast 
or 4.4.5.C. Professional Office, or listed within 4.4.6 
Retail and Service Uses have additional standards 
within the Mixed-Use (MX) Zoning Districts. See 
6.2.2 Mixed-Use (MX) Districts for more information.
4.1.7 Performance Standards for
Noxious or Hazardous Uses
Substantial and noxious amounts of cinders, dust, 
flashing, fumes, gases, odors, refuse matter, smoke, 
vapor, electromagnetic transmission, or radio￾active emission, shall be completely and effectively 
confined within the building, or so regulated as to 
prevent any nuisance or hazard to the public’s health 
or safety. No noise, vibration, or other disturbance 
that is perceptible without the use of instruments at 
the boundary of the zoning district in which the use 
is located shall be permitted. 
A. High Hazard Uses
No high hazard use (as defined by the Building Code) 
shall be permitted within the City, except where the 
land use board(s) having jurisdiction to review the 
proposed development containing such use under 
this Ordinance shall determine in each instance that 
all of the following are true:
1. Lot coverage. The impervious coverage of the 
lot shall not exceed 50 percent.
2. Separation from Residential Districts. The use 
shall not be located within 300 feet of any residential 
district boundary.
3. Site and Access Characteristics. The proposed 
location shall be such as to offer a reasonable 
protection to the immediate area against possible 
detrimental effects of such use, taking into 
consideration the physical relationship to surrounding 
properties and access to the site including any nearby 
residential streets that must be traversed in bringing 
material to the site.
4. Technical and Scientific Advance. It shall be 
convincingly demonstrated to the land use board(s) 
of jurisdiction, by competent technical or scientific 
experts, that such high hazard use can and shall 
make such use of advanced technical equipment 
and processes as shall no longer justify prohibition of 
such use based on hazard.
5. Not in Conflict with Other Laws. The use or 
operation shall not be in conflict with any other law 
or ordinance of any governmental agency having 
pertinent jurisdiction, nor in conflict with other 
provisions of this Ordinance.

ARTICLE 4: USES
Section 4.2
ORGANIZATION OF USE
TABLES
4.2.1 Uses Permitted by Right
Principal Uses, or Accessory Uses, as applicable,
of buildings and lots, which are indicated for each
district in Table 4.3-A, and Table 4.5-A as Permitted
(“P”) are allowed by right, subject to compliance
with all other applicable provisions of this Ordinance
and other local, state, and federal laws, rules and
regulations. Permission of a use by right does not
exempt the use from any use-specific conditions as
noted in Section 4.4, Section 4.6, and Section 4.7 of
this Article.
4.2.2 Uses Permitted by Special
Exception or by Conditional Use
Any Principal Use or Accessory Use, shown for the
applicable Zoning District as Permitted by Conditional
Use Permit (“CU”) or Permitted by Special Exception
(“SE”) in Table 4.3-A, and Table 4.5-A is a use that
may be authorized by a Conditional Use Permit
or Special Exception in that district, subject to all
other conditions of approval for such as specified
in this Ordinance. The Planning Board may grant
a Conditional Use permit in accordance with the
procedures and conditions set forth in Article 10
of this Ordinance, subject to all other applicable
sections of this Ordinance and other local, state,
and federal laws, rules, and regulations. The Zoning
Board of Adjustment may grant Special Exceptions
in accordance with the procedures and conditions
set forth in Article 10 of this Ordinance, subject to all
other applicable sections of this Ordinance and other
local, state, and federal laws, rules and regulations.
The conditions and requirements applicable to any
use permitted by Conditional Use Permit or Special
Exception shall be enforceable, and failure to comply
with any condition or requirement shall subject such
use permission to revocation pursuant to Article 10 .
4.2.3 Uses Not Permitted
Any use that is not specifically listed as Permitted
by Right (“P”), Permitted by Conditional Use Permit
(“CU”), or Permitted by Special Exception (“SE”) in
Table 4.3-A and Table 4.5-A , and any use that is
marked with a dash (“-”) in such applicable table or is
otherwise prohibited pursuant to any other provision
of the Ordinance, is not permitted in that district.
ORGANIZATION OF USE TABLES
Section 4.3
PRINCIPAL USES
4.3.1 Table of Principal Uses
Table 4.3-A, Principal Uses identifies the principal
uses allowed in each zoning district. Principal uses
are defined in Section 4.4, Principal Use Definitions
and Use-Specific Conditions , and each defined use
is given one of the following designations: permitted
by right in a district (“P”), permitted by Conditional
Use Permit (“CU”), permitted by Special Exception
(“SE”), or not permitted (“ - “).
4.3.2 Use Categories
Uses are grouped into general categories, which
are sometimes further broken into subcategories
and specific use types. For example, the Retail
and Service Uses category includes a subcategory
of uses for Neighborhood Retail and Service and
specific uses such as Florist. All subcategories,
when applicable, will appear in list form in the
Principal Use List Table 4.3-B , directly following the
Table of Principal Uses ( Table 4.3-A ).

ARTICLE 4: USES
Section 4.4
PRINCIPAL USE
DEFINITIONS AND USE-
SPECIFIC CONDITIONS
4.4.1 Residential Uses
A category of uses for residential accommodation.
A. Dwelling, Single-Family
One principal dwelling unit contained within one
structure on a lot that does not contain any other
principal dwelling units and consists exclusively
of one family. The structure or lot may contain
one Accessory Dwelling Unit, pursuant to Section
4.6.1.A. Accessory Dwelling Unit.
B. Dwelling, Two-Family
Two principal dwelling units located within one
detached building or horizontally attached to each
other, on one lot, with no other principal dwelling
units located on such lot. The occupancy consists
of two families living independently of one another.
C. Dwelling, Multifamily
Three or more principal dwelling units, all of which are
located on the same lot, within a building categorized
as a Residential Building pursuant to 5.1.4 , whether in
common ownership or owned as a condominium or
cooperative. The number of units permitted may be
limited by building type.
1. Residential Density Maximums in MX Districts.
No residential building type within MX-1 shall contain
more than four dwelling units. No building type within
MX-2 shall contain more than nine dwelling units.
2. Conditional Use Permit Required in ID. Within
the Innovation District, residential buildings are only
permitted through a Conditional Use permit to be
used in a mixed-use planned development.
D. Dwelling, Mixed-Use
One or more principal dwelling unit located within a
building categorized as a Mixed-Use Building pursuant
to 5.1.4 , whether in common ownership or owned as
a condominium or cooperative. The number of units
permitted may be limited by building type.
1. Residential Density Maximums in MX Districts.
No mixed-use building type within MX-1 shall contain
more than two dwelling units. No building type within
MX-2 shall contain more than nine dwelling units.
PRINCIPAL USE DEFINITIONS AND USE-SPECIFIC CONDITIONS
2. Conditional Use Permit Required in MX-1.
Within MX-1, mixed-use dwellings may only be used
in a Cottage Commercial building type, as outlined
in Section 5.3, Building Types, which requires a
Conditional Use permit from the Planning Board.
E. Manufactured Housing Park or
Subdivision
The subdivision of a tract of land into sites, lots or
other leaseholds which provide for the long-term
placement of manufactured housing, supported by
private, centrally managed improvements, services
and facilities for the residents therein. Manufactured
Housing Parks or Subdivisions do not have to adhere
to the Building Types Standards as further detailed
in Section 5.3 . However, Section 8.8 further details
the minimum standards for the development of a
Manufactured Housing Park or Subdivision.
F. Congregate Housing Facility
A building containing one or more dwelling or
rooming units serving individuals who require on-site
services that support independent living, including,
at a minimum, communal dining facilities and 24-
hour staff supervision. Congregate housing may be
characterized by on-site supportive care services,
housekeeping and linen service, and the supervision
of self-administered medication, but excludes 24-hour
nursing care.
1. Building Type Standards. The use of a Congregate
Housing Facility shall follow all requirements of either
an Apartment House or Small Multifamily building
type, as outlined in Section 5.3, Building Types. For
the purpose of calculating density requirements, two
bedrooms are equivalent to one dwelling unit.
G. Residential Care Facility
A licensed care facility that provides 24-hour medical
or non-medical care to persons in need of personal
services, supervision, protection, or assistance
essential for sustaining the activities of daily living.
Includes such uses as nursing homes, rehabilitation
and convalescent centers, independent living, assisted
living, continuum of care, and hospice facilities. Does
not include a Rooming House or Congregate Housing
Facility.
1. Building Type Standards. A Residential Care
Facility shall adhere to the standards of the building
types allowed in the zoning district in which it is located,
as allowed in Section 5.3 , excluding any residential
density requirements.

PRINCIPAL USE DEFINITIONS AND USE-SPECIFIC CONDITIONS
H. Rooming House
Also Boarding Hous e . A house, building, or portion
thereof containing one or more rooms that lack in-unit
cooking and sanitation facilities, that do not constitute
dwelling units, and that are provided as living quarters
for tenants. Rooming Houses also include sorority and
fraternity houses.
1. Building Type Standards. The use of a Rooming
House shall follow all requirements of either an
Apartment House or Small Multifamily building type, as
outlined in Section 5.3, Building Types. For the purpose
of calculating residential density requirements, two
bedrooms are equivalent to one dwelling unit.
4.4.2 Lodging Uses
A category of uses for lodging accommodation.
A. Bed and Breakfast
A dwelling house, or portion thereof, where short-term
guest lodging and meals are provided. The owner of
the Bed and Breakfast shall be the operator of the Bed
and Breakfast and shall live on the premises. Includes
related ancillary facilities, such as dining and meeting
rooms.
1. Lot and Building Type Standards. The use shall be
subject to the standards as set forth in Section 5.3.1.H.
Cottage Commercial Building Type Standards . In
place of the two-dwelling-unit maximum of the Cottage
Commercial building type, occupancy shall be limited
to no more than six sleeping rooms. The use shall not
alter the residential nature of the neighborhood and/
or the character of the dwelling as a residence.
2. Guest Room Access. Access to guestrooms shall
be via a main entrance, lobby, or foyer within the
building. No guestroom shall have a separate exterior
access, except as may be required by fire or building
codes.
3. Duration of Stay. Guest stays are limited to a
maximum of 30 consecutive days.
4. Conditional Use Permit Required in Mixed-
Use Zoning Districts (MX-1 and MX-2). In addition
to the limitations of this use as listed in this Section,
the Planning Board may further limit this use as part
of the approval process for a Conditional Use permit,
however this use is exempt from the non-residential
floor area limitations. See 6.2.2 Mixed-Use (MX)
Districts for more information.
ARTICLE 4: USES
B. Hotel
Also Motel or Extended Stay Facility. A facility offering
temporary lodging in one or more buildings to the
general public for compensation, consisting of six or
more sleeping rooms with a private bathroom for each
room and providing daily room cleaning services and
other guest services. In-room kitchen facilities may
or may not be provided. Includes related ancillary
facilities, such as dining facilities, meeting rooms,
recreation areas including pools and gyms, and other
incidental services.
1. Lot and Building Type Standards. A Hotel
4
use shall be subject to either the Large Multifamily,
E
General Mixed-Use, Mid-Rise, or High-Rise building L
type standards, as allowed in Section 5.3 , excluding C
any residential density requirements. This limitation I
T
on building types also applies to Hotels in the IND for R
any regulation pursuant to entrance types and street A
façade elements, however the building siting and height
standards for any building in the IND shall adhere to
the special district-wide regulations pursuant to Section
6.2.7 Industrial (IND) District.
4.4.3 Agricultural Uses
A category of uses generally applicable to the use of
land which may not require buildings or other facilities
used for active or passive, public or private outdoor
recreation, education, or entertainment. Pursuant to
NH RSA 674:32-c, the tilling of soil and growing and
harvesting of crops shall be allowed in any district. The

thereof containing one or more rooms that lack in-unit 
cooking and sanitation facilities, that do not constitute 
dwelling units, and that are provided as living quarters 
for tenants. Rooming Houses also include sorority and 
fraternity houses.
1. Building Type Standards. The use of a Rooming 
House shall follow all requirements of either an 
Apartment House or Small Multifamily building type, as 
outlined in Section 5.3, Building Types. For the purpose 
of calculating residential density requirements, two 
bedrooms are equivalent to one dwelling unit.
4.4.2 Lodging Uses
A category of uses for lodging accommodation.
A. Bed and Breakfast
A dwelling house, or portion thereof, where short-term 
guest lodging and meals are provided. The owner of 
the Bed and Breakfast shall be the operator of the Bed 
and Breakfast and shall live on the premises. Includes 
related ancillary facilities, such as dining and meeting 
rooms.
1. Lot and Building Type Standards. The use shall be 
subject to the standards as set forth in Section 5.3.1.H.

alter the residential nature of the neighborhood and/

be via a main entrance, lobby, or foyer within the 
building. No guestroom shall have a separate exterior 
access, except as may be required by fire or building 
codes.

maximum of 30 consecutive days.

ARTICLE 4: USES
1. Lot Standards. A minimum of one acre shall be
required to maintain one animal defined as livestock,
unless the only use on the lot is for an accessory use of
Domestic Keeping of Chickens (see 4.6.1.C. Domestic
Keeping of Chickens ). For each additional animal
defined as livestock, an additional one-quarter acre
shall be required.
B. Community Garden
A place where plants, including trees, are grown for
personal, group, shareholder, or lessee use, or for
donation, including for educational, recreational, and
beautification purposes. Community gardens may
be divided into separate plots for cultivation by one
or more individuals or may be farmed collectively
by members of the group and may include common
areas maintained or used by community group
members. The minimum lot size for the principal use
of a community garden shall be one half acre (21,780
square feet).
C. Forestry and Plant Agriculture
A commercial agricultural operation that grows
horticultural or nursery stock or fruits, vegetables,
grain, or other agricultural crops outdoors or within
hightunnels or greenhouses. May include growth and
harvesting of forest products, tree nursery, tree farm,
orchards, maple syrup production, and similar uses,
provided that only products grown on the premises are
sold.
D. Indoor Plant Agriculture
A commercial operation that grows fruits, vegetables,
grain, or other agricultural crops; horticultural or
nursery stock; or aquaculture in a permanent indoor
facility. Includes greenhouses. Includes retail sales of
products grown on the premises.
1. Use Limitation. The growth of medicinal marijuana
shall only be permitted within the IND.
E. Stables and Riding Centers
A structure(s) or land used, designed, and arranged
for the care and shelter of equines, or for rentals,
riding, shows, or training, which may include horses
not boarded on-site.
PRINCIPAL USE DEFINITIONS AND USE-SPECIFIC CONDITIONS
4.4.4 Civic and Institutional Uses
A category of uses related to fulfilling the needs of
day-to-day community life including assembly, public
services, educational facilities, and hospitals. All uses
listed in this category may utilize a Civic building type,
as defined in Section 5.3.1.P. Civic Building .
A. Assembly, Neighborhood
A smaller-scale facility that has organized services,
meetings, events, or programs to benefit, educate,
entertain, or promote discourse in a public or private
setting indoors. Includes such uses as places of
worship or religious institutions, community centers,
meeting or lecture halls, exhibition rooms, or
auditoriums. If an assembly use is ancillary to another
principal use and does not exceed a gross floor area
of 5,000 square feet, it is considered part of that
use and is not considered a separate principal use.
Includes related ancillary uses like daycare centers
and schools or other instructional facilities.
1. Maximum Floor Area. Neighborhood assembly
uses shall not exceed 20,000 square feet of gross floor
area.
B. Assembly, General
A large-scale facility that has organized services,
meetings, events, or programs to benefit, educate,
entertain, or promote discourse in a public or private
setting, indoors or outdoors. Includes such uses as
arenas, amphitheaters, and stadiums, as well as uses
classified as Assembly, Neighborhood that exceed
20,000 square feet of gross floor area. Includes related
ancillary uses like concession stands.
C. Cemeteries
Land or structures dedicated for the interment of
human or animal remains.
D. College/University
A post-secondary institution, public or private, for
higher learning that grants associate, bachelors,
masters, or doctoral degrees. Includes theological
schools and vocational or technical schools. Includes
related ancillary facilities, such as cafeterias,
restaurants, retail, indoor or outdoor recreational
facilities, research facilities, and dormitories.

PRINCIPAL USE DEFINITIONS AND USE-SPECIFIC CONDITIONS
E. Correctional Institution
A government facility designed and operated for the
purpose of providing housing, care, training, and
supervision for incarcerated persons. This category of
use shall include, but is not limited to, prisons, jails,
reformatories, and detention centers.
1. Purpose and Intent. It is the intent of this section
to establish reasonable and uniform regulations to
prevent the concentration of correctional institutions
within the City of Manchester, in order to maintain and
promote the health, safety and general welfare of the
citizens of the City of Manchester.
2. Minimum Lot Size Requirements. The minimum
lot size for the establishment of a correctional institution
shall be five acres.
3. Minimum Setback Requirements. All correctional
facility structures shall be setback from all property
lines a minimum of 50 feet.
4. Location Restriction. No correctional institution
shall be located within 1,500 feet of any:
a. Residential (R) or Mixed-Use (MX) zoning district
boundary line;
b. Uses as defined as: Assembly Neighborhood;
Assembly, General; School, Elementary/Secondary;
Day Care Center, Child; and
c. City Hall, City Library, Public Park.
5. Performance Standards. The design, construction
and operations of a correctional institution shall be
supported by expert study. The implementation and
conclusions of those studies shall be subject to the
review of the Planning Board in its consideration of a
Conditional Use Permit request or Site Plan approval.
Conditions of approval shall include criteria such as,
but not limited to, fencing or other barriers, cameras,
lighting, guards, use of guard dogs, sirens and direct
alarms connected with the Police Department, and all
other operational protocols that may be appropriate
to the use. The applicant shall develop an emergency
management plan to be implemented in the event of a
catastrophic event resulting from flooding, fire, wind,
snow, ice, earthquake, utility outage, or other similar
events. Said plan shall be reviewed and approved
by the Police and Fire Departments. It shall also
be compatible with, and made part of, the City of
Manchester Emergency Operations Plan.

A facility open to the public for cultural services and
exhibitions including, but not limited to, museums,
cultural centers, historical societies, and libraries. A
cultural facility may include ancillary assembly, retail,
or restaurant uses.
G. Day Care Center, Adult
A non-residential facility in which custodial care is
provided for up to 12 adults, related or unrelated,
who are in need of supervision and/or assistance
with routine daily functions but who are not in need
4
of regular medical attention. Such a facility shall
E
comply with all state and local statutes, codes and/ L
or ordinances regarding licensing, zoning, building, C
fire, health, and housing. Does not include a Rooming I
T
House, Congregate Housing Facility, or Residential R
Care Facility. A
1. Duration of Care. The adults are receiving said
care on a regular and recurring basis during a part of
the 12 hour period between 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m.,
for not less than three and not more than 12 hours.
H. Day Care Center, Child
A facility providing either full-day or partial day child
care services, whether or not such service is known
as a day nursery, nursery school, child development
center, day care center, or any other name, which
serve on a regular and recurring basis, three or more
unrelated children. Does not include a Rooming
House, Congregate Housing Facility, or Residential
Care Facility.
1. Open Space. There shall be provided a minimum of
50 square feet of open play space on the lot for each
child. This requirement does not apply if the facility is
within 500 feet of a public park.
2. Additional Screening Required. A solid, six-foot-
high screening fence is required around all open-air
play areas, and shall conform to Section 8.4, Visibility
at Intersections.
3. Additional Setbacks Required. In addition to the
zoning district setback requirements, every building
shall be set back a minimum distance of 25 feet
from any adjacent residential property located in a
Residential (R) or Mixed-Use (MX) District.
