records.text:
ARTICLE 4: USES
I. Food Center/Supply Pantry
A not-for-profit use that distributes or facilitates the
giving of food, clothing, and/or other essential items at
no charge or for less than fair market value to persons
in need of assistance. Examples include soup kitchens
and regularly staffed drop-off centers for clothing,
household goods, and food.
1. Permitted as Accessory Use. A Food Center or
Supply Pantry is permitted as an accessory use to
a Place of Worship, as permitted pursuant to 4.4.4 .
A. Assembly, Neighborhood or 4.4.4 . B. Assembly,
General, or a Transient Shelter Facility.
2. Designated Waiting Areas. A Food Center or
Supply Pantry shall provide indoor, fully enclosed
waiting areas on the premises, which are adequate
to accommodate the maximum number of persons to
be served at any one time. The owner/operator must
ensure that persons receiving assistance do not block
public access to sidewalks, rights-of-way, or private
property, and that emergency access points are clearly
identified and maintained.
J. Government Facilities
Facilities and/or offices owned, operated, or occupied
by a government agency, including government
officials and departments. Includes post offices,
social service facilities, public works facilities, police
and fire facilities, and courthouses, as well as public
recreational facilities like ball parks, skate parks, and
athletic fields.
K. Halfway House
A building or facility that is owned and operated by the
federal or state government, or one of their agents,
in which offenders sentenced by a court to a period
of incarceration reside for purposes of reintegration
to society and remain under the operation of a prison
system.
1. Density of Use. The number of sleeping rooms
shall be limited to the number of dwelling units
otherwise permitted in the district; in no case to exceed
16 in any one facility.
2. Location Restriction. No halfway house shall be
located within 500 feet of any:
a. Residential (R) or Mixed-Use (MX) zoning district
boundary line;
b. Uses as defined as Assembly, Neighborhood;
Assembly, General; School, Elementary/Secondary;
Day Care Center, Child; or another Halfway House; or
c. City Hall, City Library, or a public park.
PRINCIPAL USE DEFINITIONS AND USE-SPECIFIC CONDITIONS
L. Hospital
A licensed facility that provides health, medical,
or surgical care to the sick or injured, including on
an inpatient basis. Includes related ancillary uses,
such as laboratories, outpatient clinics, pharmacies,
cafeterias, gift shops, training facilities, classrooms,
day care centers, central service facilities, helicopter
landing pads, and offices integral to function of the
facility.
M. Parks and Open Space
An open, outdoor space, public or private, designed
for active or passive recreational use or natural
resources protection. Includes parks, greens,
squares, plazas, botanical or ornamental gardens,
playfields and playgrounds, and monuments.
Includes related ancillary facilities, such as picnic
areas, gazebos, restrooms, concession stands, and
community gardens. Although allowed as an ancillary
use, the principal use of the lot shall not be a ball
court, swimming pool, golf course, or skate park,
which are principal uses pursuant to Section 4.4.6.M.
Entertainment or Recreational Facility, Outdoor .
1. Open Space Regulations. Certain organized open
spaces are subject to further regulation, pursuant to
Section 8.6, Open Spaces .
N. School: Elementary or
Secondary
A public, private, or parochial institution offering
instruction at the preschool through high school
levels with a full range of curricular programs,
including vocational and technical programs. Includes
related on-site ancillary facilities, such as cafeterias,
gymnasiums, theaters, playgrounds, and athletic
facilities.
O. Transient Shelter Facility
A public or non-profit facility providing temporary
housing, and social, health, and related services for
families or individuals 18 years of age or older, who
are without resources and access to shelter.
1. Operation of Use. The use shall only be operated
by or in conjunction with a governmental, welfare, or
charitable service.
2. On-Site Staffing Required. The facility shall have
staffing on-site during all hours of operation.
40 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE

of incarceration reside for purposes of reintegration 
to society and remain under the operation of a prison 
system.
1. Density of Use. The number of sleeping rooms 
shall be limited to the number of dwelling units 
otherwise permitted in the district; in no case to exceed 
16 in any one facility.
2. Location Restriction. No halfway house shall be 
located within 500 feet of any:
a. Residential (R) or Mixed-Use (MX) zoning district 
boundary line;
b. Uses as defined as Assembly, Neighborhood; 
Assembly, General; School, Elementary/Secondary; 
Day Care Center, Child; or another Halfway House; or
c. City Hall, City Library, or a public park.
L. Hospital
A licensed facility that provides health, medical, 
or surgical care to the sick or injured, including on 
an inpatient basis. Includes related ancillary uses, 
such as laboratories, outpatient clinics, pharmacies, 
cafeterias, gift shops, training facilities, classrooms, 
day care centers, central service facilities, helicopter 
landing pads, and offices integral to function of the 
facility.
M. Parks and Open Space
An open, outdoor space, public or private, designed 
for active or passive recreational use or natural 
resources protection. Includes parks, greens, 
squares, plazas, botanical or ornamental gardens, 
playfields and playgrounds, and monuments. 
Includes related ancillary facilities, such as picnic 
areas, gazebos, restrooms, concession stands, and 
community gardens. Although allowed as an ancillary 
use, the principal use of the lot shall not be a ball 
court, swimming pool, golf course, or skate park, 
which are principal uses pursuant to Section 4.4.6.M. 
Entertainment or Recreational Facility, Outdoor.
1. Open Space Regulations. Certain organized open 
spaces are subject to further regulation, pursuant to 
Section 8.6, Open Spaces.
N. School: Elementary or 
Secondary
A public, private, or parochial institution offering 
instruction at the preschool through high school 
levels with a full range of curricular programs, 
including vocational and technical programs. Includes 
related on-site ancillary facilities, such as cafeterias, 
gymnasiums, theaters, playgrounds, and athletic 
facilities.
O. Transient Shelter Facility
A public or non-profit facility providing temporary 
housing, and social, health, and related services for 
families or individuals 18 years of age or older, who 
are without resources and access to shelter.
1. Operation of Use. The use shall only be operated 
by or in conjunction with a governmental, welfare, or 
charitable service.
2. On-Site Staffing Required. The facility shall have 
staffing on-site during all hours of operation.

4.4.5 Office Uses
A category of uses for businesses involving activities
that may or may not be associated with walk-in
customers.
A. Bank
A financial institution, including credit unions, that is
engaged in deposit banking, and that performs closely
related functions such as making loans, investments,
and fiduciary activities.
1. Maximum Floor Area. Pursuant to Section 6.2.2
Mixed-Use (MX) Districts, in the MX-2, this use shall
not exceed 3,000 square feet in gross floor area per
building by-right, or up to 8,000 SF by Conditional Use
permit.
2. Drive-Through Facilities. A Drive-Through Facility
may be permitted per Table 4.5-A, Accessory Uses .
B. Contractor Office
A building that is used by a contractor engaged in
construction-related services and trades such as,
but not limited to: plumbing, heating, air conditioning,
ventilation, roofing, carpentry, remodeling, fencing,
and painting. May include internal storage of inventory
and additional parking for fleet vehicles. Such offices
that serve customers but do not provide any internal
storage or parking of any fleet vehicles shall be
considered a Professional Office use.
C. Professional Office
A facility for the processing or application of information
or professional expertise, including by businesses,
nonprofit organizations, and the government. When
such facility offers services to the public, they are
typically provided at set appointments or meeting
times, not on a walk-in basis. A list of typical
Professional Office uses is listed in Principal Use List
Table 4.3-B.3.
1. Conditional Use Permit Required in the MX-1
Zoning District. In addition to the limitations of this
section, the Planning Board may further limit this use
as part of the approval process for a Conditional Use
permit.
2. Maximum Floor Area. Pursuant to Section 6.2.2
Mixed-Use (MX) Districts, in the following districts, a
professional office use shall not exceed the following
square footage in gross floor area:
a. MX-1: 3,000 SF per building;
b. MX-2: 3,000 SF per building by-right, or up to
8,000 SF by Conditional Use permit.
ARTICLE 4: USES
4.4.6 Retail and Service Uses
A category of uses that provide patrons with services
and retail products.
A. Retail and Service,
Neighborhood
A use that offers personal goods and services of
a type or scale that directly benefit its surrounding
neighborhoods. Any outdoor display shall be limited
to no more than five percent of the indoor gross floor
area of the retail use. Neighborhood retail and service
includes such uses as those listed in Principal Use List
4
Table 4.3-B.1. Typical Neighborhood Retail & Service

Uses . L

I
Zoning District. In addition to the limitations of this T
R
section, the Planning Board may further limit this use
A
as part of the approval process for a Conditional Use
permit.
2. Maximum Floor Area. Pursuant to Section 6.2.2
Mixed-Use (MX) Districts, in the following districts, this
use shall not exceed the following square footage in
gross floor area:
a. MX-1: 3,000 SF per building; and
b. MX-2: 3,000 SF per building by-right, or up to
8,000 SF by Conditional Use permit.
3. Outdoor Display. Any portion of the lot used for
an outdoor display shall comply with 4.6.2.H. Outdoor
Display .
4. Deliveries. Except within the BC districts, deliveries
or pick-ups related to the use are limited to box trucks
or smaller vehicles.
B. Retail and Service, General
A use that offers goods and services of a type or scale
that benefits the regional community. It may include
permanent outdoor display, service, and storage
areas. Outdoor sales shall be limited to no more than
25 percent of the indoor gross floor area of the retail
use. General retail or service includes such uses as
those listed in Table 4.3-B.2. Typical General Retail &
Service Uses . Excludes vehicle sales or rental, or a
garden center, or outdoor storage yard.
1. Outdoor Display. Any portion of the lot used for
an outdoor display shall comply with Section 4.6.2.H.
Outdoor Display .
2. Any materials stored that exceed the height of the
screening shall be located a minimum of 25 feet from
any lot line.

records.text:
ARTICLE 4: USES
C. Animal Boarding and/or
Kenneling Facility
Any structure or premises on which four or more dogs,
cats and/or other household pets are boarded during
the day or for overnight stays. Includes ancillary
activities such as breeding, selling, grooming, training,
or keeping animals for adoption or sale. This use
excludes Veterinary Services (see Section 4.4.6.AD.
Veterinary Services ) and facilities only providing
services located indoors that operate during the day,
such as animal grooming (see Section 4.4.6.A. Retail
and Service, Neighborhood ) or animal day training
(see Section 4.4.6.B. Retail and Service, General ).
1. Minimum Lot Area. The minimum lot size shall be
45,000 square feet.
D. Bar/Tavern/Night Club
An establishment primarily engaged in the sale or
dispensing of alcoholic beverages by the drink for
on-site consumption. May include related ancillary
activities, such as the sale of merchandise associated
with the branding of the establishment, the availability
of food for on-site consumption, production of alcoholic
beverages, and live entertainment, which are clearly
incidental and subordinate to the use.
E. Beer/Wine/Liquor Sales
An establishment whose primary business, in terms
of gross floor area or sales, is the sale of alcoholic
beverages for off-site consumption with such sales to
be made only in sealed bottles or other containers.
F. Brewery, Distillery, or Winery
A facility for the production and packaging of malt or
fermented beverages of alcoholic content or alcoholic
spirits for retail sales on-site. It may also include
related ancillary activities such as a tasting room
where guests may sample the facility’s products with
the availability of food for on-site consumption, the
sale of merchandise associated with the branding
of the brewery, distillery, or winery, outdoor dining,
and live entertainment that is clearly incidental and
subordinate to the brewery, distillery, or winery use.
Outdoor sales are prohibited.
1. Maximum Floor Area. Within the BC-1, DT-1,
and DT-2, the gross floor area of the facility shall not
exceed 10,000 square feet.
2. Deliveries. Except within the BC-2 and IND,
deliveries or pick-ups related to the use are limited to
parcel and box trucks or smaller vehicles.
PRINCIPAL USE DEFINITIONS AND USE-SPECIFIC CONDITIONS
G. Broadcasting Studio
An establishment containing one or more broadcasting
studios for over-the-air, cable or satellite delivery of
radio or television programs, or studios for the audio
or video recording or filming of musical performances,
radio or television programs or motion pictures. This
term does not include a telecommunications tower.
This use does not include a “podcast studio” use, as
such use is included within Section 4.4.6.A. Retail and
Service, Neighborhood .
H. Car Wash
An establishment for the washing of motor vehicles
that may employ production-line methods, mechanical
devices, staffed hand wash facilities, or unstaffed self-
wash facilities. May include ancillary vacuuming and
auto detailing services.
1. Landscaping. A landscaped buffer yard is required
at certain district boundaries, pursuant to Section 8.1.2
Landscaped Buffer Yards .
2. Location Restriction. A car wash shall be located
at least 500 feet from any other car wash use.
I. Casino or Charitable Gaming
Facility
A commercial facility where patrons wager money on
the outcome of a game including, but not limited to, a
card game or a slot machine.
J. Commercial School

PRINCIPAL USE DEFINITIONS AND USE-SPECIFIC CONDITIONS
K. Commercial Equipment and
Supply
A use involving the large-scale sale of goods to
residents or businesses within the region. The goods
or merchandise sold may be of the same type or a
variety of types and typically occupy a space greater
than 20,000 square feet. This use may include bulk
sales and typically involves frequent commercial
vehicle and consumer traffic. This use is primarily
located indoors, but may also include accessory
outdoor storage of goods. This includes such uses as
the sales and supply of building materials, hardware,
and lumber; cabinetry; electronics; farm equipment;
heating and air conditioning units; machinery; marine
and aircraft supply; plumbing; and wholesale trade.
Does not include uses as defined in Section 4.4.6.Y.
Truck and Heavy Equipment Sales, Rental, and
Repair , or Section 4.4.7.D. Bulk Fuel Storage .
1. Landscaping. A landscaped buffer yard is required
at certain district boundaries, pursuant to Section 8.1.2
Landscaped Buffer Yards .
2. Screening. Loading docks shall be fully screened
from any residential uses.
3. The use of Commercial Equipment and Supply may
or may not have an accessory use of Outdoor Storage,
as permitted per Table 4.5-A, Accessory Uses , and
defined in Section 4.6.2.I. Outdoor Storage.
L. Entertainment or Recreational
Facility, Indoor
A facility for leisure uses conducted within an
enclosed building. Includes such uses as amusement
centers, arcades, bowling alleys, live and movie
theaters, music venues, pool halls, skating and roller
rinks and facilities, and tumbling centers. Includes
related ancillary uses, such as food service. Excludes
Assembly uses, Casino or Gaming Facility, and
Shooting Range, Indoor.
M. Entertainment or Recreational
Facility, Outdoor
A facility for leisure uses conducted outdoors or within
partially enclosed structures. Includes such uses as
amusement parks, batting cages, campgrounds, drive-
in movie theaters, fairgrounds, golf courses, miniature
golf courses, golf driving ranges, recreational vehicle
parks, skating parks, and tennis clubs. Includes
related ancillary uses, such as food service. Excludes
Assembly uses and Shooting Range, Outdoor.
ARTICLE 4: USES
N. Funeral Services
A facility where the deceased are prepared for burial
display and for rituals before burial or cremation.
Includes such facilities as chapels, funeral homes,
crematoriums, and showrooms for the display and
sale of caskets, vaults, urns, and other items related
to burial services.
1. Location Restriction for Crematoriums. A
crematorium is considered a heavy industrial use and
shall comply with Section 4.4.7.B. Industrial, Heavy .
Funeral services uses that include crematoriums are
only permitted in the Industrial (IND) District.
4
2. Conditional Use Permit Required in the MX-2. In
E
addition to the limitations of this section, the Planning L
Board may further limit this use as part of the approval C
process for a Conditional Use permit. I
T
R
3. Maximum Floor Area. Pursuant to 6.2.2 Mixed-Use
A
(MX) Districts, in the MX-2, this use shall not exceed
3,000 square feet in gross floor area per building by-
right, or up to 8,000 SF by Conditional Use permit.
O. Garden Center
An establishment that includes indoor and outdoor retail
sales of plants, lawn furniture, and garden supplies.
The selling of floral arrangements and decorations is
considered a “Florist” use, and regulated as a “Retail
and Service, Neighborhood” use.
1. Maximum Outdoor Retail Area. An outdoor retail
sales area for a garden center in the BC-1 shall not
exceed 2,000 square feet.
P. Medical Clinic
Medical Clinic means a licensed institution providing
same-day, walk-in, or urgent medical care and health
services to the community, primarily ill or injured out-
patients, that is not a hospital. Provision of an indoor
waiting area for use by individuals is required, so
that clients will not be required or allowed to queue
for services outdoors. A Medical Clinic use may offer
services by physicians, optometrists, podiatrists,
dentists, chiropractors, physical therapists, mental
health practitioners and therapists, phlebotomists, or
other licensed healthcare practitioners to examine and
treat persons on an outpatient basis. A medical clinic
shall not provide rental services, storage of hazardous
materials in large quantities, or dormitory facilities.
1. Conditional Use Permit Required in the MX-2. In
addition to the limitations of this section, the Planning
Board may further limit this use as part of the approval
process for a Conditional Use permit.

vehicle and consumer traffic. This use is primarily
located indoors, but may also include accessory
outdoor storage of goods. This includes such uses as
the sales and supply of building materials, hardware,
and lumber; cabinetry; electronics; farm equipment;
heating and air conditioning units; machinery; marine
and aircraft supply; plumbing; and wholesale trade.
Does not include uses as defined in Section 4.4.6.Y.
Truck and Heavy Equipment Sales, Rental, and
Repair , or Section 4.4.7.D. Bulk Fuel Storage .

at certain district boundaries, pursuant to Section 8.1.2
Landscaped Buffer Yards .
2. Screening. Loading docks shall be fully screened
from any residential uses.
3. The use of Commercial Equipment and Supply may
or may not have an accessory use of Outdoor Storage,
as permitted per Table 4.5-A, Accessory Uses , and
defined in Section 4.6.2.I. Outdoor Storage.
L. Entertainment or Recreational
Facility, Indoor
A facility for leisure uses conducted within an
enclosed building. Includes such uses as amusement
centers, arcades, bowling alleys, live and movie
theaters, music venues, pool halls, skating and roller
rinks and facilities, and tumbling centers. Includes
related ancillary uses, such as food service. Excludes
Assembly uses, Casino or Gaming Facility, and
Shooting Range, Indoor.
M. Entertainment or Recreational
Facility, Outdoor
A facility for leisure uses conducted outdoors or within
partially enclosed structures. Includes such uses as
amusement parks, batting cages, campgrounds, drive-
in movie theaters, fairgrounds, golf courses, miniature
golf courses, golf driving ranges, recreational vehicle
parks, skating parks, and tennis clubs. Includes
related ancillary uses, such as food service. Excludes
Assembly uses and Shooting Range, Outdoor.

N. Funeral Services
A facility where the deceased are prepared for burial
display and for rituals before burial or cremation.
Includes such facilities as chapels, funeral homes,
crematoriums, and showrooms for the display and
sale of caskets, vaults, urns, and other items related
to burial services.
1. Location Restriction for Crematoriums. A
crematorium is considered a heavy industrial use and
shall comply with Section 4.4.7.B. Industrial, Heavy .
Funeral services uses that include crematoriums are
only permitted in the Industrial (IND) District.

An establishment that includes indoor and outdoor retail

and Service, Neighborhood” use.

Medical Clinic means a licensed institution providing
same-day, walk-in, or urgent medical care and health
services to the community, primarily ill or injured out-
patients, that is not a hospital. Provision of an indoor
waiting area for use by individuals is required, so
that clients will not be required or allowed to queue
for services outdoors. A Medical Clinic use may offer
services by physicians, optometrists, podiatrists,

treat persons on an outpatient basis. A medical clinic
shall not provide rental services, storage of hazardous

right, or up to 8,000 SF by Conditional Use permit.
3. Drive-through services may be permitted per Table
4.5-A, Accessory Uses.
R. Private Club/Lodge
A facility for an organization that does not operate for
profit and that excludes the general public but is open
to people upon invitation, nomination, or payment of
annual fees or dues, for social, recreational, political,
and/or entertainment activities. A Private Club/Lodge
may serve meals and alcohol on the premises for
members and their guests only.
1. Location Restriction. New Private Club/Lodges
that abut a Residential (R), or Mixed-Use (MX) zoning
district shall not be located within 1,500 feet of another
Private Club/Lodge.
S. Restaurant
An establishment where food and beverages are
prepared for and served to patrons for consumption
either on or off-premises. Includes such uses as
cafes, coffee shops, bakeries, diners, fast-food
establishments, lunch counters, and cafeterias. This
use excludes the production of food, food products,
or beverages for wholesale distribution (See Section
4.4.7.A. Industrial, Artisan or Craftsman ). Ancillary
services may include the sale of alcohol for on-site
consumption, production of alcoholic beverages,
outdoor dining, and live entertainment, that are clearly
incidental and subordinate to the use, except as further
regulated by Conditional Use permit in the Mixed-Use
(MX-1 and MX-2) Zoning Districts.
PRINCIPAL USE DEFINITIONS AND USE-SPECIFIC CONDITIONS
1. Conditional Use Permit Required in Mixed-Use
Zoning Districts (MX-1 and MX-2). In addition to the
limitations of this section, the Planning Board may
further limit this use as part of the approval process for
a Conditional Use permit.
2. Maximum Floor Area. Pursuant to 6.2.2 Mixed-
Use (MX) Districts, in the following districts, this use
shall not exceed the following square footage in gross
floor area:
a. MX-1: 3,000 SF per building;
b. MX-2: 3,000 SF per building by-right, or up to
8,000 SF by Conditional Use permit.
3. A drive-through may be permitted as accessory to
the use of a Restaurant per Table 4.5-A, Accessory
Uses.
4. Ventilation systems may not be installed on any
façade that faces a public street or an adjacent
residential property.
T. Sexually Oriented Business
A business that sells or disseminates explicit sexual
material, and at which access to the public display of
explicit sexual material is restricted by law to persons
18 years of age or older. Businesses include, but are
not limited to, the following: adult bookstore or adult
video store, adult cabaret, adult drive-in theater, adult
motion picture theater, adult motion picture arcade,
adult motel, adult theater, nude model studio, or
sexual encounter center.
1. Definitions. Please see Article 2: Definitions, for
each individual type of Sexually Oriented Business, as
listed above.
2. Location Restriction.
a. No sexually oriented business shall be permitted
within 600 feet of another sexually oriented business
which is either existing at the time of the effective
date of this Ordinance or one for which a building
permit has been applied for, and no sexually oriented
business shall be permitted within a building,
premises, structure, or other facility that contains
another sexually oriented business;
b. No sexually oriented business shall be located
within 500 feet of any:
(1) Residential (R) or Mixed-Use (MX) district
boundary line;
(2) Uses defined as: Assembly, Neighborhood;
Assembly, General; School, Elementary/
Secondary; or Day Care Center, Child; or
(3) City boundary line; and

compactors, drills, excavators, graders, harvesters,
mulchers, pavers, trailers, wheel loaders, etc). This
use also includes on-site facilities for the repair and
service of vehicles and equipment sold, leased, or
rented.

ARTICLE 4: USES
4. Any repair and service operations shall be
performed within a fully enclosed building. Bay doors
may be open during hours of operation.
5. No partially dismantled or wrecked vehicle shall be
stored outdoors.
6. Any outdoor display area shall comply with the
standards set for the accessory use in Section 4.6.2.H.
Outdoor Display .
AB. Vehicle Repair, Major
A business that offers repair services such as engine
rebuilding; major reconditioning of worn or damaged
motor vehicles or trailers; towing and collision service,
including body, frame, or fender straightening or repair;
painting of motor vehicles; or repair to commercial
vehicles, recreational vehicles, or watercraft.
This does not include Section 4.4.6.Y. Truck and
Heavy Equipment Sales, Rental, and Repair or
Section 4.4.7.I. Towing Facility/Impound Yard .
1. Landscaping. A landscaped buffer yard is required
at certain district boundaries, pursuant to Section 8.1.2
Landscaped Buffer Yards .
2. Any repair and service operations shall be
performed within a fully enclosed building. Bay doors
may be open during hours of operation.
3. Accessory outdoor storage is permitted, pursuant
to Section 4.6.2.I. Outdoor Storage. No partially
dismantled, wrecked, or unregistered vehicle may be
stored outdoors for more than 30 days. Temporary
storage of such vehicles is allowed within the side and
rear yards only, so long as they are not visible from a
public street.
AC. Vehicle Repair, Minor
A business that offers minor repairs to motor vehicles,
including, but not limited to, repair or replacement
of cooling, electrical, fuel, and exhaust systems; oil
changes; brake adjustments, relining, and repairs;
wheel servicing, alignment, and balancing; repair
and replacement of shock absorbers; detailing; and
replacement or adjustment of muffler systems, hoses,
belts, fuses, windshield wipers, and the like. Minor
vehicle repair also includes repairs to two-wheeled
and three-wheeled motor vehicles, and may include
incidental, ancillary towing and collision service.
1. Landscaping. A landscaped buffer yard is required
at certain district boundaries, pursuant to Section 8.1.2
Landscaped Buffer Yards .
PRINCIPAL USE DEFINITIONS AND USE-SPECIFIC CONDITIONS
2. Any repair and service operations must be
performed within a fully enclosed building. Bay doors
may be open during hours of operation.
3. A minor vehicle repair use may not include vehicle
dismantling. No partially dismantled, wrecked, or
unregistered vehicle may be stored on-site.
AD. Veterinary Services
A business which provides care for animals, including
the immunization, diagnosis, or treatment of
animals, where animals may be boarded during their
convalescence.
4.4.7 Industrial Uses
A category of uses for businesses involving assembly,
production, storing, transferring and disposal of goods
or products, and that may also include associated
facilities such as offices, maintenance facilities, and
fuel pumps and both indoor and outdoor activities
including storage of goods. All outdoor storage
associated with Industrial uses shall adhere to the
provisions in Section 5.6.3 Accessory Structures
Located in All Other Districts. All Industrial uses are
subject to the standards outlined in Section 4.1.7
Performance Standards for Noxious or Hazardous
Uses .
A. Industrial, Artisan or Craftsman
An indoor manufacturing use involving small-scale
production, assembly, and/or repair with no noxious
by-products. Includes related ancillary uses and
facilities, such as a restaurant, showroom, office,
storage, sales, and distribution of products. A list of
such typical uses is in Table 4.3-B.4. Typical Artisan or
Craftsman Industry Uses.
1. Maximum Floor Area. Artisan industrial uses shall
not exceed 10,000 square feet of gross floor area.
2. Landscaping. A landscaped buffer yard is required
at certain district boundaries, pursuant to Section 8.1.2
Landscaped Buffer Yards .
3. Outdoor storage is prohibited, except when it is
an accessory use within the IND. See Section 4.6.2.I.
Outdoor Storage, for additional outdoor storage
regulations.
4. Deliveries or pick-ups related to the use are limited
to parcel and small freight carriers.

manufacturing.

or for use in industrial processes and distributed to the

ARTICLE 4: USES
1. Landscaping. A landscaped buffer yard is required
at certain district boundaries, pursuant to Section 8.1.2
Landscaped Buffer Yards .
2. No outside storage shall be provided on-site.
3. Access to individual storage units shall be provided
from common areas or hallways located indoors. No
direct access or outward appearance of direct access
to an individual storage space shall be provided from
the building exterior.
I. Towing Facility/Impound Yard
An establishment that provides vehicle towing
services and/or temporary outdoor storage for
impounded vehicles, which shall only include: (1)
mechanically operable/drivable, licensed vehicles
that are to be claimed by titleholders or their agents;
and/or (2) wrecked motor vehicles awaiting insurance
adjustments and transport to repair shops. This use
excludes junkyards.
1. Landscaping. A landscaped buffer yard is required
at certain district boundaries, pursuant to Section 8.1.2
Landscaped Buffer Yards . Wherever a landscaped
buffer yard is not otherwise required, a solid, eight
foot high fence shall be provided around all stored
materials.
J. Warehouse/Distribution
A facility for the storage, transfer, wholesaling, and
distribution of goods. If a warehouse/distribution use is
ancillary to another principal use, and has a gross floor
area of less than 10,000 square feet, it is considered
part of the principal use and is not considered a
separate principal use. A list of typical uses is in Table
4.3-B. 6. Typical Warehouse / Distribution Uses.
1. Landscaping. A landscaped buffer yard is required
at certain district boundaries, pursuant to Section 8.1.2
Landscaped Buffer Yards .
2. Where allowed, outdoor storage is not permitted
within an established front or street yard unless the
storage area is enclosed with a solid screening fence
of eight feet in height.
3. Within a Business Corridor (BC-1, BC-2) or Millyard
district, all goods shall be stored within a completely
enclosed structure. Warehousing and distribution
facilities in other districts are not subject to this
limitation.
PRINCIPAL USE DEFINITIONS AND USE-SPECIFIC CONDITIONS
K. Waste Processing/Recycling
Facility
A facility for the collection, storage, and transfer of
solid waste, which may include the collection, storage,
processing, and transfer of recyclables, and organic
and yard waste. Excludes junkyards, industrial or
sanitary landfills, and waste incineration facilities.
1. Landscaping. A landscaped buffer yard is required
at certain district boundaries, pursuant to Section 8.1.2
Landscaped Buffer Yards .
2. Outdoor storage is not permitted within an
established front or street yard. See Section 4.6.2.I.
Outdoor Storage, for additional regulations.
4.4.8 Transportation Uses
A category of uses for the provision of public and
private transportation systems to support other uses.
Accessory structures may be included, and shall be
subject to any additional regulations in Section 5.6 ,
Accessory Structures .
A. Airport
A facility for the takeoff, landing, and maintenance of
civil aircraft. Includes related ancillary uses, such as
runways, passenger terminals, hangars, and control
towers.
B. Dispatch Facility
A facility where ambulances, taxis, limousines, armored
cars, tow trucks, and similar vehicles for specialized
transportation are stored, and from which they are
dispatched, and/or where ambulance vehicles and
crews not based at a hospital or fire department stand
by for emergency calls. A dispatch facility may include
ancillary professional offices and vehicle repair.
1. The storage of vehicles shall be within a fully
enclosed structure. This requirement does not apply in
the IND.
2. In the IND, outside storage of vehicles is allowed
within interior side and rear yards only, so long as it is
not visible from any public right-of-way other than an
alley.
C. Freight Terminal or Facility
A facility for freight pick-up, transfer, or distribution
by air, rail, or truck. Excludes Warehouse/Distribution
uses.

solid waste, which may include the collection, storage, 
processing, and transfer of recyclables, and organic 
and yard waste. Excludes junkyards, industrial or 
sanitary landfills, and waste incineration facilities.
1. Landscaping. A landscaped buffer yard is required 
at certain district boundaries, pursuant to Section 8.1.2

established front or street yard. See Section 4.6.2.I. 
Outdoor Storage, for additional regulations.

A category of uses for the provision of public and 
private transportation systems to support other uses.

subject to any additional regulations in Section 5.6,

civil aircraft. Includes related ancillary uses, such as 
runways, passenger terminals, hangars, and control 
towers.

cars, tow trucks, and similar vehicles for specialized 
transportation are stored, and from which they are 
dispatched, and/or where ambulance vehicles and 
crews not based at a hospital or fire department stand 
by for emergency calls. A dispatch facility may include 
ancillary professional offices and vehicle repair.

A facility for freight pick-up, transfer, or distribution

freestanding (solely self-supported by attachment

1. Minimum Lot Area. There shall be a minimum lot
area of 6,000 square feet. Telecommunications towers
located in a district with a larger minimum lot area
requirement shall still adhere to the district requirement.
2. Fencing and Landscaping. A permanent fence
with a maximum height of eight feet shall be required
to secure the base of the facility. Landscaping shall be
provided along the perimeter of the lot in compliance
with the Type 3 landscaped buffer yard, pursuant to
Section 8.1.2 Landscaped Buffer Yards .
3. Tower Height and Setback. If a new
telecommunications tower is constructed, the tower
shall not exceed the height of 160 feet and shall be
located a minimum of 160 feet, or the height of the
tower, from any lot line, measured from the base of
tower to the property line.
4. Criteria for a Conditional Use Permit. In all
instances where a Conditional Use permit is required
for a telecommunications tower, the Planning Board
shall evaluate the application using the criteria in
Section 10.1 , as well as consider the following topics:
a. Proposals to mitigate possible visual impact,
including the preservation of view corridors and
vistas;
b. Potential for preservation of preexisting character
of site;
c. Minimal impact on residential areas surrounding
commercial or industrial zoned sites; and
d. Accessibility of roads, electric power, land-based
telephone lines, or microwave link capability, other
utilities required for the proper functioning of the
communication facility.
D. Utilities and Services, Major
Large-scale facilities that primarily serve a regional
need, which because of their scale or method of
operation are more likely to produce external impacts
that are detectable beyond the property lines of the
subject property. Such facilities include, but are not
limited to, sewage treatment plants, electric or gas
generation plants.
E. Utilities and Services, Minor
Facilities and services that primarily serve local
distribution needs, including but not limited to, water
and sewer pump stations, electrical transforming

and produce electric power for distribution to
consumers, typically managed by a single entity, and
exceeding a rated capacity of 500 kW.
1. Setbacks. Wind turbines must be set back from all
buildings and all lot lines a distance of 110 percent of
the turbine tip height, as measured from the nearest
point on the foundation of the occupied building to the
nearest point on the outside edge of a tower. Turbine
tip height is measured from the base of the tower to
the tip of a propeller at maximum vertical rotation.
Accessory operation and maintenance buildings and
substations must be set back in accordance with the
corresponding building type standards as outlined in
Section 5.3 .

freestanding (solely self-supported by attachment

1. Minimum Lot Area. There shall be a minimum lot 
area of 6,000 square feet. Telecommunications towers 
located in a district with a larger minimum lot area 
requirement shall still adhere to the district requirement.
2. Fencing and Landscaping. A permanent fence 
with a maximum height of eight feet shall be required 
to secure the base of the facility. Landscaping shall be 
provided along the perimeter of the lot in compliance 
with the Type 3 landscaped buffer yard, pursuant to 
Section 8.1.2 Landscaped Buffer Yards.
3. Tower Height and Setback. If a new 
telecommunications tower is constructed, the tower 
shall not exceed the height of 160 feet and shall be 
located a minimum of 160 feet, or the height of the 
tower, from any lot line, measured from the base of 
tower to the property line.
4. Criteria for a Conditional Use Permit. In all 
instances where a Conditional Use permit is required 
for a telecommunications tower, the Planning Board 
shall evaluate the application using the criteria in 
Section 10.1, as well as consider the following topics:
a. Proposals to mitigate possible visual impact, 
including the preservation of view corridors and 
vistas;
b. Potential for preservation of preexisting character 
of site;
c. Minimal impact on residential areas surrounding 
commercial or industrial zoned sites; and 
d. Accessibility of roads, electric power, land-based 
telephone lines, or microwave link capability, other 
utilities required for the proper functioning of the 
communication facility.
D. Utilities and Services, Major
Large-scale facilities that primarily serve a regional 
need, which because of their scale or method of 
operation are more likely to produce external impacts 
that are detectable beyond the property lines of the 
subject property. Such facilities include, but are not 
limited to, sewage treatment plants, electric or gas 
generation plants.
E. Utilities and Services, Minor
Facilities and services that primarily serve local 
distribution needs, including but not limited to, water 
and sewer pump stations, electrical transforming 
substations, water conveyance stations, gas 
regulating stations, telephone exchange/switching 
centers, emergency communication warning/
broadcast facilities, and water towers and tanks.
F. Wind Farm
A site at which wind turbines are erected to generate 
and produce electric power for distribution to 
consumers, typically managed by a single entity, and 
exceeding a rated capacity of 500 kW.
1. Setbacks. Wind turbines must be set back from all 
buildings and all lot lines a distance of 110 percent of 
the turbine tip height, as measured from the nearest 
point on the foundation of the occupied building to the 
nearest point on the outside edge of a tower. Turbine 
tip height is measured from the base of the tower to 
the tip of a propeller at maximum vertical rotation. 
Accessory operation and maintenance buildings and 
substations must be set back in accordance with the 
corresponding building type standards as outlined in 
Section 5.3.

ACCESSORY USES
Section 4.5
ACCESSORY USES
4.5.1 General Provisions
A. Accessory Uses Allowed
Accessory uses are allowed only in connection with
lawfully established principal uses. Accessory uses
for nonconforming principal uses and structures are
treated under Article 10.
B. Allowed Uses
Allowed accessory uses are limited to those
expressly regulated in this article as well as those
that, in the determination of the Director, satisfy all of
the following criteria:
1. They are subordinate and clearly incidental to the
principal use(s) of the property; and
2. Either:
a. They are customarily found in conjunction with
the subject principal use(s) or principal structure;
b. They serve a necessary function for the comfort,
safety, or convenience of occupants of the principal
use(s) (cafeterias, recreation and fitness facilities,
or multimedia rooms); or
c. They serve a necessary or beneficial function to
the general public (ie. biking or pedestrian paths,
parks, or community gardens);
C. Accessory Structures
Some accessory uses also involve the establishment
of an accessory structure. Refer to Section 5.6,
Accessory Structures .
D. Time of Establishment
Accessory uses may be established only after the
principal use of the property is established.
ARTICLE 4: USES
4.5.2 Table of Accessory Uses
Table 4.5-A, Accessory Uses identifies the accessory
uses allowed in each zoning district. Accessory uses
are defined in Section 4.6, Accessory Use Definitions
and Use-Specific Conditions, and each defined use
is given one of the following designations: permitted
by right (“P”), permitted by Conditional Use permit
(“CU”), permitted by Special Exception (“SE”), or not
permitted “(-)”.

Section 4.6
ACCESSORY USE
DEFINITIONS AND USE-
SPECIFIC CONDITIONS
4.6.1 Accessory to Residential
Uses
A category of uses for residential accommodations.
A. Accessory Dwelling Unit
Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) are intended
to provide more diverse, affordable housing
opportunities to the community without the need for
additional infrastructure or further land development.
ADUs shall be subject to the following conditions
and limitations to occupancy and shall be subject to
all applicable requirements of this Ordinance, unless
expressly exempted in this Section.
1. Quantity. ADUs shall only be permitted as
accessories to single-family dwellings. Not more
than one ADU shall be permitted per single-family
dwelling. An ADU may be located within a single-
family dwelling, attached to a single-family dwelling,
within or above its attached or detached garage, or
as a standalone structure. Any ADU located within a
garage shall not displace those portions of the garage
necessary to provide required off-street parking for
the principal residential use.
2. Owner Occupied. Either the principal dwelling
unit or the ADU must be owner occupied. The
owner must demonstrate that one of the units is
the owner’s principal place of residence. Both the
principal dwelling unit and the ADU must remain in
common ownership. Transfer of either dwelling unit
to condominium ownership is not permitted. Prior to
the issuance of a certificate of occupancy for an ADU,
the property owner shall record a deed restriction or
similar document that mandates owner occupancy of
the principal dwelling unit or ADU in perpetuity.
3. Number of Bedrooms Allowed. No more than
two bedrooms shall be permitted within an ADU.
4. Size.
a. An ADU shall not exceed 950 square feet of
gross floor area.
b. An ADU located within or attached to a principal
structure shall not occupy an entire floor of the
principal structure and shall not exceed 40 percent
of the gross floor area of the principal structure.
ARTICLE 4: USES
c. The gross floor area of an ADU located within
an accessory structure that is detached from the
principal structure shall not exceed 40 percent
of the gross floor area of the principal structure.
The total floor area of the entirety of the detached
structure shall not exceed 80 percent of the total
floor area of the entirety of the principal structure,
excluding the basements of either structure.
d. The percentages in subsections b and c shall
not require an ADU to be smaller than 750 square
feet of gross floor area.
5. Parking. One additional off-street parking space
shall be provided for the ADU. The required parking 4
space shall be provided either on-site or at a legally E
dedicated off-site location, at the property owner’s L
C
discretion. No additional curb cut shall be established
I
to serve the ADU. T
R
6. Adequate Utilities. Where municipal sewer A
service is not provided, the septic system shall meet
NH Water Supply and Pollution Control Division
requirements for the combined system demand
for total occupancy of the premises. Where utilities
are available, the ADUs shall be connected to the
existing utilities within the subject parcel and shall not
be separately connected from the public right-of-way,
unless mandated by the provider of the utility.
7. Design Standards. ADUs shall adhere to the
same height, entrance type, and street façade
standards as that of a House principal building type,
pursuant to 5.3.1.A. House building type standards .
8. Impact Fees Required. The creation of a new
dwelling unit requires the payment of impact fees in
accordance with Article 11 .
9. Detached ADUs as Accessory Structures. All
detached ADUs shall be constructed in compliance
with Section 5.6.5.C. Detached Accessory Dwelling
Units (ADUs) .
B. Domestic Beekeeping
It is the intent of this section to permit the keeping
of bees and apiaries in single family residential
areas and to establish certain requirements of sound
beekeeping practices, which are intended to prevent
problems that may otherwise be associated with
domestic beekeeping in populated areas. Domestic
beekeeping and the maintenance of apiaries shall
be in accordance with the following provisions:
1. Locations Allowed. Domestic beekeeping is
only permitted as an accessory use on lots utilized
for single-family residential purposes. Domestic

beekeeping is also permitted as part of the principal
use of Agriculture with Livestock and shall be allowed
as part of that principal use in those zoning districts
designated under Table 4.3-A , Principal Uses .
2. Limitations. The owner of the property shall be
a resident of the single-family dwelling unit on the
lot where they are kept. Domestic beekeeping shall
be for personal use only, except in accordance with
Sections 4.6.2.F. Farm Stand for Agricultural Uses
and 4.7.4 Seasonal Sales for Residential Uses .
3. Nuisance. Notwithstanding compliance with the
various requirements of this Section, a beekeeper
shall be prohibited from keeping any colony or
colonies of bees in such a manner as to create a
nuisance or menace to the public health and safety
or to interfere with the normal use and enjoyment by
persons and animals of any public or private property.
4. Beehives as Accessory Structures. Any beehive
associated with the use of domestic beekeeping shall
conform to the standards as described in Section
5.6.5.B. Beehives.
C. Domestic Keeping of Chickens
It is the intent of this Section to allow for the keeping
of domestic chickens in single-family residential
areas for the sole use and enjoyment of the
residents of the lot on which such animals are kept.
It is also the intent of this Section to protect and
promote the health, safety, and welfare of residents
by not allowing chickens of a number or type that
would otherwise constitute a nuisance or menace
to the public health and safety or cause disturbance
of the peace in neighborhoods. Chickens kept as
domesticated pets by the residents of a dwelling unit
shall be maintained in accordance with all applicable
City of Manchester ordinances and regulations, New
Hampshire RSA 644:8 Cruelty to Animals, as well as
the following provisions:
1. Locations Allowed. Domestic chickens are only
permitted as an accessory use on lots which are a
minimum of a half acre (21,780 square feet) in size,
and which are utilized for single-family residential
purposes.
2. Number and Type of Chickens Allowed. Up to
six hens of any breed may be kept. Roosters are not
permitted.
3. Limitations. The keeping of chickens shall be for
personal use only. The owner of the property shall
be a resident of the single family dwelling unit on the
lot where they are kept. No person shall sell eggs

or engage in chicken breeding, slaughtering, or any
commercial activity related to the keeping of the
hens.
4. Henhouses and Fenced Areas Required. All
hens shall be kept within structures and fenced areas
and shall not be permitted to roam free nor to be kept
or raised within a dwelling. Henhouses and fenced
areas shall also meet the following standards:
a. Henhouses and fenced areas shall, at all times,
adequately contain the hens, provide them with
adequate ventilation, be kept in a neat and sanitary
condition, and be maintained in a manner that will
not disturb the use or enjoyment of neighboring
lots due to noise, odor or other adverse impact.
The henhouse shall provide a minimum of three
square feet per hen;
b. Henhouses and fenced enclosures shall be
enclosed on all sides, and shall provide adequate
protection for the hens from weather and wild or
domestic animals;
c. The henhouse shall be located upon a
permeable surface that prevents waste runoff and
the materials used in making the henhouse shall
be uniform for each element of the structure. The
use of scrap material shall be prohibited;
d. All chicken feed shall be securely stored and
protected from the elements and vermin; and
e. All stored manure shall be composted in a fully
enclosed structure or container and no more than
three cubic feet of composting manure shall be
stored on the involved lot. All other manure not
used for composting or fertilizing shall be removed
from the property.
5. Henhouses as Accessory Structures. Any
henhouse associated with the use of the domestic
keeping of chickens shall conform to the standards
as described in Section 5.6.5.G. Henhouses .

Sections 4.6.2.F. Farm Stand for Agricultural Uses 
and 4.7.4 Seasonal Sales for Residential Uses. 
3. Nuisance. Notwithstanding compliance with the 
various requirements of this Section, a beekeeper 
shall be prohibited from keeping any colony or 
colonies of bees in such a manner as to create a 
nuisance or menace to the public health and safety 
or to interfere with the normal use and enjoyment by 
persons and animals of any public or private property.
4. Beehives as Accessory Structures. Any beehive 
associated with the use of domestic beekeeping shall 
conform to the standards as described in Section 
5.6.5.B. Beehives.
C. Domestic Keeping of Chickens
It is the intent of this Section to allow for the keeping 
of domestic chickens in single-family residential 
areas for the sole use and enjoyment of the 
residents of the lot on which such animals are kept. 
It is also the intent of this Section to protect and 
promote the health, safety, and welfare of residents 
by not allowing chickens of a number or type that 
would otherwise constitute a nuisance or menace 
to the public health and safety or cause disturbance 
of the peace in neighborhoods. Chickens kept as 
domesticated pets by the residents of a dwelling unit 
shall be maintained in accordance with all applicable 
City of Manchester ordinances and regulations, New 
Hampshire RSA 644:8 Cruelty to Animals, as well as 
the following provisions:
1. Locations Allowed. Domestic chickens are only 
permitted as an accessory use on lots which are a 
minimum of a half acre (21,780 square feet) in size, 
and which are utilized for single-family residential 
purposes.
2. Number and Type of Chickens Allowed. Up to 
six hens of any breed may be kept. Roosters are not 
permitted.
3. Limitations. The keeping of chickens shall be for 
personal use only. The owner of the property shall 
be a resident of the single family dwelling unit on the 
lot where they are kept. No person shall sell eggs 
or engage in chicken breeding, slaughtering, or any 
commercial activity related to the keeping of the 
hens.
4. Henhouses and Fenced Areas Required. All 
hens shall be kept within structures and fenced areas 
and shall not be permitted to roam free nor to be kept 
or raised within a dwelling. Henhouses and fenced 
areas shall also meet the following standards:
a. Henhouses and fenced areas shall, at all times, 
adequately contain the hens, provide them with 
adequate ventilation, be kept in a neat and sanitary 
condition, and be maintained in a manner that will 
not disturb the use or enjoyment of neighboring 
lots due to noise, odor or other adverse impact. 
The henhouse shall provide a minimum of three 
square feet per hen;
b. Henhouses and fenced enclosures shall be 
enclosed on all sides, and shall provide adequate 
protection for the hens from weather and wild or 
domestic animals;
c. The henhouse shall be located upon a 
permeable surface that prevents waste runoff and 
the materials used in making the henhouse shall 
be uniform for each element of the structure. The 
use of scrap material shall be prohibited;
d. All chicken feed shall be securely stored and 
protected from the elements and vermin; and
e. All stored manure shall be composted in a fully 
enclosed structure or container and no more than 
three cubic feet of composting manure shall be 
stored on the involved lot. All other manure not 
used for composting or fertilizing shall be removed 
from the property.
5. Henhouses as Accessory Structures. Any 
henhouse associated with the use of the domestic 
keeping of chickens shall conform to the standards 
as described in Section 5.6.5.G. Henhouses.

(2) Uses involving the parking or storage of
tractor trailers, or the parking or storage of trucks
with a gross vehicle weight (GVW) greater than
10,000 lbs.;
(3) Auto or small engine repair or maintenance,
welding, or other uses which involve the visible
storage on the property of automobiles or the
parts thereof;
(4) Any use as defined under Sexually Oriented
Business in Section 4.3 ;
(5) Any uses as listed under the use category
of Industrial Uses and Transportation Uses in
Section 4.3 .
k. No more than one motor vehicle shall be used in
connection with a Home Occupation.
(1) The vehicle shall be of a type ordinarily
used for conventional private passenger
transportation, such as a passenger automobile,
van, or pickup truck;
(2) The vehicle shall not be designed to carry
more than 12 persons; and
(3) Parking of the vehicle shall be accommodated
on site.
G. Incidental Vehicle Repair
The purpose of this Section is to preserve the
character of residential areas and address nuisances
that can accompany frequent and recurring vehicle
repair while allowing for the maintenance or
improvement of personal vehicles that is consistent
with a residential use. The purpose is further to
prohibit the business of vehicle repair in residential
districts. The incidental repair of vehicles shall
be permitted as an accessory use to a residential
principal use, if it complies with the requirements of
this Section.
1. For all incidental vehicle repair, the following
restrictions apply:
a. The vehicle being repaired shall be registered
to a person living at the property;
b. The purchase, repair, and sale of more than two
vehicles per year is prohibited; and
c. Activities that cause loud, continuous noise,
such as grinding of metal, are prohibited. Activities
resulting in noxious fumes or particulates are
prohibited.
2. For incidental vehicle repair that occurs outside
of a fully enclosed structure, the following additional
restrictions apply:
ACCESSORY USE DEFINITIONS AND USE-SPECIFIC CONDITIONS
a. The vehicle being repaired shall not be in a
state of disassembly, or on jack stands, for a period
longer than five days;
b. Repair is limited to a frequency of no more than
five consecutive days and no more than 21 days in
a calendar year; and
c. R epair is limited to the hours of 8:00 am to 8:00
pm.
H. Outdoor Storage
Storage within an outdoor area of a property that is
subordinate and incidental to the principal residence.
1. Storage of Junk Prohibited. Accessory outdoor
storage shall not include junk or items that are not
consistent with a residential use, and shall not occupy
any parking spaces required for the principal use.
2. Location. Accessory outdoor storage shall not be

ACCESSORY USE DEFINITIONS AND USE-SPECIFIC CONDITIONS
4.6.2 Accessory to Non-Residential
Uses
A category of uses for non-residential accommodations.
A. Aircraft Take-offs and Landings
Sites that are used, designed, or intended to be used
for the purpose of taking off or landing of aircra fts.
B. Automated Teller Machine
(ATM)
A computerized, self-service machine used by
bank customers for financial transactions, including
deposits, withdrawals, and fund transfers, without
contact with financial institution personnel. The
machines may be located at or within a financial
institution, or at other locations.
C. Beer, Wine, and Liquor Sales
The sale of alcoholic beverages, not to be consumed
on the premises, with such sales to be made only
in sealed bottles or other containers. This use shall
be accessory to primary uses such as convenience
stores, specialty food stores, and grocery stores, as
listed within the subcategories of either Neighborhood
or General Retail and Service.
D. Drive-Through
As defined in Article 2, a drive-through is a structure,
or portion of a structure, that is designed to provide
products or services directly to customers in a motor
vehicle. It may be an accessory use to a Bank, as
allowed pursuant to Section 4.4.5 Office Uses, or to
a Restaurant or Pharmacy, as allowed pursuant to
Section 4.4.6 Retail and Service Uses . The following
requirements shall apply:
1. Auto-Oriented Structures. Any lot with a drive-
through shall be subject to additional regulation
pursuant to Section 5.5, Auto-Oriented Structures.
2. Landscaping. Landscaping shall be provided
along the perimeter of the lot in compliance with the
Type 2 landscaped buffer yard, pursuant to Section
8.1.2 Landscaped Buffer Yards .
3. Proximity to Residential Districts. The drive-
through facility shall not be located directly abutting
any lot in a residential district or any lot containing
a dwelling. A 50 foot wide limited activity buffer is
required, measured from the drive-through structure
or canopy to the closest adjacent lot line of a lot used
for residential purposes.
ARTICLE 4: USES
4. Proximity to Schools. The drive-through facility
shall not be located within 1,000 feet of a school.
5. Additional Requirements. The Planning Board
may require an applicant to modify a site plan to
provide for sufficient pedestrian amenities, reduce
the negative visual impact, and/or provide better
circulation and parking so as to reduce the potential
for accidents and the impact the proposed use may
have on neighboring development.
E. Employee Amenities
Amenities primarily serving employees of a use 4
that is principal on the property in question. These E
amenities may include cafeterias, recreational L
facilities, and childcare facilities. All standards C
I
from Section 4.4, Principal Uses , shall apply to the T
accessory employee amenities use. R
A
F. Farm Stand
A roadside stand offering agricultural or horticultural,
products for sale. A farm stand shall be accessory to
an agricultural use and not be considered a second
principal retail use, provided that at it remains
subsidiary to the Agricultural Use.
1. Farm Stand as an Accessory Structure. A farm
stand shall conform to the standards as described in
Section 5.6, Accessory Structures .
2. Maximum Footprint. In no instance shall the
footprint of the first floor of an accessory farm stand
exceed 1,000 square feet.
G. Indoor Storage/Warehousing
Accessory storage and warehousing for
manufacturing and service and retail uses, which
is entirely confined within a structure. The structure
may be accessory to the principal structure on the
lot, or can be internal to the principal structure on the
lot. Please see Section 5.6, Accessory Structures ,
for more information.
H. Outdoor Display
The outdoor display of merchandise or other items
offered for sale or advertisement. The following
regulations apply:
1. Outdoor displays shall extend at least five feet
from the building façade;
2. Merchandise or other items displayed as the
accessory use shall be restricted to those items or
merchandise which are sold at the principal use;

Section 4.7
TEMPORARY USES
4.7.1 General Standards
The purpose of this section is to expressly exempt
from some restrictions of this Ordinance certain
uses or structures that occur temporarily on
privately owned property. Additional municipal
regulations may apply and be administered by such
departments as Public Works, Health, or the Office
of the City Clerk.
4.7.2 Voting Places
The provisions of this Ordinance shall be so
construed as not to interfere with the temporary use
of any premises as a voting place for a municipal,
state, or federal election or primary.
4.7.3 Construction
Accessory structures and storage required for
construction, such as office trailers, storage
containers, dumpsters, and stored equipment or
materials, may be placed on a lot for the duration
of active, substantial, and continuous construction.
Such structures and storage shall not be placed in a
manner that poses a threat to public safety. For an
existing House, Duplex, and Triple-Decker, no such
structure or storage may remain on the lot for longer
than 120 days.
4.7.4 Seasonal Sales
The sale of seasonal, agricultural goods produced on
the lot, such as fruits and vegetables, maple syrup,
and flowers, may occur in any district, pursuant to
the following requirements:
A. Use-Specific Conditions
1. Duration shall be limited to one occurrence per
year of no more than 30 consecutive days;
2. Any signage shall comply with Section 9.2.9
Temporary Signs ;
3. Any accessory structure, such as a stand, and
goods shall be set back at least 10 feet from all
property lines; and
4. Goods for sale shall not occupy required parking
spaces or interfere with the safe flow of traffic. and
efficient flow of vehicular and pedestrian traffic.

The sale of personal property, such as garage
sales, yard sales, and estate sales, may occur in
any district, pursuant to the following requirements:

1. Duration shall be limited to two occurrences per
year of no more than three consecutive days;
2. Any signage shall comply with Section 9.2.9
Temporary Signs ;
3. Goods shall be set back at least 10 feet from all

ARTICLE 5: BUILDING AND LOT STANDARDS
62 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE
Introductory Provisions
Section 5.1
INTRODUCTORY 
PROVISIONS
5.1.1 Purpose
The purpose of this Article is to regulate the physical 
development of land and structures to maintain and 
improve the character and appearance of the City of 
Manchester.
5.1.2 Applicability
The building types detailed in Section 5.3, Building 
Types, define the required building forms for new 
construction, additions to existing structures, and 
redevelopment within all zoning districts, except as 
explained below.
A. Zoning Districts
Each building type shall be constructed only within 
districts where the building type is permitted. Refer 
to Table 5.3-A. Principal Building Types Permitted By 
District.
B. Uses
Each building type can hold a variety of uses 
depending on the district in which it is located. Refer 
to Article 4: Uses, for uses permitted per district. 
Some building types have additional limitations on 
permitted uses.
C. Exemptions from Building 
Types
The following buildings are exempt from building 
type standards and shall instead meet the other lot 
requirements by district, pursuant to Tables 6.2-
B, 6.2-C, and 6.2-D in Section 6.2, Base District 
Regulations: 
1. Buildings on lots in the Industrial (IND) and 
Conservation (CV) districts.
2. Buildings on lots where the only principal uses 
are in the Agricultural or Infrastructure use categories 
pursuant to Table 4.3-A, Principal Uses.
5.1.3 Building Design
All pincipal buildings shall be designed to be 
permanently erected on a permanent foundation 
and connected to all required utilities.
Primary façades containing the main entrance shall 
be oriented to a front lot line. 
Buildings shall provide windows and doors on 
façades facing primary and secondary streets 
that meet the transparency requirements of the 
applicable building type. 
5.1.4 Categorization of Building
Types
A. Residential Buildings
The primary function of these building types is 
to provide dwellings and homes in the City. This 
category includes the following types of buildings: 
House, Duplex, Triple-Decker, Apartment House, 
Townhouses, Small Multifamily, and Large 
Multifamily. 
B. Mixed-Use Buildings
Mixed-Use buildings provide the option for a flexible 
mix of uses contained in a single building. These 
buildings make up the primary component of a 
neighborhood center, main street, and downtown. 
This category includes the following types of 
buildings: Cottage Commercial, Live-Work, General 
Mixed-Use, Mid-Rise, and High-Rise.
C. Non-Residential Buildings
The primary function of these building types is to 
provide varied and flexible commercial space in 
business corridors and industrial districts. These 
buildings are designed for both pedestrian and 
vehicular access. This category includes the 
following types of buildings: Workshop/Warehouse 
Flex, Commercial, Shopping Center, and Civic.

1. General Description
A small- to medium-sized building designed as a single-
family detached dwelling, other than a manufactured
housing unit, set back from the front and street lot lines
to allow for landscaped yards that vary in size based
on the district in which they reside. Accessory buildings
may share the side and rear yards as permitted. This
building type typically incorporates a single residential
unit but may include one accessory dwelling unit or a
home business.
[IMAGE]
2. Entrance Types & Street Façade Elements
The following entrance types and street façade ele-
ments are permitted for the House building type, sub-
ject to the requirements of Section 5.4.2 Entrance
Types and Street Façade Elements :
A. Entrance Types - One Required
• Porch
• Recessed Porch
• Step
• Recessed Entry
B. Street Façade Elements
• Not applicable for residential building types
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 65

1. General Description
A small- to medium-sized building with two principal
dwelling units situated on small- to medium-sized lots
that are set back from the front and street lot lines to
allow for landscaped yards. The units have separate
entrances, at least one of which faces a street. Both
dwelling units, whether side-by-side, front-to-back, or
over-and-under, are contained within a single building.
This building type can be converted from a single-
family house in permitted districts.

A. Maximum lot width at the principal frontage in BC-1 and MX Districts:

BC-1 District - 200 feet.
B. Front-loaded lots are characterized by having a curb cut along a street that provides a driveway leading to conforming
parking spaces. Alley-loaded lots are characterized by having a curb cut along an alley that provides direct access to
rear yard parking.
C. Both vacant and developed lots (which contain otherwise conforming uses and structures) created prior to May 19,
1987, of at least 5,000 square feet in area and a lot width of at least 50 feet shall be considered conforming and shall
not be subject to consolidation provisions of this Ordinance.
D. The maximum impervious area in any front yard is 25%.
E. A Duplex building type is permitted to be on a lot with a maximum of two principal structures, pursuant to Section 8.7,
Planned Developments.

a Triple-Decker has been either a 3-story wood clad
building with one floor located under a gambrel roof,
or a 3-story, flat brick building with a parapet roof and
heavy cornice.

CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 71
Building Types
ARTICLE 5
1. General Description
A Triple-Decker is a narrow, smaller-scale three-unit 
building with all residential units, each having access 
from the primary/secondary street. The units are 
vertically stacked on top of each other with one unit per 
floor. Buildings are situated on small- to medium-sized 
lots with small landscaped front yards. Historically, 
a Triple-Decker has been either a 3-story wood clad 
building with one floor located under a gambrel roof, 
or a 3-story, flat brick building with a parapet roof and 
heavy cornice.
Districts Permitted
R-M MX-1 MX-2 BC-1
2. Entrance Types & Street Façade Elements
The following entrance types and street façade el-ements are permitted for the Triple-Decker building 
type, subject to the requirements of Section 5.4.2 En-trance Types and Street Façade Elements:
A. Entrance Types - One Required
• Porch
• Recessed Porch
• Step
• Recessed Entry
• Stoop
B. Street Façade Elements
• Not applicable for residential building types
5.3.1 Building Type Standards
C. TRIPLE-DECKER

D. APARTMENT HOUSE
Districts Permitted
R-M MX-1 MX-2 BC-1

1. General Description
A small- to medium-sized building containing three
or four dwelling units, situated on small- to medium-
sized lots with small landscaped yards. The units may
be accessed through an internal corridor. At least one
entrance shall face a street. Dwelling units, whether
side-by-side, front-to-back, or over-and-under, are
contained within a single building. This building type
shall be designed at a scale consistent with that of
surrounding single- and two-family dwellings.
2. Entrance Types & Street Façade Elements
The following entrance types and street façade ele-
[IMAGE]
ments are permitted for the Apartment House building
type, subject to the requirements of Section 5.4.2 En-
trance Types and Street Façade Elements :

• Porch
• Recessed Porch
• Step
• Recessed Entry
B. Street Façade Elements
• Not applicable for residential building types

records.text:
ARTICLE 5: BUILDING AND LOT STANDARDS
BUILDING TYPES
E. TOWNHOUSE
7 . Specific Standards
A. Townhouses are an attached building type. Each unit shares a minimum of one connecting party wall with another
Townhouse unit. Each independent Townhouse unit within a Townhouse building shall maintain a minimum width of
18 feet and maximum width of 36 feet along its primary façade. All townhouse units shall be situated along or running
parallel to the principal frontage line of the property adjacent to the public right-of-way, or a private way that is internal
to the property. All Townhouse units within the same building shall be oriented in the same direction.
B. If lots are subdivided by Townhouse unit, the minimum lot width of each lot may be decreased to the minimum width
of the Townhouse unit. Otherwise, the minimum lot width required at the principal frontage shall be an aggregate of
the width of all Townhouse units and any minimum side yard setbacks required, or the minimum provided in Section
5.3.1.E.3 , whichever is larger.
C. Maximum lot width at the principal frontage in BC-1 and MX Districts:
Mixed-Use District (MX-1, MX-2) - 150 feet.
BC-1 District - 200 feet.
D. Townhouse buildings may use a courtyard or pocket park along the principal street frontage, pursuant to Section 8.6,
Open Spaces, in order to be exempted from any maximum front yard setback requirement. Although placed further
away, the primary façade of the building shall remain oriented toward the public right-of-way.
E. All buildings within the Millyard District shall utilize brick as the primary building façade material to match the historic
character of the district. All Millyard District standards are regulated in Section 6.2.4 Millyard District (MILL) .
F. Unless done through a planned development, individual townhouse units shall not provide front yard parking and the
entrance to an attached or drive-under garage shall be located along the rear of the building with the bay entrance
facing an alley or internal way.
G. A Townhouse building type is permitted to be on a lot with multiple principal structures, pursuant to Section 8.7, Planned

ARTICLE 5: BUILDING AND LOT STANDARDS
80 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE
Building Types
E. TOWNHOUSE
7. Specific Standards
A. Townhouses are an attached building type. Each unit shares a minimum of one connecting party wall with another 
Townhouse unit. Each independent Townhouse unit within a Townhouse building shall maintain a minimum width of 
18 feet and maximum width of 36 feet along its primary façade. All townhouse units shall be situated along or running 
parallel to the principal frontage line of the property adjacent to the public right-of-way, or a private way that is internal 
to the property. All Townhouse units within the same building shall be oriented in the same direction.
B. If lots are subdivided by Townhouse unit, the minimum lot width of each lot may be decreased to the minimum width 
of the Townhouse unit. Otherwise, the minimum lot width required at the principal frontage shall be an aggregate of 
the width of all Townhouse units and any minimum side yard setbacks required, or the minimum provided in Section 
5.3.1.E.3, whichever is larger.
C. Maximum lot width at the principal frontage in BC-1 and MX Districts: 
Mixed-Use District (MX-1, MX-2) - 150 feet.
BC-1 District - 200 feet.
D. Townhouse buildings may use a courtyard or pocket park along the principal street frontage, pursuant to Section 8.6, 
Open Spaces, in order to be exempted from any maximum front yard setback requirement. Although placed further 
away, the primary façade of the building shall remain oriented toward the public right-of-way.
E. All buildings within the Millyard District shall utilize brick as the primary building façade material to match the historic 
character of the district. All Millyard District standards are regulated in Section 6.2.4 Millyard District (MILL).
F. Unless done through a planned development, individual townhouse units shall not provide front yard parking and the 
entrance to an attached or drive-under garage shall be located along the rear of the building with the bay entrance 
facing an alley or internal way.
G. A Townhouse building type is permitted to be on a lot with multiple principal structures, pursuant to Section 8.7, Planned 
Developments.

7 . Specific Standards
A. Maximum lot width at the principal frontage in BC-1 District:
BC-1 District - 200 feet.
B. Large Multifamily buildings may use a courtyard or pocket park along the principal street frontage, pursuant to Section
8.6, Open Spaces, in order to be exempted from any maximum front yard setback requirement. Although placed further
away, the primary façade of the building shall remain oriented toward the public right-of-way.
C. All buildings within the Millyard District shall utilize brick as the primary building façade material to match the historic
character of the district. All Millyard District standards are regulated in Section 6.2.4 Millyard District (MILL) .
D. Utility equipment shall be located on either a roof, screened by a parapet wall, or at the rear of a building where it shall
be screened or obscured from all public streets and communal open spaces, pursuant to Section 8.3, Screening of
Dumpsters and Utilities.
E. Walkways shall connect the sidewalk or driveway to building entrances.
F. The entrance to a drive-under garage shall be located along the rear of the building.

H. COTTAGE COMMERCIAL
[IMAGE]
Districts Permitted Districts Permitted by CU
MX-2 BC-1 BC-2 MX-1
[IMAGE]
1. General Description
A small- to medium-sized building, with the physical
characteristics of a residential cottage, such as a
pitched roof or porch. This building has a pedestrian-
friendly façade with moderate transparency, and a
primary entrance that faces the street. The first story
elevation may be at sidewalk grade or raised and the
building may have a small landscaped area in the front
yard. This building type includes houses that have been
converted to allow flexible space for commercial use,
and provides walkable commercial and professional
amenities to mixed-use neighborhoods.
2. Entrance Types & Street Façade Elements
[IMAGE]
The following entrance types and street façade ele-
ments are permitted for the Cottage Commercial build-
ing type, subject to the requirements of Section 5.4.2
Entrance Types and Street Façade Elements :
A. Entrance Types - One Required
• Porch
• Recessed Porch
• Step
• Recessed Entry
• Stoop
• Gallery
• Commercial
B. Street Façade Elements - Optional
• Shopfront
• Office Front

35 ft.
D.
First Story

6. Street Façade Requirements
ALL PERMITTED DISTRICTS
A.
Minimum Transparency per each Story
40% First Story 15% per each upper story
B.
Blank Wall Limitations
Maximum of 15 ft. on primary and secondary façades.
C.
Principal Entrance Location
Main entrance shall be on the primary façade and face a street, unless otherwise permitted in a planned development.
D.
Required Number of Street Entrances
1 per each 50 ft. of front façade.
E.
Permitted Roof Types
Pitched.
7 . Specific Standards
A. Maximum lot width at the principal frontage in BC-1 and MX Districts:
Mixed-Use District (MX-1, MX-2) - 150 feet.
BC-1 District - 200 feet.
B. The principal entrance shall effectively address the adjacent public realm and be given prominence on the building
façade . This may be satisfied through the use of architectural features such as entranceway roofs or recesses; sidelight
windows, transom window, or other adjacent windows; additional moldings with expression lines; or a bay of unique
width.
C. A walkway shall connect the sidewalk or driveway to the principal entrance.
D. Surface parking is not permitted between buildings and the street. Travel lanes for automobiles shall not be located in
the frontage except where access driveways into the site are needed.
E. A Cottage Commercial building type is permitted to be on a lot with multiple principal structures, pursuant to Section 8.7,
Planned Developments.
90 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE
