1. General Description
A set of multiple Live-Work units, connected by party
walls, within a building located on the same lot or
adjacent lots. Each Live-Work unit has a separate
entrance to the street. If on separated lots, each unit
occupies the full frontage of its lot and shares at least
one party wall with another unit of the same type. Each
unit includes a flexible space for commercial use on the
first floor with internally connected residential dwelling
units above the flexible space. This building type
can serve as a filler building in denser neighborhood
centers.
2. Entrance Types & Street Façade Elements
The following entrance types and street façade ele-
ments are permitted for the Live-Work building type,
subject to the requirements of Section 5.4.2 Entrance
Types and Street Façade Elements :
A. Entrance Types - One Required
• Porch
• Recessed Entry
• Stoop
• Stoop with Lightwell
• Terrace
• Commercial
B. Street Façade Elements - One Required
• Shopfront
• Office Front
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 91

ARTICLE 5: BUILDING AND LOT STANDARDS
BUILDING TYPES
I. LIVE-WORK
7 . Specific Standards
A. Live-Work buildings are an attached building type. A single Live-Work unit is not allowed to be constructed if it does not
share a minimum of one connecting party wall with another Live-Work unit or an adjacent building. Each independent
Live-Work unit within a Live-Work building shall maintain a minimum width of 18 feet and maximum width of 36 feet. All
Live-Work units shall be situated along or run parallel to the principal frontage line of the property adjacent to the public
street, or a private way that is internal to the property. All Live-Work units within the same building shall be oriented in
the same direction.
B. If lots are subdivided by Live-Work unit, the minimum lot width of each lot may be decreased to the minimum width of the
Live-Work unit. Otherwise, the minimum lot width required at the principal frontage shall be an aggregate of the width
of all Live-Work units and any minimum side yard setbacks required, or the minimum provided in Section 5.3.1.I.3 ,
whichever is larger.
C. Maximum lot width at the principal frontage in BC-1 and MX Districts:
Mixed-Use District (MX-1, MX-2) - 150 feet.
BC-1 District - 200 feet.
D. Any side yard setbacks required in 5.3.1.I.3.D & E only apply to the end units within a row of Live-Work units and not
interior units.
E. Live-Work buildings may use a publicly accessible courtyard or pocket park along the principal street frontage, pursuant
to Section 8.6, Open Spaces, in order to be exempted from any maximum front yard setback requirement. Although
placed further away, the primary façade of the building shall remain oriented toward the public right-of-way.
F. All buildings within the Millyard District shall utilize brick as the primary building façade material to match the historic
character of the district. All Millyard District standards are regulated in Section 6.2.4 Millyard District (MILL) .
G. A walkway shall connect the sidewalk or driveway to the principal entrance.
H. If 18 feet or more in height, the first story shall count as two stories.
I. A live-work building type is permitted to be on a lot with multiple principal structures, pursuant to Section 8.7, Planned
Developments.
94 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE

ARTICLE 5: BUILDING AND LOT STANDARDS
BUILDING TYPES
J. GENERAL MIXED-USE
7 . Specific Standards
A. General Mixed-Use buildings may use a publicly accessible courtyard, plaza, or pocket park along the principal street
frontage line, pursuant to Section 8.6, Open Spaces, in order to be exempted from any maximum front yard setback re -
quirement. Although placed further away, the primary façade of the building shall remain oriented towards a public street.
B. The first 30 feet in depth of the first story of the General Mixed-Use building, as measured from the wall of the primary
street façade, shall be occupied by any uses as permitted under the Civic, Office, or Retail and Services use categories
in Table 4.3-A , Principal Uses or the ancillary uses of a lobby, recreational area, exhibit hall, or meeting room that are
customary to accompanying a residential or lodging use. Any building face oriented towards a surface parking area shall
also reserve the first 30 feet in depth of the first story, as measured from the wall of the building facing the surface parking
area, for any non-residential use as permitted in Table 4.3-A , Principal Uses. Residential dwelling or rooming units or the
lodging units of hotels are otherwise permitted on the first story.
C. Maximum lot width at the principal frontage in BC-1 and MX Districts:
Mixed-Use District (MX-1, MX-2) - 150 feet.
BC-1 District - 200 feet.
D. All buildings within the Millyard District shall utilize brick as the primary building façade material to match the historic
character of the district. All Millyard District standards are regulated in Section 6.2.4 Millyard District (MILL) .
E. Utility equipment shall be located on either a roof, screened by a parapet wall, or at the rear of a building where it shall
be screened or obscured from all public streets and communal open spaces, pursuant to Section 8.3, Screening of
Dumpsters and Utilities.
F. A walkway shall connect the sidewalk or driveway to the principal entrance.
G. Surface parking shall not be permitted between buildings and the street. Travel lanes for automobiles shall not be located
in the frontage except where access driveways into the site are needed.
H. The entrance to a drive-under or internal parking garage shall not be located along the principal frontage.
I. If 18 feet or more in height, the first story shall count as two stories.
J. A General Mixed-Use building type is permitted to be on a lot with multiple principal structures, pursuant to Section 8.7,
Planned Developments.

records.text:
ARTICLE 5: BUILDING AND LOT STANDARDS
BUILDING TYPES
K. MID-RISE
7 . Specific Standards
A. Mid-rise buildings may use a publicly accessible courtyard, plaza, or pocket park along the principal street frontage line,
pursuant to Section 8.6, Open Spaces, in order to be exempted from any maximum front yard setback requirement. Al-
though placed further away, the primary façade of the building shall remain oriented toward the public street.
B. The first 30 feet in depth of the first story of the Mid-rise building, as measured from the wall of the primary street façade,
shall be occupied by any uses as permitted under the Civic, Office, or Retail and Services use categories in Table 4.3-A ,
Principal Uses, or the ancillary uses of a lobby, recreational area, exhibit hall, or meeting room that are customary to
accompanying a residential or lodging use. Any building face oriented towards a surface parking area shall also reserve
the first 30 feet in depth of the first story, as measured from the wall of the building facing the surface parking area, for
any non-residential use as permitted in Table 4.3-A, Principal Uses. Residential dwelling or rooming units or the lodging
units of hotels are otherwise permitted on the first story.
C. All buildings within the Millyard District shall utilize brick as the primary building façade material to match the historic
character of the district. All Millyard District standards are regulated in Section 6.2.4 Millyard District (MILL).
D. Vinyl siding shall not be used on mid-rise buildings in any Zoning District.
E. Utility equipment shall be located on either a roof, screened by a parapet wall, or at the rear of a building where it shall
be screened or obscured from all public streets and communal open spaces, pursuant to Section 8.3, Screening of
Dumpsters and Utilities.
F. Surface parking shall not be permitted between buildings and the street. Travel lanes for automobiles shall not be located
in the frontage except where access driveways into the site are needed.
G. The entrance to a parking garage shall not be located along the principal frontage.
H. A walkway shall connect the sidewalk or driveway to the principal entrance.
I. If 18 feet or more in height, the first story shall count as two stories.
J. A Mid-rise building type is permitted to be on a lot with multiple principal structures, pursuant to Section 8.7, Planned
Developments.
102 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE

ARTICLE 5: BUILDING AND LOT STANDARDS
BUILDING TYPES
L. HIGH-RISE
7 . Specific Standards
A. High-rise buildings may use a publicly accessible plaza along the principal street frontage, pursuant to Section 8.6, Open
Spaces, in order to be exempted from any maximum front yard setback requirement. Although placed further away, the
primary façade of the building shall remain oriented toward the public street.
B. The first 30 feet in depth of the first story of the High-rise building, as measured from the wall of the primary street façade,
shall be occupied by any uses as permitted under the Civic, Office, or Retail and Services use categories in Table 4.3-A ,
Principal Uses, or the ancillary uses of a lobby, recreational area, exhibit hall, or meeting room that are customary to
accompanying a residential or lodging use. Any remaining area of the first story may be occupied by uses listed above
or any other use as permitted in Table 4.3-A, Principal Uses , excluding dwelling, rooming, or lodging units.
C. Vinyl siding shall not be used on High-rise buildings.
D. Utility equipment shall be located on either a roof, screened by a parapet wall, or at the rear of a building where it shall
be screened or obscured from all public streets and communal open spaces, pursuant to Section 8.3, Screening of
Dumpsters and Utilities.
E. The entrance to a parking garage shall not be located along the principal frontage.
F. A walkway shall connect the sidewalk or driveway to the principal entrance.
G. If 18 feet or more in height, the first story shall count as two stories.
H. Any portion of a High-rise building above 8 stories, or 100 feet, shall taper its overall massing in no more than eight-story
increments. Each increment shall not exceed 80 percent of the floor area below it.
I. A horizontal expression line is required in between the first and second floor as well as the sixth and seventh floor of the
High-rise building.
J. A High-rise building type is permitted to be on a lot with multiple principal structures, pursuant to Section 8.7, Planned
Developments.
106 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE

BUILDING TYPES
N. COMMERCIAL
7 . Specific Standards
A. Maximum lot width at the principal frontage in BC-1 and MX Districts:
Mixed-Use District (MX-1, MX-2) - 150 feet.
BC-1 District - 200 feet.
B. In the following districts, the maximum building area of a Commercial building type on a lot shall not exceed the following
square footage:
1. MX-2 - 3,000 SF
2. DT-1 - 25,000 SF
3. BC-1 - 10,000 SF
4. BC-2 - 50,000 SF
C. Commercial buildings may use a publicly accessible courtyard, plaza, or pocket park along the principal street frontage,
pursuant to Section 8.6, Open Spaces, in order to be exempted from any maximum front yard setback requirement.
Although placed further away, the primary façade of the building shall remain oriented toward the public right-of-way.
5
D. All buildings within the Millyard District shall utilize brick as the primary building façade material to match the historic
E
character of the district. All Millyard District standards are regulated in Section 6.2.4 Millyard District (MILL) .
L
E. If 18 feet or more in height, the first story shall count as two stories. C
I
F. Utility equipment shall be located on either a roof, screened by a parapet wall, or at the rear of a building where it shall T
R
be screened or obscured from all public streets and communal open spaces, pursuant to Section 8.3, Screening of
A
Dumpsters and Utilities.
G. A walkway shall connect the sidewalk, driveway, or parking lot to the main entrance.
H. Surface parking shall not be permitted between buildings and the street. Travel lanes for automobiles shall not be located
in the frontage except where access driveways into the site are needed.
I. The entrance to a drive-under or internal parking garage shall not be located along the principal frontage.
J. The side of the building that provides access to the main parking area shall have a minimum transparency of 30%.
K. A Commercial building type is permitted to be on a lot with multiple principal structures, pursuant to Section 8.7, Planned
Developments.

BC-2

Blank Wall Limitations
Maximum of 30 ft. on the pri - mary faç ade and a maximum of 50 ft. on the secondary fa çade.

Principal Entrance Location
Main entrance shall be on the primary façade and face a street, unless otherwise permit- ted in a planned development.

7 . Specific Standards
A. Shopping Centers may use a publicly accessible plaza along the principal street frontage, pursuant to Section 8.6, Open
Spaces, in order to be exempted from any maximum front yard setback requirement. Although placed further away, the
primary façade of the building shall remain oriented toward the public right-of-way.
B. If 18 feet or more in height, the first story shall count as two stories.
C. Utility equipment shall be located on either a roof, screened by a parapet wall, or at the rear of a building where it shall
be screened or obscured from all public streets and communal open spaces, pursuant to Section 8.3, Screening of
Dumpsters and Utilities.
D. A walkway shall connect the sidewalk, driveway, or parking lot to the main entrance.
E. The side of the building that provides access to the main parking area shall have a minimum transparency of 30%.
F. The entrance to a drive-under or internal parking garage shall not be located along the principal frontage.
G. A Shopping Center building type is permitted to be on a lot with multiple principal structures, pursuant to Section
8.7,Planned Developments.

1. General Description
A medium- to large-sized building, which is operated
by a governmental or institutional entity dedicated to
civic activities, and is designed to stand apart from its
surroundings due to the specialized nature of its civic
purpose. Examples include City Hall, libraries, places
of assembly or worship, courthouses, schools, centers
of government, performing arts venues, and museums.
Civic buildings are often the most prominently sited
and architecturally significant buildings in a community.

ARTICLE 5: BUILDING AND LOT STANDARDS
BUILDING TYPES
P. CIVIC
7 . Specific Standards
A. Maximum lot width at the principal frontage in BC-1 and MX Districts:
Mixed-Use District (MX-1, MX-2) - 150 feet.
BC-1 District - 200 feet.
B. Civic buildings may use a publicly accessible courtyard, plaza, or pocket park along the principal street frontage, pursu-
ant to Section 8.6, Open Spaces , in order to be exempted from any maximum front yard setback requirement. Although
placed further away, the primary façade of the building shall remain oriented toward the public right-of-way.
C. All buildings within the Millyard District shall utilize brick as the primary building façade material to match the historic
character of the district. All Millyard District standards are regulated in Section 6.2.4 Millyard District (MILL) .
D. If 18 feet or more in height, the first story shall count as two stories.
E. Utility equipment shall be located on either a roof, screened by a parapet wall, or at the rear of a building where it shall
be screened or obscured from all public streets and communal open spaces, pursuant to Section 8.3, Screening of
Dumpsters and Utilities.
F. A walkway shall connect the sidewalk or driveway to the main entrance.
G. The entrance to a drive-under or internal parking garage shall not be located along the principal frontage.
H. A Civic building type is permitted to be on a lot with multiple principal structures, pursuant to Section 8.7, Planned De-
velopments.
120 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE

ARTICLE 5: BUILDING AND LOT STANDARDS
EXPLANATION OF BUILDING TYPE STANDARDS
2. PORCH
Dimensions
Width, Clear
8’ min. A
Depth, Clear
6’ min. B
Height With visible basement
48” max C 54" max
Railing/Porch Wall Height
4’ max D
Standards
• A porch shall have a roof. • If unenclosed and open on three sides, a porch, or its ramp or steps, may encroach into a required front or street setback by 2 feet max - imum. • Open porch bases shall be enclosed with latticework or similar material, or visually con- cealed with landscape.
[IMAGE]
A porch is a raised, roofed platform attached to a
building to form an articulated entryway and private
or semi-private social space. Porches shall project
from the building façade and have three open sides,
which may be screened. A visible basement shall be
a maximum of one half the height of the first story.
This frontage element is recommended to accompany
residential uses.
3. RECESSED PORCH
Dimensions
Width, Clear
6’ min. A
Depth, Clear
6’ min. B
Height With visible basement
48” max C 54" max
Railing/Porch Wall Height
4’ max D
Standards
• A porch shall have a roof. • The porch's steps or ramp may encroach into a required front or street setback by 2 feet max - imum. • Open porch bases shall be enclosed with latticework or similar material, or visually con- cealed with landscape.
[IMAGE]
The main façade of the building typically has a
small-to-medium setback from the frontage line. The
recessed porch has two adjacent sides of the porch
that are attached to the building while the other two
sides are open. The open sides may be screened.
A visible basement shall be a maximum of one half
the height of the first story. This frontage element is
recommended to accompany residential uses.
122 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE

6. STOOP
[IMAGE]
Dimensions
Width, Clear
4’ min. A
Depth, Clear
6’ min. B
Height With visible basement
48” max. C 54" max
Railing/Porch Wall Height
4’ max D
Standards
• A stoop shall be at least 18" above the side - walk and shall directly connect to the sidewalk, walkway, or driveway. • A stoop shall have a railing or wall, a covering, or be at least 18" above the adjacent walkway or driveway. • If unenclosed and open on three sides, a stoop may encroach into a required front or street yard setback by 2 feet maximum.
A raised platform that serves as an entryway to
a building. An exterior stair and landing provides
access to the entrance. A visible basement shall
be a maximum one half the height of the first story.
Otherwise, the stoop with lightwell entrance type is
required. This type is recommended for first story
residential or commercial use.

Dimensions
Width, Clear
14’ min. A
Depth, Clear
6’ min. B
Visible Basement Height, Measured from Grade
C 54" min., 8' max.
Standards
• If a lightwell entrance type is used with a build- ing type that requires a street façade element, the requirement shall be applied to a minimum of either the first story or basement floor. If both floors are intended for non-residential, commer - cial uses, both floors shall meet the requirement.
[IMAGE]
An entrance set back from the frontage line by a
sunken lightwell, allowing for activation of a basement.
An exterior stair and landing provides access to
the entrance. This type is recommended for either
residential or commercial uses.

ARTICLE 5: BUILDING AND LOT STANDARDS 
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 127
Explanation of building type Standards
ARTICLE 5
B. Street Façade Elements
The Street Façade Element standards are applicable 
to the development of street façades for buildings with 
non-residential first stories. These elements regulate 
additional standards for façades that will accompany 
any entrance type chosen. 
Street façade elements are required for the following 
building types: Live-Work, General Mixed-Use, Mid￾Rise, High-Rise, Commercial, and Shopping Center.
Street façade elements are optional for the following 
building types: Cottage Commercial, Workshop/
Warehouse Flex, and Civic.
1. SHOP FRONT
A façade conventional for retail and service, or office uses. 
Unless otherwise noted, a minimum of 70% transparency is 
required on the first story.
a. The first story façade is defined from the upper 
stories with a horizontal expression line.
b. The first story window sill height is a minimum of 0.5 
feet and a maximum of 2.5 feet from grade, or from the 
bottom of the first story.
c. On corner lots, the shop front street façade element 
requirements, including the minimum transparency 
required for the primary façade, shall extend a minimum 
of 30 feet along the secondary façade. After the initial 
30 feet from the corner, the transparency required for 
the secondary first story façade as listed in the building 
type standards shall apply to the remaining building 
width.
d. Upper stories may utilize regular residential 
windows, or may continue the shop front façade to 
upper stories. If the façade is continued, the minimum 
sill height requirement no longer applies. 
2. OFFICE FRONT
A façade conventional for civic or office uses, as well as his￾toric millyard buildings. Unless otherwise noted, a minimum 
of 40% transparency is required on the first story.
a. The first story façade is defined from the upper 
stories with a horizontal expression line.
b. Windows shall be symmetrically spaced and sized 
throughout each story of the façade. Windows shall 
have additional ornamentation through the use of 
molding, sills and lintels, and mullions and muntins.
c. In all districts, the sills and lintels shall be of distinct 
ornamental character with the use of materials such as 
brick or brick veneer, stone or stone veneer, decorative 
concrete, wood, or other natural materials as reviewed 
and approved by the Planning and Community 
Development Department.
d. In the Millyard District, required ornamentation shall 
include stone or brick sills and lintels. Lintels may be 
replaced by brick or stone segmental arches.
e. On corner lots, the office front street façade element 
requirements, including transparency requirements, 
shall apply to both the primary and secondary façades.
f. Upper stories shall maintain a consistent design as 
mandated on the first story, although the sizes of the 
windows do not have to match that of the first story.

ARTICLE 5: BUILDING AND LOT STANDARDS
128 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE
Explanation of building type Standards
5.4.3 Building Siting
The following defines the line item requirements 
within subsections 5.3.1.A.3. through 5.3.1.P.3.
Building Siting in each Building Type Table. 
A. Minimum/Maximum Lot Width
See Section 2.3, "Lot Width." Lot width shall be the 
distance between the two side lot lines measured 
along the frontage line. For corner lots, the lot width 
shall be measured along the principal frontage lot line 
where the primary façade is oriented. Certain building 
types may be subject to a maximum lot width.
B. Minimum Lot Depth
See Section 2.3, "Lot Depth." The minimum lot 
depth for all building types is 100’. The minimum lot 
width shall be maintained for a depth of 100’. Corner 
lots need not comply with requirements for lot depth, 
but shall comply with requirements for lot width on all 
front and street lot lines. 
C. Minimum/Maximum Front and 
Street Yard Setback
The minimum allowable distance from the street right￾of-way line to the closest point of the foundation of 
a building or projection thereof, or parking lot. Minor 
projections into required setbacks, including balconies, 
bay windows, open terraces, steps, stoops, window 
sills, eaves, chimneys, and fire escapes are permitted 
such that the projection does not exceed two feet.
D. Minimum Side Yard Setback 
(Total of Both Sides)
The total distance of both side setbacks, as described 
below in 5.4.3.E. The intent of this standard is to allow 
variation in the placement of a building, as long as 
the sum of the two distances still equals the total 
required. Minor projections into required setbacks, 
including balconies, bay windows, open terraces, 
steps, stoops, window sills, eaves, chimneys, and fire 
escapes are permitted such that the projection does 
not exceed two feet.
E. Minimum Setback of One Side
The minimum distance from a single side lot line to 
the nearest point of the allowable principal building 
measured perpendicularly to the side lot line. This 
standard shall only apply to internal lots. Corner lots 
shall always have a minimum setback of one side that 
is greater than or equal to half of the minimum side 
setback as described above in 5.4.3.D.
F. Minimum Rear Yard Setback
The minimum distance from the rear lot line to the 
nearest point of the allowable principal building 
measured perpendicular to the rear lot line. Minor 
projections into required setbacks, including 
balconies, bay windows, open terraces, steps, 
stoops, window sills, eaves, chimneys, and fire 
escapes are permitted such that the projection does 
not exceed two feet.
G. Minimum Buildable Lot Area
The minimum buildable lot area shall be calculated 
pursuant to how it is defined in Section 2.3, 
"Buildable Lot Area."
H. Maximum Lot Coverage
Within all districts, any hard-surfaced, man-made 
area that does not readily absorb or retain water, 
including but not limited to building roofs, parking 
and driveway areas, graveled areas, sidewalks, and 
paved recreation areas, count towards the maximum 
required lot coverage.
I. Surface Parking Locations
A site or a portion of a site, devoted to the off street 
parking of vehicles, including parking spaces, aisles, 
access drives, and landscaped areas, and providing 
vehicular access to a public street.
J. Garage Location
A site, or a portion of a site, devoted to the siting of 
an attached or detached garage or parking structure. 
Garages shall not extend past the front façade of a 
building. 
5.4.4 Uses Within Floors and
Residential Density
Subsections 5.3.1.A.4 through 5.3.1.P.4 establish the 
permitted primary uses within each floor according to 
Table 4.3-A, Principal Uses. The maximum number 
of residential dwelling units permitted within some 
building types is also explained in this subsection, 
as well as the any additional lot area required based 
on the residential density of certain building types.

ARTICLE 5: BUILDING AND LOT STANDARDS 
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 129
Explanation of building type Standards
ARTICLE 5
5.4.5 Height
The following explains how height will be measured 
for each building type as set forth in 5. Height. Refer 
to 5.3.1.A.5 through 5.3.1.P.5, in Building Types. 
A. Minimum Overall Height 
(Stories)
Measured in stories, starting with "Story, First," as 
defined in Section 2.3.
B. Maximum Overall Height 
(Stories)
Measured in stories, starting with "Story, First," as 
defined in Section 2.3.
C. Maximum Overall Height (Feet)
Measured from the grade plane to the highest point 
of the roof. Spires, steeples, chimneys, smoke 
stacks, and antennas may exceed the maximum 
overall height in feet of a building by a maximum of 
10 feet over the peak, or highest point, of the roof in 
all Residential (R) or Mixed-Use (MX) districts and a 
maximum of 50 feet over the peak, or highest point, 
of the roof in all other districts. 
Notwithstanding the height allowances in Article 5, no 
building shall be constructed to a height greater than 
allowed by Section 6.3.2 Airport Approach Overlay
or by Section 154.11 of the Manchester Code of 
Ordinances.
D. First Story
For the purpose of building standards in Section 5.3, 
the height of the first story is the vertical distance in 
feet between the top of the finished first floor surface 
and the top of the finished second floor surface. If 18 
feet or more in height, the first story shall count as 
two stories. 
5.4.6 Street Façade Requirements
The following explains the line item street façade 
requirements for each building type table within 
subsection 6. Street Façade Requirements. Refer 
to 5.3.1.A.6 through 5.3.1.P.6, in Building Types. 
This applies only to building façades facing a public 
or private street. Alley-facing, rear, or side elevations 
are not required to fulfill these standards unless 
otherwise stated.
A. Minimum Transparency
Minimum window glazing of transparent glass in the 
street facing portion(s) of a building. If a building 
has more than one street façade, then transparency 
requirements apply to all street-facing façades. 
1. For any first floor used for a commercial or non￾residential use, the transparency is calculated based 
on the total façade area located between two feet 
and eight feet above the finished first story. This is 
applicable for the first floors of all mixed-use and non￾residential building types. 
2. All other transparency is calculated based on the 
total façade area located between the upper surface 
of any floor to the upper surface of the floor above it 
or, if there is no floor above, from the upper surface 
of the floor to the roof next above.
B. Blank Wall Limitations
The horizontal distance of a façade's surface without 
fenestration, measured per story. 
C. Principal Entrance Location
The principal entrance provides ingress and egress 
to and from a structure. The principal entrance 
location shall face a public street and engage with 
the public domain beyond the private frontage.
D. Required Number of Street 
Entrances
The number of entrances providing ingress and 
egress to and from a building along with the 
architectural treatments that accompany it.

Explanation of building type Standards
E. Permitted Roof Types
A structural covering over any portion of a building 
or structure including projections beyond the walls 
or supports of the building or structure. Roof type 
standards apply to the roofs of all building types as 
defined in this Article.
1. General Provisions. The following provisions apply 
to all roof types:
a. Applicability. All buildings shall fulfill the 
requirements of one of the roof types permitted for 
the building type.
b. Measuring Height. The roof height shall be 
included when measuring the maximum overall 
building height in feet. Refer to 5.3.1.A.5.C to 
5.3.1.P.5.C in the Building Type pages.
c. Other Roof Types. Other roof types not listed 
as a specific type may be made by a request to the 
Director with the following requirements:
(1) The roof type must not create additional 
occupied space beyond that permitted by the 
building type.
(2) The shape of the roof type must be significantly 
different from those defined in this section Roof 
Types, i.e. a dome, spire, vault.
2. Pitched Roof Type. This roof type has a pitch or 
slope. Slope is the ratio of the of the number of inches 
of vertical rise to 12 inches of vertical run, i.e. 4:12 
(rise:run).
a. Allowable Slope. The roof may not be sloped 
less than 4:12 (rise:run) or more than 16:12. 
b. Configurations. Pitched roofs include Shed, Hip, 
Gable, Salt Box, Gambrel, Mansard, and Butterfly 
roofs. A combination of hips and gables with or 
without dormers are permitted as well. (Refer to 
Figure 5.4.6.E.2-A)
Figure 5.4.6.E.2-A
Figure 5.4.6.E.2-B
Parallel Ridge Line with Gable
Figure 5.4.6.E.3-A
c. Parallel Ridge Line. A gabled end or perpendicular 
ridge line shall occur at least every 100 feet of roof 
when the ridge line runs parallel to the front lot line. 
(Refer to Figure 5.4.6.E.2-B) 
d. Occupied Space. Occupied space may be 
incorporated behind this roof type.
3. Flat Roof Type. (Refer to Figure 5.4.6.E.3-A). This 
roof type has a flat roof with overhanging eaves.
a. Configuration. Roofs with no visible slope are 
acceptable. Eaves are required on all street facing 
façades.
b. Eave Depth. Eave depth is measured from the 
building façade to the outside edge of the eave. 
Eaves shall have a depth of at least 12 inches.
c. Eave Thickness. Eave thickness is measured 
at the outside edge of the eave, from the bottom of 
the eave to the top of the eave. Eaves shall be a 
minimum of six inches thick.
d. Occupied Space. Occupied space shall not be 
incorporated behind this roof type.

ARTICLE 5: BUILDING AND LOT STANDARDS 
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 131
Explanation of building type Standards
ARTICLE 5
4. Parapet Roof Type. (Refer to Figure 5.4.6.E.4-A 
Parapet Roof Type) A parapet is a low wall projecting 
above a building’s roof along the perimeter of the 
building. It can be utilized with a flat or low pitched roof 
and also serves to limit the view of roof-top mechanical 
systems from the street.
a. Parapet Height. Height is measured from the top 
of the upper story to the top of the parapet.
(1) Minimum height is two feet with a maximum 
height of six feet.
(2) Roof appurtenances shall be located a 
distance behind the parapet so as not to be visible 
from any street sidewalk.
b. Horizontal Expression Lines. An expression 
line shall define the parapet from the upper stories 
of the building and shall also define the top of the 
parapet.
c. Occupied Space. Occupied space may be 
incorporated behind this roof type. 
F. Façade Variety
Façade articulation is intended to encourage walkable 
environments by creating visually interesting buildings 
with human scale details and proportions. Façade 
articulation is required for certain building types as per 
Section 5.3.1.G.6.F through 5.3.1.P.6.F and shall be 
applicable to all buildings greater than 50 feet in width.
1. Segmentation. A façade shall be organized using 
a consistent rhythm and pattern of windows, building 
articulation, or other architectural features. Façades 
shall be organized into building segments that consist 
of regularly repeated special elements making a 
vertical division in a structure commonly defined by the 
number of windows and door openings per floor or by 
the space between columns or piers.
2. Main Entrance Detailing. A main entrance shall 
effectively address the adjacent public realm and be 
given prominence on the building facade. This may 
be satisfied through the use of architectural features 
such as entranceway roofs or recesses; a chamfered 
corner; sidelight windows, transom window, or other 
adjacent windows; additional moldings with expression 
lines; or a bay of unique width. 
Figure 5.4.6.E.5-A
Figure 5.4.6.E.4-A
5. Towers. (Refer to Figure 5.4.6.E.5-A Tower). When 
utilized, a tower must be used in conjunction with other 
roof types.
a. Quantity. All building types, with the exception 
of the Civic Building, are limited to one tower per 
building.
b. Tower Height. Maximum height, measured from 
the top of the parapet or eave to the top of the tower, 
is equivalent of the height of one upper floor of the 
building to which the tower is applied.
c. Tower Width. Maximum width along all façades 
is one-third the width of the front façade or 30 feet, 
whichever is less.
d. Horizontal Expression Lines. An expression line 
shall define the tower from the upper stories, except 
on House or Townhouse building types.
e. Occupied Space. Towers may be occupied by the 
same uses permitted in upper stories of the building 
type to which they are applied.
f. Application. May be combined with all other roof 
types.
g. Tower Cap. The tower may be capped by the 
parapet, pitched, or flat roof types.

5.5.1 Parking Structures
Parking structures as the principal use on a lot 
require a Conditional Use permit, pursuant to 
Section 10.1 and shall meet the additional following 
requirements, as determined by the Planning Board.
A. Materials
At least 50 percent of each façade of the parking 
structure shall be lined with brick. The remaining 
area of façades shall be covered with architectural 
cladding that utilizes materials and colors consistent 
with nearby building façades.
B. Blank Wall Limitations
No rectangular area greater than 30 percent of any 
story’s façade, as measured from floor to floor, and 
no horizontal segment of a story’s façade greater 
than 30 feet in width may be a solid, blank wall.
C. Pedestrian Entrance
A defined pedestrian entrance and exit is required 
separate from the vehicular entrance and directly 
accessing the sidewalk. 
5.5.2 Car Washes, Vehicle Fueling
Stations, Vehicle Service Stations
and Drive-Through Services
Properties with a principal use of Car Wash, Truck 
Stop, Vehicle Fueling Station, and Vehicle Repair

meeting all Building Type Standards pursuant to 
Section 5.4 of this Article. However, the structures

ARTICLE 5: BUILDING AND LOT STANDARDS 
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 135
Accessory Structures
ARTICLE 5
5.6.4 Accessory Structures on 
Lots Without a Principal Structure
Where a lot has an established principal use, such 
as a parking lot, but does not have a principal 
structure, one accessory structure shall be permit￾ted for every 10,000 square feet of lot area. All 
accessory structures shall be set back a minimum 
of 15 feet from all lot lines. Any such structure shall 
be limited to 300 square feet in gross floor area 
and 15 feet in height. 
5.6.5 Special Requirements for
Certain Accessory Structures
A. Air-Conditioner (AC) 
Condensing Units
Air-conditioning (AC) condensing units, including 
ground-mounted and mounted on a building for 
residential uses, shall conform to the following:
1. Front Yard. AC condensing units shall not be 
located in the front yard or mounted on the primary 
façade of the principal building.
2. Side and Rear Yards. AC condensing units are 
permitted in the side or rear yard, four feet from the 
side or rear property lines.
B. Beehives
Beehives shall only be permitted where there is a 
single-family dwelling in the R-S and R-1A Districts, 
as further regulated in Section 4.6.1 Accessory to 
Residential Uses, or where there is a principal use 
of Agriculture with Livestock, and shall conform with 
the following standards:
1. Allowed Densities. Beehives shall not be 
permitted on a lot smaller than one-half acre in size. 
One beehive shall be permitted for each half acre 
thereafter.
2. Location. Hives shall be located in the rear yard. 
Hives shall be located a minimum of 30 feet from any 
property line.
C. Detached Accessory Dwelling 
Units (ADUs)
All Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) shall be 
regulated as specified in Section 4.6.1 Accessory 
to Residential Uses. ADUs that are detached from 
the principal structure are accessory structures and 
shall conform to the following standards:
1. Yard. ADUs shall be located in side or rear yards 
only.
2. Setback and Lot Coverage. ADUs shall be 
located a minimum of 10 feet from the side or rear 
lot line and five feet from the principal structure and 
shall conform to lot coverage requirements of Section 
5.6.2. Pursuant to RSA 674:72, setback and lot 
coverage requirements shall not apply to ADUs that 
are converted from existing structures constructed 
prior to July 1, 2025.
3. Height. The height of the ADU shall not exceed 
the height of the principal structure.
4. Façade. Front and street façades shall have a 
minimum transparency of 10 percent. If the ADU 
is constructed on a second floor above a detached 
garage, the first story of the façade is exempt from 
this requirement.
5. Roof Type. A pitched roof type is required.
D. Dumpsters
Dumpsters shall not be located in the front or street 
yard and shall conform to screening requirements of 
Section 8.3, Screening of Dumpsters and Utilities.
E. Electric Vehicle Charging 
Stations
Electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) are public 
or private parking spaces that are served by battery 
charging equipment with the purpose of transferring 
electric energy to a battery or other energy storage 
device in an electric vehicle. EVCSs shall conform to 
the following standards:
1. Location. An EVCS shall not be located within a 
parking space, but may be located within a landscape 
buffer.
2. Setback. An EVCS shall not be located closer 
than five feet to any lot line.
3. Walkway Clearance. An EVCS may be located 
on a private walkway but shall not reduce the clear 
width of the walkway or sidewalk to less than 36 
inches.
4. Signage. The total sign area for an EVCS shall 
not exceed two square feet per side.
5. Parking. A parking space with an EVCS shall be 
considered a parking space pursuant to Article 7: 
Parking Regulations.

ground-mounted and mounted on a building for 
residential uses, shall conform to the following:
1. Front Yard. AC condensing units shall not be 
located in the front yard or mounted on the primary 
façade of the principal building.
2. Side and Rear Yards. AC condensing units are 
permitted in the side or rear yard, four feet from the 
side or rear property lines.
B. Beehives
Beehives shall only be permitted where there is a 
single-family dwelling in the R-S and R-1A Districts, 
as further regulated in Section 4.6.1 Accessory to 
Residential Uses, or where there is a principal use 
of Agriculture with Livestock, and shall conform with 
the following standards:
1. Allowed Densities. Beehives shall not be 
permitted on a lot smaller than one-half acre in size. 
One beehive shall be permitted for each half acre 
thereafter.
2. Location. Hives shall be located in the rear yard. 
Hives shall be located a minimum of 30 feet from any 
property line.
C. Detached Accessory Dwelling 
Units (ADUs)
All Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) shall be 
regulated as specified in Section 4.6.1 Accessory 
to Residential Uses. ADUs that are detached from 
the principal structure are accessory structures and 
shall conform to the following standards:
1. Yard. ADUs shall be located in side or rear yards 
only.
2. Setback and Lot Coverage. ADUs shall be 
located a minimum of 10 feet from the side or rear 
lot line and five feet from the principal structure and 
shall conform to lot coverage requirements of Section 
5.6.2. Pursuant to RSA 674:72, setback and lot 
coverage requirements shall not apply to ADUs that 
are converted from existing structures constructed 
prior to July 1, 2025.
3. Height. The height of the ADU shall not exceed 
the height of the principal structure.
4. Façade. Front and street façades shall have a 
minimum transparency of 10 percent. If the ADU 
is constructed on a second floor above a detached 
garage, the first story of the façade is exempt from 
this requirement.
5. Roof Type. A pitched roof type is required.
D. Dumpsters
Dumpsters shall not be located in the front or street 
yard and shall conform to screening requirements of 
Section 8.3, Screening of Dumpsters and Utilities.
E. Electric Vehicle Charging 
Stations
Electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) are public 
or private parking spaces that are served by battery 
charging equipment with the purpose of transferring 
electric energy to a battery or other energy storage 
device in an electric vehicle. EVCSs shall conform to 
the following standards:
1. Location. An EVCS shall not be located within a 
parking space, but may be located within a landscape 
buffer.
2. Setback. An EVCS shall not be located closer 
than five feet to any lot line.
3. Walkway Clearance. An EVCS may be located 
on a private walkway but shall not reduce the clear 
width of the walkway or sidewalk to less than 36 
inches.
4. Signage. The total sign area for an EVCS shall 
not exceed two square feet per side.
5. Parking. A parking space with an EVCS shall be 
considered a parking space pursuant to Article 7: 
Parking Regulations.

ARTICLE 5: BUILDING AND LOT STANDARDS
136 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE
Accessory Structures
F. Flag Pole
A flag pole is a freestanding vertical pole, constructed 
of wood or metal, installed for the sole purpose 
of flying a flag and shall conform to the following 
standards:
1. Yard. Permitted in all yards.
2. Height. A flag pole shall not exceed the following 
height limits:
a. R and MX Districts. In the R and MX Districts, 
a flagpole shall not exceed 20 feet in height.
b. All Other Districts. In all other districts, a 
flagpole shall not exceed 50 feet in height.
3. Setback. The minimum setback shall equal the 
height of the flag pole.
G. Henhouses
Henhouses shall only be permitted where there is 
a single-family dwelling with a half-acre of land in 
the R-S, R-1A, R-1B, and R-2 Districts, as further 
regulated in Section 4.6.1 Accessory to Residential 
Uses, or where there is a principal use of Agriculture 
with Livestock, and shall conform with the following 
standards:
1. Yard. Henhouses shall not be located within the 
front yard.
2. Setback. Henhouses and associated fenced 
enclosures shall not be located within 20 feet of a 
side or rear lot line.
3. Size. Henhouses shall be no larger than 64 square 
feet and shall not exceed six feet in height.
4. Fence. The fence enclosing the area for hens 
shall not exceed six feet in height.
H. Pools and Hot Tubs 
All pools and hot tubs and associated decks, patios, 
and equipment, such as filters and heaters, shall 
conform to the applicable setback requirements for 
accessory structures, regardless of whether they are 
attached to a a principal structure.
I. Propane Tanks 
Propane tanks buried underground may be located 
in any yard, with a minimum setback of 10 feet from 
any property line. Above-ground propane tanks 
greater than 125 gallons shall conform to Sections 
5.6.2 and 5.6.3. Above-ground propane tanks of 125 
gallons or less shall conform to the following:
1. Front and Street Yards. Shall not be permitted in 
the front or street yards.
2. Side and Rear Yards. Permitted in the side or rear 
yard, four feet from the side or rear property lines.
J. Solar - Freestanding
A solar energy system with a supporting framework 
that is placed on, or anchored in, the ground and 
that is independent of any building or other structure, 
other than parking lot canopy solar energy systems, 
shall conform to the following:
1. Lot Size. The minimum lot size for a freestanding 
solar array is 20,000 square feet.
2. Lot Coverage. The size of a freestanding solar 
array shall not exceed five percent of the lot area.
3. Setbacks. The minimum setback of a freestanding 
solar array shall be 25 feet from all property lines.
4. Maximum Height. A freestanding solar array 
shall not exceed 25 feet in height.
5. Glare. Freestanding solar arrays shall be oriented 
to minimize glare directed at abutting buildings and 
roadways.
K. Solar - Parking Lot Canopy
A solar energy system with a supporting framework 
that is placed on, or anchored in, the ground and 
that is independent of any building or other structure, 
which is used in a parking lot or the top story of a 
parking structure to shade vehicles parked in such 
lot or structure, shall conform to the following:
1. Where Permitted. A solar parking lot canopy shall 
not be permitted on a parking area of less than 50 
parking spaces.
2. Setbacks. The minimum setback of a solar 
parking lot canopy shall be 25 feet from all property 
lines.
3. Maximum Height. A solar parking lot canopy shall 
not exceed 25 feet in height.
4. Glare. Solar parking lot canopies shall be oriented 
to minimize glare directed at abutting buildings and 
roadways.

8. Perimeter Buffer Required. A 20-foot, natural 
buffer along the perimeter of the cluster development 
shall be provided. No structures or parking facilities 
may be located within this buffer, and it shall not be 
disturbed from its natural state, except as permitted by 
the Planning Board. The Planning Board may permit 
streets, walking paths, and utilities to cross through the 
buffer.
9. Common Open Space.
a. All land that is not used for building lots, or streets 
and sidewalks shall be preserved as common open 
space. A minimum of 20 percent of the buildable 
lot area of the parent lot shall be included in the 
common open space.
b. A maximum of five percent of the parent lot’s 
buildable lot area that is within the common 
open space may be used for structured common 
amenities, such as game courts, pools, and 
playgrounds, which may include impervious surface. 
No enclosed structure may be constructed within 
the common open space. No part of the common 
open space may be used for parking, drive aisles, or 
similar vehicular uses. 
c. The common space shall be subdivided 
separately from the building lots, with title conveyed 
as proportionate, undivided interests in common, to 
the owners of each lot in the cluster development, 
including the right of each lot owner to access the 
common open space. Responsibility for monitoring 
and maintenance of the common open space shall 
be borne by an association of the building lot owners, 
unless the common open space is encumbered by 
a conservation easement owned by a land trust or 
similar entity that would bear the responsibility for 
permanent preservation and monitoring. 
10. Infrastructure. 
a. Municipal water and sewer services shall 
be provided to all buildings within the cluster 
development.

ARTICLE 6: SPECIAL DISTRICT-WIDE REGULATIONS
142 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE
Base District Regulations
6.2.4 Millyard District (MILL)
A. Special Design Standards
The following are minimum construction standards 
that apply to the Millyard District. When an overlay 
district imposes different standards, the more stringent 
standards shall apply. 
1. Building Materials. At least 75 percent of the 
cumulative surface area of a building’s exterior walls 
shall be faced with brick, excluding fenestration, 
penetrations and other openings. Buildings may use 
a higher percentage of brick on walls that face public 
rights-of-way and lower percentages on walls that are 
less visible by the public, so long as the total surface 
area of the building’s exterior walls amounts to 75 
percent brick. Brick veneer may be used, so long as it 
consists of real brick, with real mortar or grout, and is 
visually indistinguishable from full-brick construction. 
Exterior Insulation and Finishing Systems (EIFS) and 
vinyl siding are not permitted. Foundations, where 
exposed, shall be constructed of natural stone or use 
a natural-stone veneer. Cultured stone is prohibited.
2. Windows. Window sills shall be constructed 
of granite or brick. Window lintels shall either be 
constructed of granite or use brick arches.
3. Lighting. Lighting fixtures affixed to buildings shall 
be constructed of black aluminum (or similar metal) or 
wrought iron. 
B. Other Lot Standards
Any lot with a Civic Building Type, as well as any lot that 
does not require a principal building type pursuant to 
Article 5, shall adhere to the building siting standards 
in Table 6.2-C Other Lot Standards by Mixed-Use, 
Downtown, or Millyard District. 
6.2.5 Innovation District (ID)
A. Special Design and Use Standards
1. Building Materials. At least 75 percent of each 
street façade shall be constructed of a combination of 
a minimum of two of the following building materials: 
high-quality, durable, natural materials such as stone 
and brick; wood lap siding; lapped, shingled, or panel 
fiber cement board siding; glass; and metal. Exterior 
Insulation and Finishing Systems (EIFS) and vinyl 
siding are not permitted. 
2. Mixed Uses. Any lot on which a principal residential 
use is located shall also contain at least one principal 
non-residential use. The non-residential use may be 
located in a Mixed-Use Building or a Non-Residential 
Building.
B. Other Lot Standards
Any lot with a Civic Building Type, as well as any 
lot that does not require a principal building type 
pursuant to Article 5, shall adhere to the building 
siting standards in Table 6.2-D Other Lot Standards 
by Innovation, Business Corridor, Industrial, or 
Conservation District. All other attributes of a principal 
building type, including Street Façade Requirements, 
shall still be applicable as required within Section 5.3.
6.2.6 Business Corridor (BC)
Districts
A. Maximum Lot Widths in BC-1
As regulated within Section 5.3, all lots within the BC-1 
District shall have a maximum lot width of 200 linear 
feet, as measured along the principal frontage line.
B. Other Lot Standards
Any lot with a Civic Building Type, as well as any 
lot that does not require a principal building type 
pursuant to Article 5, shall adhere to the building 
siting standards in Table 6.2-D Other Lot Standards 
by Innovation, Business Corridor, Industrial, or 
Conservation District. All other attributes of a principal 
building type, including Street Façade Requirements, 
shall still be applicable as required within Section 5.3.
6.2.7 Industrial (IND) District
A. Building Lot Standards
Lots within the Industrial District shall not need to 
adhere to the principal building type regulations in 
Article 5. All lots within the district shall adhere to the 
standards within Table 6.2-D Other Lot Standards 
by Innovation, Business Corridor, Industrial, or 
Conservation District.
6.2.8 Conservation (CV) District
A. Building Lot Standards
Lots within the Conservation District shall not need 
to adhere to the principal building type regulations 
in Article 5. All lots within the district shall adhere to 
the standards within Table 6.2-D Other Lot Standards 
by Innovation, Business Corridor, Industrial, or 
Conservation District.

ARTICLE 6: SPECIAL DISTRICT-WIDE REGULATIONS
144 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE
Overlay District Regulations
Section 6.3
OVERLAY DISTRICT 
REGULATIONS
The following overlay standards are applicable, 
respectively, within the following Overlay Districts 
as indicated. Except as otherwise expressly set 
forth below with respect to each Overlay District, 
the standards of the underlying Base Zoning District 
remain applicable within such Overlay District.
6.3.1 Airport Navigational Hazard
Overlay.
A. Performance Standard
Notwithstanding any other provisions of this 
Ordinance, no use may be made of the land within 
100,000 feet of the Manchester-Boston Regional 
Airport air traffic control tower (ATCT) in such manner 
as to create electrical interference with radio aids or 
communications between the airport and the aircraft, 
make it difficult for pilots to distinguish between 
airport lights and others, result in glare in the eyes 
of pilots using the airport or the air traffic controllers, 
impair visibility in the vicinity of the airport by the 
creation and discharge of smoke, steam, dust or 
other obstructions to visibility or otherwise endanger 
the landing, taking-off, or maneuvering of aircraft.
B. Marking of Hazards
Any development approval granted within the City of 
Manchester, may if such action is deemed advisable 
to effectuate the purposes of this Ordinance and 
reasonable in the circumstances, be so conditioned 
as to require the owner of the structure in question to 
install, operate and maintain thereon such markers 
and lights as may be necessary to indicate to pilots 
the presence of an airport hazard.
6.3.2 Airport Approach Overlay
A generalized map of the approximate location of 
these zones is illustrated in the Airport Approach 
Overlay Map located in Appendix B.
A. Height Limitations
No structure or tree shall be erected, altered or 
allowed to grow within the Airport Approach Overlay 
to a height which would exceed the plane of the 
imaginary surface created by such district. The 
height limitations shall in no case be imposed to limit 
the height of a structure or tree to less than 30 feet 
above the ground upon which it is located.
B. Determination of Compliance 
and Conditions
The Director shall make a determination of 
compliance in consultation with the Director of 
Manchester-Boston Regional Airport as required. In 
the case of an application for a use which lies within 
the Airport Approach Overlay District or which is 
believed to lie within such district, the Director shall 
request of the Airport Director: 
1. A determination of the maximum height of the 
imaginary surface plane of the Airport Approach 
District at the proposed location of the use, and
2. Specific recommendation for additional 
navigational safety measures that should be 
required of the use to mitigate any special approach 
hazards created by such use. The Director may 
attach such reasonable conditions as are necessary 
or prudent to protect navigation safety on the lands 
within the Airport Approach District.
C. Permits
No permit shall be granted that would allow the 
establishment or creation of an airport hazard or 
permit a non-conforming use, structure or tree to be 
made or become higher, or become a greater hazard 
to air navigation, than it was on the effective date of 
this Ordinance or than it is when the application for 
a permit is made.
D. Non-conforming Uses
The height limitations required by this section shall 
not be construed to require the removal, lowering, or 
other change or alteration of any structure or tree not 
conforming to the regulations as of the effective date 
hereof, or otherwise interfere with the continuance of 
any non-conforming use. Nothing herein contained 
shall require any change in the construction, 
alteration, or intended use of any structure, the 
construction or alteration of which was begun prior 
to the effective date of this Ordinance, and diligently 
prosecuted and completed within two years thereof.
6.3.3 Airport Noise Overlay
A. Objective and Purpose
The increasing aircraft activity that is occurring at 
the Manchester-Boston Regional Airport has created 
the need for a noise overlay district located within 
the 65 Ldn (Day-Night Sound Level) contour in 
accordance with the most recently adopted Part 150 
Noise Compatibility Plan prepared by Manchester-

CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 145
Overlay District Regulations
ARTICLE 6
Boston Regional Airport. To avoid land use conflicts 
with uses which may be incompatible with noise 
levels generated at Manchester-Boston Regional 
Airport, the regulations of the Noise Overlay District 
provide for the exclusion of certain land uses, and 
for soundproofing to be required in the construction 
of other uses which may be compatible if mitigating 
action is taken to reduce noise interference with the 
use.
B. Noise Compatibility Zones 
Established
Noise compatibility zones for the affected areas in 
the vicinity of Manchester-Boston Regional Airport 
are hereby established based on the Ldn contours 
for aircraft noise as defined by the most recently 
approved Federal Aviation Regulation Part 150 Noise 
Compatibility Program for the Manchester-Boston 
Regional Airport. The following noise compatibility 
zones are hereby established:
1. The N-1 zone generally corresponds to the area 
between the 65 Ldn and the 70 Ldn contours.
2. The N-2 zone generally corresponds to the area 
within the 70 Ldn contour.
C. Noise Overlay Boundaries
A generalized map of the approximate location of 
these zones is illustrated in the Noise Exposure Map 
located in Appendix C. The boundaries of the Noise 
Overlay Zones are shown in the Part 150 Manchester 
Airport Noise Compatibility Program. Because of 
the averaging inherent in making Ldn calculations 
and the assumptions necessary in the forecasting 
procedure, the Ldn contour lines are not capable of 
being precisely defined in the field. Therefore, the 
boundaries between the noise overlay zones, while 
bearing a very close relationship to the Ldn contour 
lines, have been adjusted to facilitate understanding 
and agreement as to the location of the boundaries.
D. Uses Prohibited and Uses 
Subject to Soundproofing
Land Uses prohibited in the noise overlay zones shall 
be as specified in Table 6.3.3-A Land Use Compatibility 
& Soundproofing Standards. Soundproofing shall be 
required for certain land uses in each of the noise 
overlay zones as shown in Table 6.3.3-A Land Use 
Compatibility & Soundproofing Standards. Where 
soundproofing is required, no building permits shall 
be issued until the applicant has demonstrated that 
the building design is capable of achieving the noise 
level reduction required in Table 6.3.3-A Land Use 
Compatibility & Soundproofing Standards. 
E. Determination of Compliance
Compliance with soundproofing standards can be 
met by incorporating specific building design and 
construction standards, or through other design 
standards which achieve noise attenuation at the 
levels specified in Table 6.3.3-A Land Use Compatibility 
& Soundproofing Standards. The applicant may 
use design features other than those prescribed in 
Section 6.3.3.F. Soundproofing Design Standards,
provided that the final design is capable of achieving 
the noise reduction required in Table 6.3.3-A Land 
Use Compatibility & Soundproofing Standards.
F. Soundproofing Design 
Standards
1. Noise Level Reduction (NLR) of 30 Decibels
(dB):
a. Window glass shall be set in an elastomer 
gasket. Double glazing shall be installed, with an 
air space of at least three inches between the 
two panes of glass. Windows of dome skylights 
shall be permitted as long as they have a sound 
transmission class (STC) of at least 30.
b. The top-floor ceiling construction shall consist 
of plaster or gypsum board at least 5/8-inch thick 
supported on resilient clips or channels. A non￾hardening caulking compound shall be provided 
around the entire perimeter of the suspended 
ceiling.
c. The floor of the lowest room or area containing 
the uses to which those insulation requirements 
apply shall be a concrete slab, or shall be similarly 
sealed otherwise against exterior noise.
d. Masonry walls, if used, shall be at least 
equivalent in weight to eight-inch light-weight 
concrete blocks, at least one surface of which shall 
be painted or plastered.
e. The roof deck shall weigh at least twelve pounds 
per square foot. Wood roof sheathing shall be 
continuous and at least 3/4-inch thick.
2. Noise Level Reduction (NLR) of 25 Decibels
(dB):
a. If wood frame construction is used, all exterior 
stud walls shall have interior and exterior surfaces 
of an approved material at least as thick as half￾inch thick gypsum wallboard, and the intervening

1 All residences in the N-1 Zone are marginally noise compatible and shall be soundproofed to achieve a 25 dB reduction from outdoor
noise levels (NLR). All residences in the N-2 Zone are marginally noise compatible and shall be soundproofed to achieve a 30 dB NLR.
Soundproofing will not eliminate outdoor noise problems. However, building location and site planning design, and use of berms and
barriers, can help mitigate outdoor noise exposure particularly from ground level sources. Measures that reduce noise at a side should be
used wherever practical in preference to measures which only protect interior spaces. Manufactured housing is not compatible within any
of the Zones.
2 Measures to achieve NLR of 25 shall be incorporated into the design and construction of portions of these buildings where the public is
received, office areas, noise sensitive areas or where the normal noise level is low.
3 Measures to achieve NLR of 30 shall be incorporated into the design and construction of portions of these buildings where the public is
received, office areas, noise sensitive areas or where the normal noise level is low.
4 Land use (outdoor) is compatible provided special sound amplification system is installed.
This table is based on an interpretation of the Land Use Guidance Chart for the Manchester Airport contained within the FAR Part 150
Update Noise Compatibility Program (Draft) prepared by Greiner, Inc. September 1996. These standards have been interpreted from that
source and applied to the land use classification system of this Ordinance.

ARTICLE 6: SPECIAL DISTRICT-WIDE REGULATIONS
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 149
Overlay District Regulations
ARTICLE 6
6.3.4 Historic Districts Under 
Heritage Commission Purview
A. Authority for Historic Districts
The Amoskeag Millyard Historic (AMH) District and 
the Amoskeag Corporation Housing Historic (ACH) 
District are adopted pursuant to Section 1.1.3 
Authority, of this Ordinance, and in accordance with 
the provisions of RSA 674:46, Authority Granted (for 
Historic Districts). Pursuant to RSA 674:44b, Powers 
(of Heritage Commissions), within the Historic 
Districts the Heritage Commission is authorized to 
assume the powers and duties granted to historic 
district commissions in accordance with RSA 
674:46a, Powers and Duties of the Historic District 
Commission.
B. Establishment of the Historic 
Districts
The Historic Districts are established in accordance 
with, and for the purposes so stated in Section 3.3.3 
Overlay Districts, of this Ordinance, and encompass 
lands as indicated in Section 3.2, Official Zoning 
Maps, of this Ordinance.
C. Permit Requirements in Historic 
Districts
1. Except as provided in Section 6.3.4.C.3 below, 
within the Amoskeag Corporation Housing Historic 
(ACH) District it shall be unlawful to construct, alter, 
move, demolish, change the use, or modify the 
appearance or design of any building, structure, or 
place without applying for and receiving from the 
Director a permit for such activity. Activities which 
require permits include, but are not limited to, changing 
the materials, color, finish, or architectural detail of 
exterior walls; replacement or modification of window 
or door openings; installation or removal of porches 
or fire escapes; roofing or chimney modification or 
replacement; the installation of antennae or other 
appurtenances on the building exterior; regrading; 
paving or repaving; installation or removal of fences, 
retaining walls, signage, or on-site lighting; or similar 
activities for which a building or zoning permit might 
not otherwise be required.
2. Except as provided in Section 6.3.4.C.3 below, 
within the Amoskeag Millyard Historic (AMH) 
District it shall be unlawful to carry out major 
exterior rehabilitation or restoration of existing 
buildings, changes to exterior signage or additions, 
or construction of new free standing structures, or 
to demolish a building or structure or any external 
portion thereof, without applying for and receiving 
from the Director a permit for such activity.
3. A permit is not required for ordinary maintenance 
or repair activities which do not involve changes in 
design, materials, or external appearance. Such 
activities include but are not limited to roof repair, 
incidental painting, repointing, groundskeeping, or 
other similar activities.
D. Review of Permit Applications 
by the Heritage Commission
All permit applications required under Article 10,
shall be submitted by the Director to the Heritage 
Commission for its consideration. A permit may be 
issued only following approval of an application 
by the Heritage Commission and the transmittal 
of a Certificate of Approval to the Director. In the 
event of disapproval of a permit application by the 
Heritage Commission, a notice of disapproval shall 
be forwarded to the Director.
1. Standards for Review of Permits by the
Heritage Commission
a. In reviewing a permit application within the 
Amoskeag Corporation Housing Historic District, 
the Heritage Commission shall take into account 
the purposes of the District, and give consideration 
to the following:
(1) The historical and/or architectural value of 
the building or structure and its setting; 
(2) The general compatibility of the proposed 
exterior modifications including design, scale, 
arrangement, textures, colors, and materials in 
relationship to the existing building or structure 
and its setting, and to the District; 
(3) The general size and scale of proposed 
new construction in relationship to the existing 
surroundings, including such factors as the 
building height and mass, orientation to adjacent 
streets, type of roof, fenestration, materials, 
colors, and architectural details; and 
(4) The design, scale, arrangement, textures, 
colors, and material of site features and 
improvements including yards, parking lots, 
driveways, walkways, signs, and landscaping as 
they affect the setting for a building or structure 
and the character of the District.
b. In reviewing a non-demolition permit application 
in the Amoskeag Millyard Historic District, the

Overlay District Regulations
Heritage Commission shall take into account the 
purposes of the District, and find that the proposed 
action:
(1) Shall not cause unnecessary destruction 
or blight of important natural or man-made 
features of the landscape, nor the unnecessary 
obstruction of views of the Merrimack River. 
(2) Shall be reasonably harmonious with the 
terrain, open space, and the design, materials, 
and scale of existing buildings; 
(3) Shall provide for safe and convenient 
pedestrian circulation and appropriate supportive 
amenities; and 
(4) Shall incorporate signs of a scale, design, 
and type that are consistent with the architectural 
and design guidelines of studies and reports 
commissioned by the City.
c. In reviewing a demolition permit application 
within the Amoskeag Historic District, the Heritage 
Commission shall take into account the purposes 
of the District. The Commission shall consider 
selective demolition of portions of the buildings 
if such demolition does not disrupt the integrity 
of the overall structure. The Commission shall 
give consideration to the following as reasonable 
grounds for approving the demolition of an entire 
structure:
(1) If the structure is structurally unsound or 
unsafe as determined by the Director; 
(2) If the structure is not a contributing element 
to the qualities that make the AMH District a 
unique resource; or 
(3) If there is no foreseeable or reasonable 
economic use for the structure and the loss of the 
structure would not adversely affect the overall 
continuity or eliminate landmark elements in the 
AMH District.
E. Certificate of Approval 
Expiration
If a permit, for which a Certificate of Approval has 
been issued, has not been exercised within two years 
from the date of the decision, then the Certificate 
shall be deemed to have expired.
F. Extra Requirements for the ACH
1. Uses Not Permitted. Within the ACH District, 
uses, as identified in Table 4.3-A, Principal Uses, 
of this Ordinance are permitted as they would be 
in its Base Zoning District, with the exception of the 
following uses: Medical Office, Pharmacy, Funeral 
Services, and College or University. These uses 
shall not be permitted within the bounds of the ACH 
Overlay District.
2. Special Design Standards. Within the ACH 
District, the special Millyard District design standards 
as outlined in Section 6.2.4 Millyard District (MILL),
shall apply to this overlay area.

Overlay
A. Development Review for the 
Gaslight Historic District Overlay
The Heritage Commission shall maintain the ability 
to act in an advisory capacity to the Planning Board 
and shall have the power to require application 
review of all development cases in advance of any 
Planning Board decision.
B. Exemption from Minimum 
Parking Requirements
Properties within this overlay district shall not 
be mandated to abide by the minimum parking 
requirements pursuant to Table 7.2-A Off-Street 
Parking Requirements.
6.3.6 Manchester Landfill
Groundwater Management Zone
(ML-GMZ)
A. Authority
The Manchester Landfill Groundwater Management 
Zone is adopted pursuant to Section 1.1.3 Authority,
of this Code, and in accordance with the provisions 
of RSA 674:21, Innovative Land Use Controls. 
Monitoring wells and surface water sampling stations 
constitute remediation activities and the ML-GMZ 
Overlay District is considered to be an innovative

zoning.

Zone Overlay is established in accordance with, and 
for the purposes stated in Section 3.3.3 Overlay 
Districts, and encompasses lands as indicated

ARTICLE 6: SPECIAL DISTRICT-WIDE REGULATIONS
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 151
Overlay District Regulations
ARTICLE 6
in the NHDES Manchester Landfill Groundwater 
Management Zone Permit.
The Manchester Landfill Groundwater Management 
Zone Overlay contains those parcels affected 
by groundwater contamination by virtue of lying 
down gradient of the City landfill. Withdrawal of 
groundwater from this area is prohibited in the 
interest of public health, safety and general welfare. 
The area contains monitoring wells and surface 
water sampling stations that survey the remediation 
of degraded groundwater supplies. The extent of the 
area is referenced by NHDES Permit.
C. Uses Prohibited
Pumping of groundwater for any well, trench, sump or 
other structure for residential, irrigation, agricultural 
or industrial purpose is prohibited, unless it is for the 
specific purpose of pumping groundwater out of a 
sump to keep a cellar from flooding. 
6.3.7 Lake Massabesic Protection
Overlay District (LMPOD)
A. Authority
The Lake Massabesic Protection Overlay District 
is adopted pursuant to Section 1.1.3 Authority, and 
in accordance with the provisions of RSA 674:21, 
Innovative Land use Controls.
B. Establishment
The Lake Massabesic Protection Overlay District 
includes the entire Lake Massabesic watershed 
located in the City. This area is called out to avoid 
impacts that may affect the drinking water supply 
over the long term, addressing such issues as 
stormwater contamination, impervious surfaces, 
steep slope disturbance and other land use activities 
that could potentially be a nonpoint source water 
quality issue or diminish surface water recharge. 
EPA Phase II Stormwater Regulation criteria apply 
to all development creating disturbance to land in the 
Lake Massabesic Protection Zone.
C. Prohibitions
1. Within the Lake Massabesic Protection Overlay 
District, regardless of the underlying district, the 
following land uses in Table 6.3.7-A are deemed 
incompatible with the intent of and are prohibited in 
the Lake Massabesic Protection Overlay District:
TABLE 6.3.7-A PROHIBITIONS WITHIN THE 
LAKE MASSABESIC PROTECTION OVERLAY 
DISTRICT
Use
Passenger Terminal
Vehicle Rental, Sales, or Repair
Truck and Heavy Equipment Sales, Rental or Repair
Major or Minor Vehicle Repair
Vehicle Fueling Station
Car Wash
Accessory Outdoor Storage
2. Impervious surfaces are not permitted within 50 
feet of waterways or wetlands in the Lake Massabesic 
Protection Overlay District. The exception from this 
restriction includes residential lots of 10,000 square 
feet or less and commercial or industrial use lots of 
less than one acre in BC-2.
3. Within the Lake Massabesic Protection Overlay 
District, regardless of the underlying district, the 
maximum lot coverage shall not exceed 60 percent.
D. Additional Restrictive Policies
In addition to the restrictions listed in this Overlay 
District, the Lake Massabesic Protection Overlay 
District is also subject to criteria and guidelines 
contained in the following documents on file in the 
City:
1. City Stormwater Ordinance (and any subsequent 
revisions) – Highway Department.
2. City Stormwater Rules and Regulations (and any 
subsequent revisions) – Highway Department.
3. Subdivision and Site Plan Review Regulations (and 
any subsequent revisions) – Planning and Community 
Development Department.
