ARTICLE 6: SPECIAL DISTRICT-WIDE REGULATIONS
152 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE
City-wide Regulations
Section 6.4
CITY-WIDE REGULATIONS
6.4.1 Junkyards and the Storage
of Junk
A. Purpose
The excessive accumulation of junk stored on private 
property in the City has the potential to become a 
nuisance, a hazard to the public health, safety, 
and welfare, and a source of declining property 
values and aesthetics. Accordingly, it is the purpose 
and intent of this section to establish reasonable 
regulations to prevent the excessive accumulation 
and storage of junk in all areas of the City.
B. Storage of Junk in Residential 
and Mixed-Use Districts
1. The storage or accumulation of junk in the front 
yard or side yard of any lot within a Residential (R) or 
Mixed-Use (MX) District is prohibited. 
2. The storage of junk in the rear yard of a lot shall 
be considered de minimis and permitted within a 
residential district if it:
a. Is located no closer than 10 feet to a property 
line;
b. Is incidental to the normal use of a residential 
property;
c. Does not exceed an aggregate area of 75 
square feet;
d. Does not exceed a height of four feet; and
e. Is not visible from a public street.
C. Storage of Junk and Junkyards 
in All Other Districts
1. The storage or accumulation of junk in the front 
and side yards of any property within any district not 
specified above in 6.4.1.B is prohibited.
2. The storage of junk in the rear yard of a lot shall 
be considered de minimis and permitted within a non￾residential district if it:
a. Is located no closer than 10 feet to a property 
line;
b. Is incidental to the normal use of the use 
classification on the property;
c. Does not exceed an aggregate area of 150 
square feet; and
d. Does not exceed a height of four feet. 
D. Licensing and Standards of 
Junkyards
1. All junkyards shall comply with this Ordinance and 
the municipal licensing requirements of RSA 236:111, 
et seq. This shall include the requirement that no 
junkyard may be established without (1) a license 
from the Board of Mayor and Aldermen to operate a 
junkyard and (2) a certificate from the Zoning Board 
of Adjustment stating that the proposed location of 
the junkyard is neither within a zoning district that 
restricts such use nor contrary to the prohibitions of 
this Ordinance. The process and fees for establishing 
a junkyard shall be as described in RSA 236:114 – 
122. 
2. Junkyards shall only be permitted as a Heavy 
Industrial use within the IND Zoning District.
3. All junkyards shall be located no closer than 200 
feet from the right-of-way lines of a non-interstate 
class I, class II, class III, or class III-a highway. 
4. All junkyards shall be located no closer than 100 
feet from the right-of-way lines of a class IV, class V, 
or class VI highway. 
5. All junkyards shall be completely screened by an 
eight feet high solid fence.
6. The following uses shall be exempt from the 
definition of “junkyard” and the related licensing 
requirement:
a. The principal place of business of any motor 
vehicle dealer that is registered with the New 
Hampshire Director of Motor Vehicles, so long 
as all junk, including vehicles that are wrecked 
or disassembled, is removed from the lot within 
160 days from the date of arrival and screened 
in conformance with Section 4.6.2.I. Outdoor 
Storage; and
b. Any solid waste facility that has been approved 
and permitted by the New Hampshire Department 
of Environmental Services, pursuant to RSA 149-M, 
including landfills, incinerators, recycling centers, 
transfer stations, or other waste-processing 
facilities.

CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 153
City-wide Regulations
ARTICLE 6
6.4.2 Limited Activity Buffers
A. Requirements for Properties 
Adjacent to Primarily Residential 
Districts
A limited activity buffer shall be required for parcels 
with non-residential uses within the BC-1, BC￾2, ID, and IND districts that abut the boundary of 
any parcel with a residential principal building type 
within a Residential (R) or Mixed-Use (MX) district. 
A limited activity buffer is also required for parcels 
used for non-residential purposes within Residential 
(R) districts. The buffer shall be established at 
such time as a new non-residential use is located 
on a parcel or that an existing non-residential use 
is expanded or undergoes substantial renovation. 
The limited activity buffer shall be 50 feet in width 
as measured from the closest adjacent lot line of 
a lot used for residential purposes. The following 
activities, improvements, facilities, and accessory 
uses are prohibited within the limited activity buffer:
1. Ventilators or exhaust systems from commercial 
food preparation or processing facilities;
2. Exterior lighting fixtures at a height in excess of 
10 feet;
3. Illuminated signs;
4. Truck docks, loading spaces or bays, or 
designated truck parking areas;
5. Exterior speaker systems;
6. Drive-through windows or vehicle stacking lanes 
for the same;
7. The repair, dismantling, or storage of equipment 
or machinery;
8. Dumpsters or waste storage facilities of any kind:
9. Commercial kennels; or
10. Heating, ventilation, or air conditioning 
equipment that is not enclosed within a building.
B. Requirements for Properties 
Adjacent to the Conservation 
District
All properties, regardless of their primary use, that 
are located within BC-2 or IND districts shall keep 
a limited activity buffer of no less than 50 feet in 
width between any structure, impervious surface, 
or use on the property and the closest adjacent lot 
line of a lot within the Conservation District. This 
buffer shall remain free of clearing, grading, filling, 
or other disturbance, other than what is necessary 
for stormwater management or the construction of 
a trail or pathway used for passive recreation. The 
buffer shall be established at such time as: a) a 
new non-residential use is located on a parcel; or 
b) an existing non-residential use is expanded or 
undergoes substantial renovation.
C. Waiver
The Planning Board may grant a waiver(s) to this 
section in the course of the Site Plan review process 
provided that the applicant can demonstrate that the 
granting of such waiver(s) would be in the public 
interest, and that it would not be detrimental to the 
abutting properties.
6.4.3 Wetland Setbacks & Buffers
A. Overview
The location of wetlands and vernal pools shall be 
determined by a wetland scientist licensed by the 
State of New Hampshire. 
The regulations for wetland setbacks and wetland 
buffers shall not apply to wetlands and vernal pools, 
or portions thereof, that have been permitted for filling 
by the NH Department of Environmental Services. 
B. Definitions
The following definitions shall apply only to the 
wetlands ordinance contained in this Section, and 
shall not be affected by the provisions of any other 
Ordinance:
Wetland Buffer: A naturally vegetated area adjacent 
to a wetland or vernal pool that shall be free of all 
buildings, structures, or impervious surfaces, and shall 
also remain in its natural state, free from mowing, 
clearing, grading, filling, or other disturbance.
Wetland Setback: The linear distance extended 
outward in all directions from the edge of a wetland or 
vernal pool that shall be free of all buildings, structures, 
or impervious surfaces. However, low impact stormwater 
structures (e.g., bioretention areas, infiltration trenches, 
or grass swales) are permitted within the setback area.
C. Regulations For All Wetlands 
and Vernal Pools
1. Setbacks. Except as otherwise specified for 
Highest Priority Wetlands, a 25-foot wetland setback 
shall be maintained from any wetland or vernal pool 
within the State Statutory jurisdiction of the NH 
Department of Environmental Services.

154 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE
City-wide Regulations
2. Buffer. Within this 25-foot setback, the first 10 
feet starting from the edge of the wetland or vernal 
pool shall be maintained as a wetland buffer.
D. Further Regulation for Highest 
Priority Wetlands
1. Setbacks. A 50-foot wetland setback shall be 
maintained from any wetland identified on the 
“Manchester Highest Priority Wetlands Overview 
Map” and associated index maps, as included 
herein. 
2. Buffer. Within this 50-foot setback, the first 25 
feet starting from the edge of the wetland shall be 
maintained as a wetland buffer.
E. Setback and Buffer Reductions 
and Variances
For projects under the Site Plan or Subdivision 
jurisdiction of the Planning Board, the Board may 
reduce such setback or buffer to promote the public 
interest. In addition to the project appearing before 
the Planning Board, the Board may also require an 
appearance before the Conservation Commission. 
The Planning Board may attach such conditions 
as may be necessary to mitigate such reduction. 
In instances where a project is not under Planning 
Board jurisdiction, the Zoning Board may consider 
the granting of a Variance to these setback and buffer 
requirements, but shall first require an appearance 
before the Conservation Commission.
F. Setback for On-site Subsurface 
Disposal Systems
No on-site subsurface disposal system or any part 
thereof shall be constructed or enlarged within 125 
feet of a wetland or vernal pool.
6.4.4 Floodplain Management
A. Statutory Authority and Purpose
1. This Section, adopted pursuant to the authority 
of RSA 674:16, RSA 674:17, and 674:56, shall be 
known as the City of Manchester, NH Floodplain 
Management Ordinance (“Floodplain Ordinance”). 
The regulations in this Floodplain Ordinance shall 
overlay and supplement the regulations in the 
Manchester, NH Zoning Ordinance, and shall be 
considered part of the Zoning Ordinance for purposes 
of administration and appeals under state law.
2. The purpose of this Section is to promote the 
public health, safety, and general welfare; minimize 
hazards to persons and property from flooding; 
protect watercourses from encroachment; and 
maintain the capability of floodplains to retain and 
carry off floodwaters. 
B. Findings of Fact and Applicability.
1. Certain areas of the City are subject to periodic 
flooding, causing serious damages to properties 
within these areas. Relief is available in the form of 
flood insurance as authorized by the National Flood 
Insurance Act of 1968. Therefore, the City has chosen 
to become a participating community in the National 
Flood Insurance Program (NFIP), and agrees to 
comply with the requirements of the National Flood 
Insurance Act of 1968 (P.L. 90-488, as amended) as 
detailed in this Section.
2. The following regulations in this Section shall 
apply to all lands within the City and designated as 
special flood hazard areas by the Federal Emergency 
Management Agency (FEMA) in its “Flood Insurance 
Study (FIS) for Hillsborough County, NH” dated 
September 25, 2009, together with the associated 
Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) panels dated 
September 25, 2009, and associated amendments 
and revisions, which are declared to be a part of this 
Section and are hereby incorporated by reference.
3. This Floodplain Ordinance establishes a permit 
system and review procedure for development in a 
special flood hazard area of the City.
C. Administrative Provisions
1. If any provision of this Floodplain Ordinance 
differs or appears in conflict with any other ordinance 
or regulation, the provision imposing the greater 
restriction or more stringent standard shall be 
controlling.
2. Should any section or provision of this Floodplain 
Ordinance be declared by the courts to be 
unconstitutional or invalid, such decision shall not 
affect the validity of the Floodplain Ordinance as 
a whole, or any part thereof other than the part so 
declared to be unconstitutional or invalid.
3. In accordance with RSA 676, the Floodplain 
Administrator shall enforce and administer the 
provisions of this Floodplain Ordinance.
4. The degree of flood protection required by this 
Floodplain Ordinance is considered reasonable for 
regulatory purposes and is based on scientific and 
engineering considerations. Larger floods can and will 
occur, and flood heights may be increased by man-

made or natural causes. This Floodplain Ordinance 
does not imply that land outside of a special flood 
hazard area or uses that are permitted within such 
areas will be free from flooding or flood damage.
D. Floodplain Administrator Duties 
and Responsibilities
1. The Director is hereby appointed to administer 
and implement these regulations and is referred to 
herein as the “Floodplain Administrator.”
2. The duties and responsibilities of the Floodplain 
Administrator shall include, but are not limited to:
a. Ensuring that permits are obtained for proposed 
development in a special flood hazard area;
b. Reviewing all permit applications for 
completeness and accuracy, and coordinating 
with the applicant for corrections or further 
documentation, as needed;
c. Interpreting the special flood hazard area and 
floodway boundaries and determining whether a 
proposed development is located in a special flood 
hazard area, and if so, whether it is also located in 
a floodway;
d. Providing available flood zone and base flood 
elevation information pertinent to the proposed 
development;
e. Making the determination as to whether a 
structure will be substantially improved or has 
incurred substantial damage as defined in this 
Floodplain Ordinance and enforcing the provisions 
of this Floodplain Ordinance for any structure 
determined to be substantially improved or 
substantially damaged;
f. Issuing or denying a permit based on review of the 
permit application and any required accompanying 
documentation;
g. Ensuring prior to any alteration or relocation 
of a watercourse that the required submittal 
and notification requirements in this Floodplain 
Ordinance are met;
h. Reviewing all required as-built documentation 
and other documentation submitted by the applicant 
for completeness and accuracy and verifying that 
all permit conditions have been completed in 
compliance with this Floodplain Ordinance; 
i. Notifying the applicant in writing of either 
compliance or non-compliance with the provisions 
of this Floodplain Ordinance; 
j. Ensuring the administrative and enforcement 
procedures detailed in RSA 676 are followed for 
any violations of this Floodplain Ordinance;
k. Submitting to FEMA, or requiring applicants to 
submit to FEMA, data and information necessary 
to maintain FIRMs, including hydrologic and 
hydraulic engineering analyses prepared by or 
for the City, within six months after such data and 
information becomes available if the analyses 
indicate changes in base flood elevations, special 
flood hazard areas and/or floodway boundaries;
l. Maintaining and permanently keeping and 
making available for public inspection all 
records that are necessary for the administration 
of these regulations, including: local permit 
documents, flood zone and base flood elevation 
determinations, substantial improvement and 
damage determinations, variance and enforcement 
documentation, and as-built elevation and dry 
floodproofing data for structures subject to this 
Floodplain Ordinance; and
m. Delegating duties and responsibilities set 
forth in these regulations to qualified technical 
personnel, inspectors, or other community officials 
as needed.
E. Flood Zone and Floodway 
Determinations
1. The Floodplain Administrator shall determine 
whether any portion of a proposed development 
is located in a special flood hazard area and if so, 
whether it is also located in a floodway, using the 
effective FIRM. If the development is located wholly or 
partially in a special flood hazard area, the Floodplain 
Administrator shall determine the flood zone and the 
applicable requirements in the Floodplain Ordinance 
that shall apply to the development.
2. Where it is unclear whether a site is in a special 
flood hazard area and/or in a floodway, the Floodplain 
Administrator may require additional information from 
the applicant to determine the development’s location 
on the effective FIRM.

5. Within a riverine special flood hazard area 
designated as Zone A, the Floodplain Administrator 
shall obtain, review, and reasonably utilize any 
floodway data available from Federal, State, or other 
sources. If floodway data is available, the applicant 
shall meet the floodway requirements in Section 14 
of this Floodplain Ordinance.
F. Substantial Improvement and 
Damage Determinations
1. For all development in a special flood hazard 
area that proposes to improve an existing structure, 
including alterations, movement, enlargement, 
replacement, repair, additions, rehabilitations, 
renovations, repairs of damage from any origin (such 
as, but not limited to flood, fire, wind or snow) and 
any other improvement of or work on such structure 
including within its existing footprint, the Floodplain 
Administrator, in coordination with any other 
applicable community official(s), shall be responsible 
for the following:
a. Reviewing description of proposed work 
submitted by the applicant;
b. Using the community’s current assessed 
value of the structure (excluding the land) to 
determine the market value of the structure prior 
to the start of the initial repair or improvement, or 
in the case of damage, the market value prior to 
the damage occurring. If the applicant disagrees 
with the use of the community’s assessed value 
of the structure, the applicant is responsible for 
engaging a licensed property appraiser to submit a 
comparable property appraisal for the total market 
value of only the structure;
c. Reviewing cost estimates of the proposed 
work including donated or discounted materials 
and owner and volunteer labor submitted by the 
applicant. Determining if the costs are reasonable 
for the proposed work, or using other acceptable 
methods, such as those prepared by licensed 
contractors or professional construction cost 
estimators and from building valuation tables, to 
estimate the costs;
d. Determining if the proposed work constitutes 
substantial improvement or repair of substantial 
damage as defined in this Floodplain Ordinance; 
and
e. Notifying the applicant in writing of the result 
of the substantial improvement or damage 
determination. If the determination is that the work 
constitutes substantial improvement or substantial 
damage, the written documentation shall state 
that full compliance with the provisions of this 
Floodplain Ordinance is required.
2. Repair, alteration, additions, rehabilitation, or 
other improvements of historic structures shall not 
be subject to the elevation and dry floodproofing 
requirements of this Floodplain Ordinance if 
the proposed work will not affect the structure’s 
designation as a historic structure. The documentation 
of a structure’s continued eligibility and designation 
as a historic structure shall be required by the 
Floodplain Administrator in approving this exemption.
G. Floodplain Permitting 
Requirements
1. All proposed development within a special flood 
hazard area shall require a permit from the City, 
prior to the commencement of any development 
activities. Development, as defined in this Floodplain 
Ordinance, includes both building and non-building 
activities.
2. To obtain a permit, the applicant shall first submit 
a completed application in writing on a form furnished 
by the City, for that purpose. Every application shall 
include, but is not limited to:
a. The name, address and phone number of the 
applicant, owner, and contractor(s);
b. A map indicating the location of the proposed 
development sufficient to accurately locate 
property and structure(s) in relation to existing 
roads and waterbodies;
c. A description of the proposed development 
and the use or occupancy for which the proposed 
development is intended;
d. If the development involves proposed work 
on an existing structure, a description of the total 
costs of the proposed work including all materials 
and labor;
e. In a Zone A, for proposed developments 
either greater than 50 lots or greater than 
five acres, the base flood elevation(s) established 
for the area, including any data such as hydraulic 
and hydrologic analyses, used to determine the 
elevation(s);

City-wide Regulations

or located so as to prevent water from entering 
or accumulating within the components during

f. Adequately drained to reduce exposure to flood 
hazards;
g. Compliant with the applicable requirements 
of the State Building Code and the applicable 
standards in this Floodplain Ordinance, whichever 
is more restrictive.
K. Structure Requirements
1. New construction of a residential structure, or 
an existing residential structure to be substantially 
improved or replaced, or that has incurred substantial 
damage, located in a special flood hazard area shall 
have the lowest floor elevated at least to one foot 
above the base flood elevation.
2. New construction of a non-residential structure, or 
an existing non-residential structure to be substantially 
improved or replaced, or that has incurred substantial 
damage, located in a special flood hazard area shall:
a. Have the lowest floor elevated at least one foot 
above the base flood elevation; or
b. Together with attendant utility and sanitary 
facilities:
(1) Be floodproofed at least one foot above the 
base flood elevation so that below this elevation 
the structure is watertight with walls substantially 
impermeable to the passage of water;
(2) Have structural components capable of 
resisting hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loads 
and the effects of buoyancy; and
(3) Be certified by a registered professional 
engineer or architect that the dry floodproofing 
design and methods of construction are in 
accordance with accepted standards of practice 
for meeting the provisions of this section. Such 
certification shall be provided to the Floodplain 
Administrator in the form of a completed and 
signed Floodproofing Certificate for Non￾Residential Structures.
3. A fully enclosed area for new construction of a 
structure, or an existing structure to be substantially 
improved or replaced, or that has incurred substantial 
damage located in a special flood hazard area that is 
below the lowest floor of a structure, below the base 
flood elevation, and therefore subject to flooding, 
shall meet the following requirements:
a. Be constructed with flood damage-resistant 
materials;
b. Be used solely for the parking of vehicles, 
building access, or storage; 
c. Be constructed with the floor of the enclosed 
area at grade on at least one side of the structure; 
and
d. Be constructed with flood openings installed in 
the enclosure walls so that they are designed to 
automatically equalize hydrostatic flood forces on 
exterior walls by allowing for the entry and exit of 
floodwater. Designs for meeting this requirement 
shall either be certified by a registered professional 
engineer or architect or must meet or exceed the 
following minimum criteria:
(1) A minimum of two flood openings on different 
sides of each enclosed area having a total net 
area of not less than one square inch for every 
square foot of enclosed area subject to flooding 
shall be provided; 
(2) The bottom of all flood openings shall be no 
higher on the enclosure wall than one foot above 
either the interior or exterior grade, whichever is 
higher; and
(3) Flood openings may be equipped with 
screens, louvers, or other coverings or devices 
provided that they permit the automatic entry 
and exit of floodwaters.
4. A fully enclosed area that has a floor that is below 
grade on all sides, including below-grade crawlspaces 
and basements, is prohibited for new structures, 
existing structures to be substantially improved or 
replaced, or that have incurred substantial damage 
located in a special flood hazard area.
L. Detached Accessory Structures
1. In a special flood hazard area, new construction 
or substantial improvement of a small, detached 
accessory structure of 500 square feet or less does 
not have to meet the elevation or non-residential 
dry floodproofing requirements as detailed in this 
Floodplain Ordinance if the following wet floodproofing 
standards are met:

b. The structure is not located in the floodway;

d. The structure is wet floodproofed and designed 
to allow for the automatic entry and exit of 
flood water as detailed in 6.4.4.K. Structure 
Requirements; 
e. The structure shall be firmly anchored to prevent 
flotation, collapse and lateral movement;
f. When possible, the structure shall be constructed 
and placed on the building site so as to offer the 
minimum resistance to the flow of floodwaters and 
be placed further from the source of flooding than 
the primary structure; and
g. Service facilities such as electrical, mechanical 
and heating equipment shall be elevated or dry 
floodproofed to or above the base flood elevation.
M. Manufactured Homes and 
Recreational Vehicles
1. A new manufactured home to be placed in a special 
flood hazard area, or an existing manufactured home 
to be substantially improved or replaced, or that has 
incurred substantial damage, located in a special 
flood hazard area shall:
a. Have the lowest floor elevated at least one foot 
above the base flood elevation; 
b. Be on a permanent, reinforced foundation;
c. Be installed using methods and practices which 
minimize flood damage; 
d. Be securely anchored to an adequately 
anchored foundation system to resist flotation, 
collapse and lateral movement. Methods of 
anchoring are authorized to include, but are not to 
be limited to, use of over-the-top or frame ties to 
ground anchors. This requirement is in addition to 
applicable state and local anchoring requirements 
for resisting wind forces; and
e. Comply with the requirements of this Floodplain 
Ordinance in cases where fully enclosed areas are 
present below an elevated manufactured home, 
including enclosures surrounded by rigid skirting or 
other material attached to the frame or foundation. 
Flexible skirting and rigid skirting not attached to 
the frame or foundation of a manufactured home 
are not required to have flood openings.
2. A recreational vehicle located within a special 
flood hazard area shall meet one of the following 
requirements:
a. Be on a site for fewer than 180 consecutive 
days; or
b. Be fully licensed, on wheels or jacking system, 
attached to the site only by quick disconnect 
type utilities and security devices, and with no 
permanently attached additions; or
c. Meet the requirements for “manufactured 
homes” as stated in this Floodplain Ordinance.
N. Water Supply and Sewage 
Disposal Systems
1. The following standards shall apply to all water 
supply, sanitary sewage, and on-site waste disposal 
systems located in a special flood hazard area:
a. All new and replacement water supply systems 
shall be designed to minimize or eliminate 
infiltration of flood waters into the systems;
b. New and replacement sanitary sewage systems 
shall be designed and located to minimize or 
eliminate infiltration of flood waters into the 
systems and discharge from the system into flood 
waters; and 
c. On-site waste disposal systems shall be located 
and constructed to avoid impairment to them or 
contamination from them during flooding.
O. Floodway Requirements

fill, new construction, substantial improvements

City-wide Regulations

also obtain a Letter of Map Revision (LOMR) from 
FEMA. CLOMR and LOMR submittal requirements 
and fees shall be the responsibility of the applicant.
2. Within a riverine special flood hazard area 
where a base flood elevation has been determined 
but a floodway has not been designated, for any 
development, including fill, new construction, 
substantial improvements and other development or 
land disturbing-activity, the applicant must, prior to a 
permit being issued by the Floodplain Administrator, 
submit certification prepared by a registered 
professional engineer, along with supporting 
technical data and analyses, that demonstrates that 
the cumulative effect of the proposed development, 
when combined with all other existing and anticipated 
development, will not increase the base flood 
elevation more than one foot at any point within the 
community.
If the analyses demonstrate that the proposed 
activities will result in more than a one foot increase 
in the base flood elevation, the applicant must obtain 
a Conditional Letter of Map Revision (CLOMR) from 
FEMA prior to permit issuance by the Floodplain 
Administrator. The Floodplain Administrator reserves 
the right to deny a permit for the project if concerns 
about the development being reasonably safe from 
flooding remain following issuance of the CLOMR. 
If a permit is issued and the project completed, the 
applicant must also obtain a Letter of Map Revision 
(LOMR) from FEMA. CLOMR and LOMR submittal 
requirements and fees shall be the responsibility of 
the applicant.
P. Watercourse Alterations
1. Prior to a permit being issued by the Floodplain 
Administrator for any alteration or relocation of any 
riverine watercourse, the applicant shall:
a. Notify the Wetlands Bureau of the New 
Hampshire Department of Environmental Services 
and submit copies of such notification to the 
Floodplain Administrator, in addition to the copies 
required by RSA 482-A: 3; and
b. Submit to the Floodplain Administrator 
certification provided by a registered professional 
engineer, assuring that the flood carrying capacity 
of an altered or relocated watercourse can and will 
be maintained.
2. Prior to a permit being issued for any alteration or 
relocation of any riverine watercourse, the Floodplain 
Administrator shall notify adjacent communities and 
the State NFIP Coordinating Agency, and submit 
copies of such notification to FEMA’s Federal 
Insurance Administrator.
Q. Variances and Appeals
1. Any order, requirement, decision or determination 
of the Floodplain Administrator made under this 
Floodplain Ordinance may be appealed to the Zoning 
Board of Adjustment as set forth in RSA 676:5.
2. If the applicant, upon appeal, requests a Variance 
as authorized by RSA 674:33,I(b), the applicant 
shall have the burden of showing in addition to the 
Variance standards under state law that:
a. The Variance will not result in increased flood 
heights of any magnitude, additional threats to 
public safety, fraud on or victimization of the public; 
or extraordinary public expense;
b. The issuance of the Variance will not conflict 
with other State, Federal or local laws or Floodplain 
Ordinances; 
c. If the requested Variance is for activity within 
a floodway, no increase in flood levels during the 
base flood discharge will result; and
d. The Variance is the minimum necessary, 
considering the flood hazard, to afford relief.
3. The Zoning Board of Adjustment shall notify the 
applicant in writing that:
a. The issuance of a Variance to construct below 
the base flood elevation will result in increased 
premium rates for flood insurance up to amounts 
as high as $25 for $100 of insurance coverage; and 
b. Such construction below the base flood 
elevation increases risks to life and property.
Such notification shall be maintained with a record of 
all Variance actions.
4. The community shall:
a. Maintain a record of all Variance actions, 
including their justification for their issuance; and 
b. Report such Variances issued in its annual 
or biennial report submitted to FEMA’s Federal 
Insurance Administrator.
R. Definitions
The following definitions shall apply only to the 
Floodplain Ordinance contained in this Section, and 
shall not be affected by the provisions of any other 
Ordinance.

ARTICLE 6: SPECIAL DISTRICT-WIDE REGULATIONS
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 161
City-wide Regulations
ARTICLE 6
Accessory Structure: A structure which is: 1) 
detached from and clearly incidental and subordinate to 
the principal use or structure on a lot, 2) located on the 
same lot as the principal structure or use, 3) clearly and 
customarily related to the principal structure or use, and 
4) only used for vehicle parking, storage, or primarily 
building access. Examples include garages, garden 
and tool sheds, and playhouses.
Base Flood or One Percent Annual Chance Flood:
The flood having a one‑percent possibility of being 
equaled or exceeded in any given year. 
Base Flood Elevation (BFE): The elevation of surface 
water resulting from the “base flood” referenced to a 
specified vertical datum (National Geodetic Vertical 
Datum of 1929 or North American Vertical Datum of 
1988).
Basement: Any area of a structure having its floor 
subgrade (below ground-level) on all sides. 
Building: ‑ See “Structure”.
Conditional Letter of Map Revision (CLOMR):
FEMA’s comment on a proposed project that would, 
upon construction, affect the hydrologic and/or hydraulic 
characteristics of a flooding source and thus result in 
the modification of the existing floodway, base flood 
elevation, or the special flood hazard area. CLOMRs 
do not revise an effective FIRM since they do not reflect 
as-built conditions.
Development: Any man‑made change to improved 
or unimproved real estate, including but not limited to 
buildings or other structures, mining, dredging, filling, 
grading, paving, excavating or drilling operations or 
storage of equipment or materials.
Elevation Certificate: A form developed by FEMA 
to collect surveyed elevations and other information 
about a building, which can be used for the purposes of 
compliance with a community’s floodplain regulations, 
flood insurance rating, and Letters of Map Amendment 
applications.
Enclosed Area: An area created by a crawlspace or 
solid walls that fully enclose an area below an elevated 
building.
FEMA: The Federal Emergency Management Agency.
Flood or Flooding: A general and temporary condition 
of partial or complete inundation of normally dry land 
areas from: 
1. The overflow of inland or tidal waters, or
2. The unusual and rapid accumulation or runoff of 
surface waters from any source. 
Flood Damage-Resistant Materials: Any building 
product (material, component or system) capable 
of withstanding direct and prolonged contact with 
floodwaters without sustaining significant damage. See 
FEMA “Technical Bulletin 2, Flood Damage-Resistant 
Materials Requirements.”
Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM): The official map 
incorporated with this Floodplain Ordinance, on which 
FEMA has delineated both the special flood hazard 
areas and the risk premium zones applicable to the 
community. The FIRM is a graphic representation of the 
data contained in the accompanying Flood Insurance 
Study.
Flood Insurance Study (FIS): A compilation and 
presentation of flood risk data for specific watercourses, 
lakes, and coastal flood hazard areas within a 
community. The FIS report contains detailed flood 
elevation data in flood profiles and data tables.
Flood Opening: An opening in a foundation or 
enclosure wall that allows automatic entry and exit of 
floodwaters. See FEMA “Technical Bulletin 1, Openings 
in Foundation Walls and Walls of Enclosures.”
Floodplain or Flood‑prone Area: Any land area 
susceptible to being inundated by water from any 
source (see definition of “Flooding”).
Floodplain Administrator: A person responsible for 
administering and implementing the community’s local 
floodplain ordinance and ensuring that the community is 
complying with minimum NFIP standards and enforcing 
any locally imposed higher standards.
Floodproofed or Floodproofing: Any combination 
of structural and non‑structural additions, changes, or 
adjustments to structures that reduce or eliminate flood 
damage to real estate or improved real property, water 
and sanitation facilities, structures and their contents.
Floodproofing Certificate for Non-Residential
Structures: The form developed by FEMA for use in 
the certification of non-residential dry floodproofing 
designs. 
Floodproofing, Dry: Making a structure watertight 
below the level that needs flood protection to prevent 
floodwaters from entering.

ARTICLE 6: SPECIAL DISTRICT-WIDE REGULATIONS
162 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE
City-wide Regulations
Floodproofing, Wet: Permanent or contingent 
measures applied to a structure and/or its contents that 
prevent or provide resistance to damage from flooding 
by allowing flood waters to enter the structure.
Floodway: The channel of a river or other watercourse 
and the adjacent land areas that must be reserved in 
order to discharge the base flood without cumulatively 
increasing the water surface elevation more than a 
designated height.
Highest Adjacent Grade: The highest natural elevation 
of the ground surface prior to construction next to the 
proposed walls of a structure.
Historic Structure: Any structure that is:
1. Listed individually in the National Register of 
Historic Places (a listing maintained by the 
Department of Interior) or preliminarily determined 
by the Secretary of the Interior as meeting the 
requirements for individual listing on the National 
Register;
2. Certified or preliminarily determined by the 
Secretary of the Interior as contributing to the 
historical significance of a registered historic 
district or a district preliminarily determined by the 
Secretary to qualify as a registered historic district;
3. Individually listed on a state inventory of historic 
places in states with historic preservation programs 
which have been approved by the Secretary of the 
Interior; or
4. Individually listed on a local inventory of historic 
places in communities with historic preservation 
programs that have been certified either:
• by an approved state program as determined by 
the Secretary of the Interior; or
• directly by the Secretary of the Interior in states 
without approved programs.
Letter of Map Change: An official document issued 
by FEMA that revises or amends the flood hazard 
information shown on the FIRM without requiring the 
FIRM to be physically revised and/or re-published. 
Letters of Map Change can include Letters of Map 
Amendment, Letters of Map Revision, and Letters of 
Map Revision Based on Fill.
Letter of Map Revision (LOMR): FEMA’s modification 
to an effective FIRM, usually as a result of physical 
changes to the flooding source and floodplain that 
result in the modification of the existing Regulatory 
floodway, base flood elevations, or special flood hazard 
area. LOMRs are a cost effective way to keep FIRMs 
up to date without republishing an entire map panel 
or panels. The LOMR is generally accompanied by an 
annotated copy of the affected portions of the FIRM 
and/or FIS report.
Lowest Floor: The lowest floor of the lowest enclosed 
area (including basement). An unfinished or flood 
resistant enclosure, usable solely for parking of 
vehicles, building access or storage in an area other 
than a basement area is not considered a building’s 
lowest floor; provided, that such an enclosure is built 
in compliance with the applicable non‑elevation design 
requirements in this Floodplain Ordinance. 
Manufactured Home: A structure, transportable in 
one or more sections, which is built on a permanent 
chassis and is designed for use with or without a 
permanent foundation when connected to the required 
utilities. For floodplain management purposes the term 
“manufactured home” includes park trailers, travel 
trailers, and other similar vehicles placed on site for 
greater than 180 consecutive days. This includes 
manufactured homes located in a manufactured home 
park or subdivision.
Manufactured Home Park or Subdivision: A parcel 
(or contiguous parcels) of land divided into two or more 
manufactured home lots for rent or sale.
Mean Sea Level: The National Geodetic Vertical 
Datum (NGVD) of 1929, North American Vertical Datum 
(NAVD) of 1988, or other vertical datum to which base 
flood elevations shown on a community’s FIRMs are 
referenced.
National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP): The 
program created by the Congress of the United States 
in 1968 through the National Flood Insurance Act of 
1968 (P.L. 90-448). The program enables property 
owners in participating communities to purchase 
insurance protection, administered by the government, 
against losses from flooding.
Natural Grade: The grade unaffected by construction 
techniques such as fill, landscaping or berming.
New Construction: Structures for which the start of 
construction commenced on or after the effective date 
of a floodplain management regulation adopted by a 
community and includes any subsequent improvements 
to such structures.
Recreational Vehicle: Means a vehicle:
1. Built on a single chassis;

lowest floor; provided, that such an enclosure is built

flood elevations shown on a community’s FIRMs are 
referenced.

program created by the Congress of the United States 
in 1968 through the National Flood Insurance Act of 
1968 (P.L. 90-448). The program enables property 
owners in participating communities to purchase 
insurance protection, administered by the government, 
against losses from flooding.

techniques such as fill, landscaping or berming.

of a floodplain management regulation adopted by a 
community and includes any subsequent improvements 
to such structures.

Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA): The land in the

Start of Construction: The date the building permit was 
issued, provided the actual start of construction, repair, 
reconstruction, placement, or other improvement, 
including substantial improvements, was within 180 
days of the permit date. The actual start means either the 
first placement of permanent construction of a structure 
on site, such as the pouring of slab or footings, the 
installation of piles, the construction of columns, or any 
work beyond the stage of excavation; or the placement 
of a manufactured home on a foundation. Permanent 
construction does not include land preparation, such 
as clearing, grading and filling; nor does it include 
the installation of streets and/or walkways; nor does 
it include excavation for a basement, footings, piers, 
or foundations or the erection of temporary forms; 
nor does it include the installation on the property of 
accessory buildings, such as garages or sheds not 
occupied as dwelling units or part of the main structure. 
State Building Code: The current codes adopted by 
the State of New Hampshire.
State NFIP Coordinating Agency: The agency of the 
state government (or other office designated by the 
Governor of the state or by state statute) that, at the 
request of the Federal Insurance Administrator, assists 
in the implementation of the National Flood Insurance 
Program (NFIP) in that state.
Structure:A walled and roofed building, including a gas 
or liquid storage tank that is principally above ground, 
as well as a manufactured home.
Substantial Damage: Damage of any origin sustained 
by a structure whereby the cost of restoring the structure 
to its before-damaged condition would equal or exceed 
50 percent of the market value of the structure before 
the damage occurred. The market value of the structure 
should equal the appraised value of the structure prior 
to the damage occurring. 
Substantial Improvement: Any reconstruction, 
rehabilitation, addition, or other improvement of a 
structure, the cost of which equals or exceeds 50 percent 
of the market value of the structure before the “start of 
construction” of the improvement. This term includes 
structures which have incurred “substantial damage”, 
regardless of the actual repair work performed. The 
term does not, however, include either:
1. Any project for improvement of a structure to 
correct existing violations of state or local health, 
sanitary, or safety code specifications which have 
been identified by the local code enforcement 
official and which are the minimum necessary to 
assure safe living conditions; or 
2. Any alteration of a “historic structure,” provided 
that the alteration will not preclude the structure’s 
continued designation as a “historic structure”. 
Water Surface Elevation: The height, in relation 
to the National Geodetic Vertical Datum (NGVD) of 
1929, North American Vertical Datum (NAVD) of 1988, 
or other datum, where specified, of floods of various 
magnitudes and frequencies in the floodplains.
Violation: The failure of a structure or other 
development to be fully compliant with the community’s 
floodplain management regulations.

ARTICLE 7: PARKING
Section 7.1
GENERAL PROVISIONS
7.1.1 Intent
The primary purpose of this Article is to provide
adequate vehicular access to land uses in the city.
This Article, in combination with other provisions
of this Ordinance, is also intended to encourage
the use of public transportation, planned parking
structures, and flexible parking arrangements to
provide access to the Downtown and the Millyard
Districts, and to discourage the reliance on surface
parking lots to serve uses in these areas.
7.1.2 Applicability
A. Areas and Buildings Subject to
Parking Requirements
In any district, except the DT-2 District and the
Gaslight Historic Overlay District, if any structure
is constructed or enlarged or if any use of land is
established or changed, off-street parking spaces
provided by garage spaces or by open-air spaces
shall be provided for the entire use in accordance
with the parking requirements established by this
Article. Existing or new accessory parking or loading
spaces necessary to meet the requirements of this
Article in connection with any existing use shall
hereafter be maintained; except that they may be
relocated but not reduced in number.
B. Changes in Use or Expansion
of Existing Buildings
A change in or expansion of a use shall require
compliance with the number of parking, stacking,
and loading spaces required by this Article, except in
the case of a property that has received a Conditional
Use permit for reduced parking, which may continue
to provide reduced parking if the change in use does
not require more parking or loading spaces than the
use on which the permit was based.
C. Parking Exemptions and
Reductions
1. The DT-2 District and the Gaslight Historic
Overlay District are exempt from the on-site parking
minimums required in Table 7.2-A Off-Street Parking
Requirements .
2. The DT-1 and Millyard Districts shall provide on-
GENERAL PROVISIONS
site parking for one half (1/2) of what would otherwise
be required in Table 7.2-A Off-Street Parking
Requirements , except for Residential or Lodging
uses, which shall provide one parking space per
dwelling, rooming, or lodging unit.
3. Outdoor seating that is located on a sidewalk
within the public right-of-way and has been otherwise
approved by the City of Manchester is exempt from
parking minimums required in Table 7.2-A Off-Street
Parking Requirements. Outdoor seating on private
property is not exempt from parking minimums.
7.1.3 Use and Availability
Required parking spaces shall, at all times, be
available for the parking of vehicles of residents,
customers, patrons, or employees of the principal
use(s) that the spaces are intended to serve.
Required spaces shall not be used for storage of
vehicles, goods, or materials, or for the sale, repair,
or servicing of any vehicles, except for temporary
construction activities on the site.
7.1.4 Parking Access
Unless permitted as a tandem parking space by this
Article, all off-street parking shall have access to a
public right-of-way from the property on which it is
located. Such access may include travel across an
appurtenant easement that encumbers an adjoining
property and that has been recorded.
7.1.5 Plan Required
A plot plan drawn to scale, including the bounds
of the entire parcel and all structures and
impervious areas, is required for all building permit
applications and land use board applications for
new development, paving of driveways and parking
areas, or expansions of buildings. The plan shall
show the layout of all parking spaces, loading areas,
driveways, drive aisles, and required landscaping,
as applicable, for review for conformance with
this Ordinance by the Planning and Community
Development Department.
7.1.6 Conditional Use Permits for
Alternative Parking Arrangements
The Planning Board is authorized to issue Conditional
Use permits to reduce or alter the number of off-

General Provisions
Section 7.1
GENERAL PROVISIONS
7.1.1 Intent
The primary purpose of this Article is to provide 
adequate vehicular access to land uses in the city. 
This Article, in combination with other provisions 
of this Ordinance, is also intended to encourage 
the use of public transportation, planned parking 
structures, and flexible parking arrangements to 
provide access to the Downtown and the Millyard 
Districts, and to discourage the reliance on surface 
parking lots to serve uses in these areas.
7.1.2 Applicability
A. Areas and Buildings Subject to 
Parking Requirements 
In any district, except the DT-2 District and the 
Gaslight Historic Overlay District, if any structure 
is constructed or enlarged or if any use of land is 
established or changed, off-street parking spaces 
provided by garage spaces or by open-air spaces 
shall be provided for the entire use in accordance 
with the parking requirements established by this 
Article. Existing or new accessory parking or loading 
spaces necessary to meet the requirements of this 
Article in connection with any existing use shall 
hereafter be maintained; except that they may be 
relocated but not reduced in number.
B. Changes in Use or Expansion 
of Existing Buildings
A change in or expansion of a use shall require 
compliance with the number of parking, stacking, 
and loading spaces required by this Article, except in 
the case of a property that has received a Conditional 
Use permit for reduced parking, which may continue 
to provide reduced parking if the change in use does

within the public right-of-way and has been otherwise

Required parking spaces shall, at all times, be 
available for the parking of vehicles of residents, 
customers, patrons, or employees of the principal

vehicles, goods, or materials, or for the sale, repair, 
or servicing of any vehicles, except for temporary 
construction activities on the site.

Unless permitted as a tandem parking space by this 
Article, all off-street parking shall have access to a 
public right-of-way from the property on which it is 
located. Such access may include travel across an 
appurtenant easement that encumbers an adjoining 
property and that has been recorded.

REQUIRED NUMBER OF OFF-STREET PARKING SPACES
issued by the Planning Board for alternative parking
arrangements based on adequate off-premises
parking, or a determination that parking to meet
the normal requirements would not be used, or a
combination thereof.
A. Off-Premises Parking
Off-premises parking shall meet the requirements of
either (1) or (2) below, or a combination thereof:
1. Public Parking. The public parking available to the
proposed use, in combination with other uses placing
demands on such facilities, is sufficient in volume,
convenience, safety, and availability to satisfy the
anticipated parking demands of the proposed use.
2. Private Parking. Private parking spaces may be
provided off-site if the use served cannot practically
supply all of its parking on-site and the off-site parking
meets the following requirements:
a. The off-site parking spaces shall be dedicated
to the proposed use and reserved either with
pavement markings or signs;
b. The owner of the lot on which the off-site parking
is located shall be bound by a deed or long-term
lease, requiring the owner, its heirs, and its assigns
to maintain the required number of parking spaces
for the duration of the use served;
c. The off-site parking shall not be located within a
Residential (R) zoning district; and
d. Adequate provisions shall be made to assure
safe pedestrian access between the off-site parking
location and the proposed use.
3. Location of Parking. Whether off-premises
parking is public or private, it shall be within the
following number of feet, measured from the principal
entrance of the use served:
a. 500 feet from a residential use.
b. 1,000 feet from a non-residential use.
c. Parking may be located beyond these minimums
where a regular shuttle or similar means of
transportation is provided along a direct route from
the off-premises parking to the use.
B. Reduced Parking
The Planning Board may reduce the parking
minimums required in Table 7.2-A Off-Street Parking
Requirements upon a showing by the applicant that
the number of parking spaces required would not be
used and that such a reduction in parking would not
negatively impact surrounding properties.

DRIVEWAY DESIGN STANDARDS
Section 7.4
DRIVEWAY DESIGN
STANDARDS
7.4.1 General Requirements
All driveways providing site access from a street,
alley, or other right-of-way shall be designed,
constructed, and maintained as required herein.
7.4.2 Driveway Dimensions
A. Driveway Width
The width of any entrance or exit driveway shall
not exceed 24 feet at its intersection with a lot line,
and shall be maintained for a minimum depth of 10
feet. Wider driveways not exceeding 36 feet in width
are permitted in the BC-2, IND, and Innovation (ID)
Districts.
B. Planning Board Modification
The Planning Board may allow an increase to the
maximum driveway width for an application over
which it has jurisdiction, upon finding that the
increased width:
1. Would not jeopardize pedestrian or motorist
safety; and
2. Would be consistent in character with surrounding
properties and the intent of the zoning district.
7.4.3 Driveway Locations
A. Distance of Driveways to
Intersecting Street
No portion of a driveway shall be closer than 20 feet
to the street lot line of an intersecting street.
B. Distance Between Driveways
within a Lot
The closest points of any two driveways leading from
the same street to a single lot shall not be within
30 feet of each other at their intersections with the
street lot line. On corner lots, the closest points of
driveways providing access to intersecting streets
shall be no closer than 50 feet as measured along
the property line and no closer than 36 feet as
measured diagonally between their closest points at
their intersection with the property line.
ARTICLE 7: PARKING
Section 7.5
PARKING AREA DESIGN
STANDARDS
7.5.1 Parking Design for Lots
with Small Residential Buildings
The following parking standards apply to properties
with House, Duplex, Triple-Decker, and Apartment
House building types with no more than four
dwelling units. The following standards may also
apply to Townhouse building types within a planned
development that have access from a private drive.
A. Setbacks
1. All parking areas, driveways, and drive aisles, as
described in Section 7.3.2 Parking Surfaces , shall be
set back at least four feet from lot lines, except:
a. The intersection of a driveway with a street, alley,
or adjacent lot over which there is an easement for
access; and
b. Where parking spaces are located in a rear or
side yard and are directly accessed from an alley.
In such cases, no setback from side or rear lot lines
shall be required.
2. A maximum of two parking spaces may be located

3. Parking spaces shall be set back at least two feet A
from structures, except that there shall be no setback
required for parking in front of a garage.
B. Location
1. The location of parking on a lot shall conform
with the requirements of the principal building types,
as stated in Sections 5.3.1.A. House to 5.3.1.D.
Apartment House .
2. Parking spaces shall not be located between a
building façade and the principal frontage, except for
parking in front of a garage.
C. Tandem Parking
Tandem parking is permitted, so long as not more
than one required parking space blocks another from
egress. A tandem parking space shall be assigned
to the same dwelling unit as the parking space that
blocks it.

Section 7.5
PARKING AREA DESIGN 
STANDARDS
7.5.1 Parking Design for Lots
with Small Residential Buildings
The following parking standards apply to properties 
with House, Duplex, Triple-Decker, and Apartment 
House building types with no more than four 
dwelling units. The following standards may also 
apply to Townhouse building types within a planned 
development that have access from a private drive.
A. Setbacks
1. All parking areas, driveways, and drive aisles, as 
described in Section 7.3.2 Parking Surfaces, shall be 
set back at least four feet from lot lines, except:
a. The intersection of a driveway with a street, alley, 
or adjacent lot over which there is an easement for 
access; and 
b. Where parking spaces are located in a rear or 
side yard and are directly accessed from an alley. 
In such cases, no setback from side or rear lot lines 
shall be required. 
2. A maximum of two parking spaces may be located 
within 10 feet of any street, side, or rear lot line, 
except where parking spaces are directly accessed 
from an alley, in which case the number of such 
parking spaces within 10 feet of the rear or side lot 
lines shall not be limited. 
3. Parking spaces shall be set back at least two feet 
from structures, except that there shall be no setback 
required for parking in front of a garage. 
B. Location
1. The location of parking on a lot shall conform 
with the requirements of the principal building types, 
as stated in Sections 5.3.1.A. House to 5.3.1.D. 
Apartment House. 
2. Parking spaces shall not be located between a 
building façade and the principal frontage, except for 
parking in front of a garage. 
C. Tandem Parking
Tandem parking is permitted, so long as not more 
than one required parking space blocks another from 
egress. A tandem parking space shall be assigned 
to the same dwelling unit as the parking space that 
blocks it.

Section 7.4
DRIVEWAY DESIGN
STANDARDS
7.4.1 General Requirements
All driveways providing site access from a street,
alley, or other right-of-way shall be designed,
constructed, and maintained as required herein.
7.4.2 Driveway Dimensions
A. Driveway Width
The width of any entrance or exit driveway shall
not exceed 24 feet at its intersection with a lot line,
and shall be maintained for a minimum depth of 10
feet. Wider driveways not exceeding 36 feet in width
are permitted in the BC-2, IND, and Innovation (ID)
Districts.
B. Planning Board Modification
The Planning Board may allow an increase to the
maximum driveway width for an application over
which it has jurisdiction, upon finding that the
increased width:
1. Would not jeopardize pedestrian or motorist
safety; and
2. Would be consistent in character with surrounding
properties and the intent of the zoning district.
7.4.3 Driveway Locations
A. Distance of Driveways to
Intersecting Street
No portion of a driveway shall be closer than 20 feet
to the street lot line of an intersecting street.
B. Distance Between Driveways
within a Lot
The closest points of any two driveways leading from
the same street to a single lot shall not be within
30 feet of each other at their intersections with the
street lot line. On corner lots, the closest points of
driveways providing access to intersecting streets
shall be no closer than 50 feet as measured along
the property line and no closer than 36 feet as
measured diagonally between their closest points at
their intersection with the property line.

ARTICLE 7: PARKING
1. Tandem parking may be located in a conforming
front yard parking area if: (a) the area is not also
being used to access other spaces that would be
blocked by the tandem parking and (b) the parking
area does not contain more than two aisles of
tandem spaces, or a total of four parking spaces,
with a maximum of two parking spaces front-to-
back and side-by-side. Refer to Figure 7.5.1-A.
2. Where more than one tandem parking aisle
is located in a parking area, spaces shall be
demarcated as to which dwelling unit it belongs,
with either a sign or with pavement markings.
FIGURE 7.5.1-A Tandem Parking Spaces
D. Safety of Design for Triple-
Deckers and Apartment Houses
Except for tandem parking spaces, all parking areas
with five or more spaces that are accessed by
driveways shall be designed to permit automobiles
to freely enter and exit a lot. Parking areas shall be
designed so that, without resorting to extraordinary
movements, vehicles may exit the parking area
without backing onto a public street and without
inhibiting pedestrian safety. Parking spaces that
are not 90 degrees to the drive aisle shall not be
permitted if maneuverability out of the parking space
cannot be accomplished in the direction of travel.
E. Landscaping
Parking areas are exempt from the requirements of
Article 8: Site and Landscaping Standards. Areas
not used for walkways, parking spaces, driveways,
or refuse pads shall be built and maintained as a
landscaped area and shall not be paved.
PARKING AREA DESIGN STANDARDS
7.5.2 Parking Design for All
Other Residential and All Non-
Residential Buildings and Uses
The following parking standards apply to all uses
and building types not addressed in Section 7.5.1
Parking Design for Lots with Small Residential
Buildings .
A. Setbacks
1. All parking surfaces, as described in Section
7.3.2 Parking Surfaces , shall be set back at least
10 feet from lot lines, except:
a. The intersection of a driveway with a street, alley,
or adjacent lot over which there is an easement for
access;
b. Parking spaces contained within parking
structures, which shall adhere to the setbacks of
the applicable zoning district and building type; and
c. Where parking spaces are located in a rear or
side yard and are directly accessed from an alley.
In such cases, no setback from side or rear lot lines
shall be required.
d. Where there are less than ten parking spaces in
a lot, parking surfaces may be located within five
feet of a side or rear lot line, so long as a Type
1 Buffer Yard is provided pursuant to Section 8.1,
Landscaping .
2. Parking spaces shall be set back at least four feet
from structures, except that there shall be no setback
required for parking in front of a garage.
B. Location
1. The location of parking on a lot shall conform with
the requirements of the principal building types, as
stated in Sections 5.3.1-E. Townhouse to 5.3.1-P.
Civic .
2. Parking shall not be located between the building
façade and the sole or principal frontage, unless the
building type permits adequate space for parking, a
drive aisle, and maneuverability without exceeding
any maximum front yard setback imposed.
3. Parking shall not be located in driveways or drive
aisles.
C. Tandem Parking
1. Tandem parking is prohibited for non-residential
uses, except those for which an on-site attendant
parks and retrieves automobiles.

Except for tandem parking spaces, all parking areas,

shall be built and maintained as a landscaped area
and shall not be paved.
F. Bumpers
All parking or loading areas within 10 feet of any
structure or property line shall have a curb or
substantial bumper of masonry, steel, or heavy
timber not less than four feet from those structures
or lot lines for property protection. Such stops or
guards shall be securely anchored.
G. Demarcation
Parking spaces, stacking lanes, entry and exit
drives, direction of traffic flow, and pedestrian ways
shall be appropriately demarcated. Demarcation
shall be accomplished with paint or similar method,
and maintained in clearly visible condition.
H. Illumination
Any fixture used to illuminate any parking or loading
area shall be full-cut-off and shall not direct light
toward adjoining premises and rights-of-way.

7.5.3 Stacking Spaces
A. Facilities Requiring Stacking 
Spaces
Any development that involves a Drive-Through 
Facility, as defined in Section 4.6.2.D. Drive-Through, along with all other uses as listed in Table 
7.5.3-A Stacking Spaces, shall provide stacking 
spaces in accordance with this section. 
2. For residential uses, tandem parking is permitted 
when parking spaces have direct access to an alley. 
A tandem parking space shall be assigned to the 
same dwelling unit as the parking space that blocks 
it, and both shall be noted as such with either a sign 
or with pavement markings.
D. Safety of Design
Except for tandem parking spaces, all parking areas, 
loading areas, driveways, and drive aisles shall 
be designed to permit automobiles to freely enter 
and exit a lot. Parking areas shall be designed so 
that, without resorting to extraordinary movements, 
vehicles may exit the parking area without backing 
onto a public street and without inhibiting pedestrian 
safety. Parking spaces that are not 90 degrees to the 
drive aisle shall not be permitted if maneuverability 
out of the parking space cannot be accomplished in 
the direction of travel.
E. Landscaping
All parking areas shall meet the requirements of 
Section 8.1.3 Parking Lot Perimeter Landscape. 
Areas not used for sidewalks, walkways, parking 
spaces, drive aisles, loading spaces, or refuse pads 
shall be built and maintained as a landscaped area 
and shall not be paved.
F. Bumpers
All parking or loading areas within 10 feet of any 
structure or property line shall have a curb or 
substantial bumper of masonry, steel, or heavy 
timber not less than four feet from those structures 
or lot lines for property protection. Such stops or 
guards shall be securely anchored.
G. Demarcation
Parking spaces, stacking lanes, entry and exit 
drives, direction of traffic flow, and pedestrian ways 
shall be appropriately demarcated. Demarcation 
shall be accomplished with paint or similar method, 
and maintained in clearly visible condition. 
H. Illumination
Any fixture used to illuminate any parking or loading 
area shall be full-cut-off and shall not direct light 
toward adjoining premises and rights-of-way.
B. Stacking Space Dimensions
Stacking spaces shall have the same minimum 
dimensions of a standard, 90-degree parking space 
(eight feet six inches in width and 18 feet six inches 
in depth).
C. Design
Stacking spaces shall be located on the same lot as 
the principal use and shall not interfere with other 
required parking spaces or access aisles to said 
parking spaces. Stacking spaces shall be located a 
minimum of 10 feet from all lot lines and shall be 
designed to avoid interference with public rights-of-way.

7.5.4 Loading Area Requirements
All loading areas and facilities shall adhere to the 
following requirements.
A. Table of Off-Street Loading 
Requirements
For each principal use on a lot, the number of loading 
spaces required, if any, shall be determined by the 
gross floor area of the use or building in square feet, 
according to the ranges in Table 7.5.4-A Loading 
Space Requirements.
B. Location
All required loading facilities shall be located on the 
same lot as the use to be served. No loading space 
shall block or project into a street, alley, drive aisle, 
or parking area. Maneuvering space for loading bays 
may, however, be located in drive aisles. Loading 
spaces shall be separate from pedestrian pathways 
and crosswalks. Except within the Industrial (IND) 
District, no loading area shall be located within a 
front or street yard.
C. Parking
Required loading areas shall not be used to satisfy 
requirements for parking.
D. Screening and Landscaped 
Buffers
1. Where any loading area is within 50 feet of, and 
visible from, a public street, the loading area shall be 
screened by a Type 2 Buffer Yard in conformance 
with Section 8.1.2 Landscaped Buffer Yards, except 
for loading areas in the IND District.
2. Where any loading area is located within 50 feet 
of, and visible from, a side or rear lot line that abuts 
any lot in any R or MX Districts, the loading area shall 
be screened by a Type 4 Buffer Yard, in conformance 
with Section 8.1.2 Landscaped Buffer Yards.
E. Dimensions
A small loading space shall be a minimum of 10 feet 
in width by 26 feet in length. A large loading space 
shall be a minimum of 12 feet in width and 40 feet 
in length. Dimensions shall be exclusive of aisle and 
maneuvering space. Loading spaces shall have a 
minimum vertical clearance of 15 feet.

7.6.5 Standard Accessible
Parking Spaces
Accessible parking spaces, other than van-
accessible parking spaces, shall be a minimum of
96 inches (8’) wide and 222 inches (18’6”) long,
and shall be served by a 60-inch-wide (5’) access
aisle that is the same length as the adjacent parking

Spaces
One in every six accessible parking spaces, but not
less than one, shall be van- accessible. Where van-

space shall be a minimum of 132 inches (11’) wide
and 222 inches (18’6”) long. Where van-accessible
parking spaces are served by a 96-inch-wide (8’)
access aisle, the van-accessible parking space
shall be 96 inch (8’) wide. An access aisle shall be
the same length as the adjacent parking space.

ARTICLE 8: SITE AND LANDSCAPING STANDARDS
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 181
Landscaping
ARTICLE 8
Section 8.1
LANDSCAPING
8.1.1 General Provisions
A. Intent
Landscaping is an essential element of site design 
and promotes public health, safety, comfort, 
convenience, and general welfare. Landscaping 
regulations are intended to:
1. Mitigate incompatibilities between adjacent land 
uses and reduce the negative impacts of higher 
intensity land uses on less intense adjacent land 
uses;
2. Provide critical visual and noise buffering between 
higher intensity districts and less intense districts; 
3. Lessen the impact of development by reducing 
glare and heat buildup; and 
4. Break up large expanses of pavement so as to 
reduce impervious surface area, storm water run-off, 
and the level of pollutants from non-point sources.
B. Applicability
All new developments and all additions to existing 
development (building additions, parking area 
expansions, etc.) shall provide landscaping as 
required by this section and within the applicable 
zoning district.
C. Temporary Uses
These provisions do not apply to temporary uses, 
unless determined otherwise by the Director.
D. Minimum Size of Plantings
All plant materials specified within this Ordinance 
shall comply with the minimum sizes at time of 
planting as specified in Table 8.1.1-A, Minimum Size 
at Time of Planting.
E. Relation to Utilities
Plant material located underneath or within 10 
feet of overhead utilities shall be limited to small￾growing trees which do not exceed 25 feet in height 
at maturity. Landscape plantings may be shifted to 
avoid underground utilities.
F. Location of Landscaping
To the greatest extent possible, landscaping required 
by this section shall not interfere with utilities. The 
location of landscaping shall also adhere to Section 
8.4, Visibility at Intersections.
G. Maintenance of Landscape
All plant materials shall be maintained in a healthy, 
growing condition. The owner shall be responsible 
for the replacement of any required planting that 
is removed or dies after the date of planting. Such 
replacement shall occur within three months after the 
start of the next planting season. Failure to maintain 
required landscape areas shall constitute a violation 
of this Ordinance enforceable under the provisions 
of Section 10.3, Administration and Enforcement.
8.1.2 Landscaped Buffer Yards
A. Definition
A buffer yard provides screening or buffering between 
adjacent uses or zoning districts. Buffer yards may 
include a combination of shrubs, trees, fences, and 
walls installed per the requirements Table 8.1.2-A 
Landscaped Buffer Yard Types.
B. Applicability
The installation of a landscaped buffer yard is 
required as listed below. All plantings shall be 
maintained in order to perpetuate the visual barrier. 
The landscaped buffer yards as described in this 
Section are screening requirements that may 
coincide with, but not replace, any limited activity 
buffer required pursuant to Section 6.4.2 Limited 
Activity Buffers.
1. A buffer yard is required between certain district 
boundaries in Table 8.1.2-B Landscaped Buffer Yard 
Required at Certain District Boundaries.

TABLE 8.1.2-A Landscaped Buffer Yard Types
Type 1 Buffer Yard
Type 2 Buffer Yard
The yard shall span a minimum depth of five feet and requires 30 shrubs for every 100 feet of length, spaced evenly or grouped together as desired.
The yard shall span a minimum depth of 10 feet and requires 30 shrubs for every 100 feet of length, spaced evenly or grouped together as desired. In addition, four shade trees shall be provided for every 100 feet of length, spaced evenly at approximately 25 feet on center.

ARTICLE 8: SITE AND LANDSCAPING STANDARDS
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 183
Landscaping
ARTICLE 8
C. Exemptions
1. A buffer is not required for any residential buildings 
of up to four units located in any zoning district. 
2. When a street or alley separates applicable 
zoning districts, a buffer is not required along the lot 
line abutting the street or alley.
D. Buffer Yard Requirements
1. A buffer yard shall be located within the outer 
perimeter of the lot, parallel to and extending to the 
applicable lot line. A buffer yard may not be located 
within the adjacent public right-of-way.
2. Any fractional result shall be rounded up to the 
next whole number. For example, if a minimum 
requirement of two evergreen trees per 25 feet of 
adjacent lot line is applied to a 40-foot lot, the resulting 
fraction of 3.2 is rounded up to four required trees.
3. No building, accessory structure, or vehicle 
parking, may encroach upon a buffer yard. However, 
pedestrian and vehicle access points, plus related 
signs, may encroach upon a buffer yard.
4. When two buffer yard types are required, only the 
more stringent buffer is required to be installed.
E. Buffer Yard Landscaping
1. Pre-existing, equivalent vegetation that is 
conserved within the buffer yard may substitute for 
any required landscape installation, so long as the 
pre-existing vegetation is healthy and growing.
2. Any required trees or shrubs may be installed at 
varying distances to create a naturalistic landscape 
design, so long as the per linear foot requirement is 
applied as an average, and the landscape is arranged 
so as to provide sufficient screening.
3. Buffer yards shall be integral, where possible, with 
on-site stormwater management facilities.
4. All required plant materials within the buffer yard 
shall be maintained in a healthy, growing condition 
over their lifetime, or replaced where necessary.
5. Except as it relates to the required height of 
fences and walls for buffer yards, fences, and walls 
shall be installed and maintained in accordance with 
Section 8.2.

ARTICLE 8: SITE AND LANDSCAPING STANDARDS
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 185
Landscaping
ARTICLE 8
C. Landscape Islands
Landscape islands shall be installed as follows:
1. A terminal island shall be provided at the 
beginning and end of each parking row. No more 
than 40 parking spaces consisting of two rows may 
be located between terminal islands. Internal islands 
located between parking spaces shall be used to 
separate parking spaces into groups of no more than 
20 contiguous spaces per row.
2. Internal islands and terminal islands shall extend 
along the depth of the parking row. An internal or 
terminal island shall be at least eight feet in width 
and the length of an adjacent parking space. In the 
case of an internal or terminal island that spans two 
parking rows, the island shall be the length of two 
adjacent parking spaces. 
3. At least one shade tree is required in each internal 
or terminal island that extends the length of a single 
parking row or, in the case of a double parking row, at 
least two shade trees are required. 
4. Landscape islands may be consolidated or 
intervals may be adjusted as necessary to preserve 
existing trees or facilitate stormwater management.
D. Landscape Medians
1. A landscape median shall be provided between 
every six parking rows.
2. A landscape median shall be at least seven feet in 
width and planted with landscaping, including at least 
one shade tree for every 30 feet of median length. In 
lieu of one shade tree, three ornamental trees may 
be planted.
3. A landscape median may also serve as the 
location for a sidewalk connecting the parking and 
the use served by the parking area, in which case the 
width shall be at least 12 feet and a shade tree every 
30 feet shall not be required.
4. Landscape medians may be consolidated or 
intervals may be adjusted where necessary to 
preserve existing trees or facilitate stormwater 
management.
E. Stormwater Integration
Parking lot interior landscape shall be integrated, 
where possible, with on-site stormwater management 
facilities.

ARTICLE 8: SITE AND LANDSCAPING STANDARDS
FENCES AND WALLS
Section 8.2
FENCES AND WALLS
FIGURE 8.2.4-A FENCE HEIGHT
8.2.1 Applicability
[IMAGE]
The construction of a new fence or wall, or
reconstruction of an existing fence or wall, shall
comply with the standards of this Section.
8.2.2 Permit Required
No fence, wall, or similar barrier shall be installed
without first securing a permit.
8.2.3 Location
Fences and walls may encroach into any required
setback and be located in any established yard.
No fence or wall shall encroach across a lot line or
into a public right-of-way. All fences and walls shall
comply with Section 8.4 Visibility at Intersections.
8.2.4 Height
Fences and walls shall not exceed the maximum
height listed in Table 8.2.4-A . An additional one foot
of height is allowed above the maximum permitted
height for posts, columns, or light fixtures.
