OPEN SPACES
Open spaces are accessory areas on a lot that 
are open to the sky and designed to provide active 
or passive, public or private, outdoor recreation, 
education, cultivation, beautification, or entertainment. 
Any property may provide an open space. Some 
development may require the utilization of open 
spaces.
8.6.1 General Standards
A. Prohibited Uses within Open 
Spaces
Open spaces shall remain free of driveways, 
parking spaces, garage entrances, loading berths, 
exhaust vents, mechanical equipment, or refuse and 
recycling storage. 
B. Landscape and Hardscape 
Standards
The types of open space shall dictate how much of 
the area should be reserved for landscaping versus 
hardscaping. Asphalt may not be used as a surface 
material within any open space type provided in this 
Section.
C. Front Yard Setback Exemption
In the event that a property provides an open 
space type as defined within, in the front yard of the 
property, the principal building type associated with 
the property shall be exempt from any maximum

ARTICLE 8: SITE AND LANDSCAPING STANDARDS
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 191
Planned Developments
ARTICLE 8
Section 8.7
PLANNED DEVELOPMENTS
As defined in Section 2.3, a planned development is 
any development involving the construction or creation 
of two or more principal buildings on a single lot.
8.7.1 General Standards
A. Approval
A planned development shall be permitted if it meets 
the requirements of this Section and is approved 
by the Planning Board pursuant to the Manchester 
Subdivision and Site Plan Review Regulations.
B. Manufactured Housing Parks
This Section shall not apply to Manufactured Housing 
Parks, which shall comply with the requirements of 
Section 8.8.1 Manufactured Housing Parks.
C. Building Types
Planned developments shall only include such 
building types as are permitted in the district. Houses, 
Duplexes, Triple-Deckers, and Apartment Houses 
shall not be permitted in planned developments with 
more than two principal structures.
D. Mixed-Use Developments
1. Mixed-Use Development Required. Within the 
MX-2, Downtown (DT), Millyard, Innovation, and 
Business Corridor (BC) Districts, any planned 
development with a starting tract of over five acres 
shall include a minimum of one mixed-use or non￾residential building type.
2. Non-Residential First Floor Required. Within 
the BC-2, Downtown (DT), and Millyard Districts, 
planned developments containing a mixture 
of residential and nonresidential uses are not 
permitted to have buildings that contain residential 
dwelling, rooming, or lodging uses on the first floor. 
E. Underground Utilities
Planned developments with more than two principal 
structures shall install all utilities underground.
8.7.2 Building Siting Standards
A. Lot Area
The minimum lot area required for the total site shall 
be determined by totaling the lot areas required for 
each individual principal structure, including the 
additional lot requirements based on the number of 
dwelling units in each principal structure.
B. Setbacks and Buffers
1. Front Yard. The front yard setback shall be 
determined by the type of building closest to the 
street. The maximum front yard setback, if any, shall 
be applied to a minimum of one principal building on 
the property. All other principal buildings shall not 
need to adhere to the maximum setback.
2. Side and Rear Yards. For parcels that are less 
than five acres, the rear yard setback of the district 
shall apply to all side and rear lot lines. Parcels of five 
acres in size or greater shall adhere to the following 
buffer regulations in place of the normal side and rear 
setbacks:
a. For parcels that are five acres up to 25 acres 
shall have a 30-foot buffer.
b. For parcels with more than 25 acres up to 50 
acres shall have a 40-foot buffer.
c. For parcels with more than 50 acres shall have 
a 50-foot buffer. 
d. Such buffers shall exclude all structures, other 
than fences and necessary utility equipment, and 
impervious surfaces.
3. Separation from Other Buildings. All principal 
buildings shall be separated by a minimum distance 
of 20 feet.
C. Lot Frontage
The minimum lot frontage shall be the greater of 
100 feet or the minimum lot frontage required for the 
largest principal building on the lot. For corner lots, 
the principal frontage shall be determined by the 
orientation of the primary façade of the building.
D. Primary Façades of Buildings
The primary façade of any principal building within 
20 feet of a public street shall face the street.

Manufactured Housing
ARTICLE 8
Section 8.8
MANUFACTURED HOUSING
8.8.1 Manufactured Housing
Parks
A. Purpose
It is the purpose of these regulations to provide 
for reasonable opportunities for the siting of 
manufactured housing consistent with RSA 674:32, 
to provide suitable and affordable living environments 
in manufactured housing parks, and to ensure 
the compatibility of such parks with other forms of 
adjacent development.
B. Minimum Standards for Park 
Development
The following define the minimum standards for the 
establishment of a manufactured housing park:
1. Land Area. The minimum land area for the 
establishment of a manufactured housing park 
shall be 20 acres, with access to the tract from an 
accepted city street. The expansion of an existing 
manufactured housing park having less than the 
minimum tract area required by this section, may be 
authorized by a Conditional Use permit, provided that 
the development can conform to all other standards 
for park development in this Section.
2. Density. The maximum density of a manufactured 
housing park shall not exceed five units per gross 
acre.
3. Minimum Number of Sites or Spaces. The 
minimum number of spaces required to comprise 
a manufactured housing park shall be 30 sites or 
spaces, which shall be completed and ready for 
occupancy before the first occupancy is permitted.
4. Height. The maximum height for all structures 
within a manufactured housing park shall be 25 feet.
5. Buffers to Surrounding Property. A landscaped 
buffer not less than 25 feet in width may be required 
by the Planning Board along streets and park 
boundaries. Such buffer may be used for drainage 
structures and utilities easements but shall not be 
used for any other purpose. The buffer area shall be 
landscaped so as to provide effective screening year 
round.
6. Recreation Area and Facilities. Not less than 
eight percent of the gross land area of the park 
shall be developed for recreational purposes. No 
manufactured home site, required buffer strip, 
street right-of-way, storage area, utility site, or utility 
easement shall be counted as recreation area in 
meeting this requirement. Recreation areas and 
facilities shall be owned and maintained by the park 
owner, or by the community association or owners 
association as the context requires.
C. Minimum Standards for 
Development of Lots, Sites, or 
Spaces Within Park
The minimum standards contained within Article 
5: Building and Lot Standards, as to minimum 
lot size, setbacks, yards, and height shall not be 
applied within a manufactured housing park. The 
following standards shall apply to the development 
of individual lots, sites or spaces for manufactured 
housing within a park:
1. Minimum Area. The lot, site, or space designated 
for the placement of a manufactured home shall be a 
minimum of 6,000 square feet with a minimum width 
of at least 60 feet. Sites at street intersections may 
be required by the Planning Board to have wider lots 
in order to provide adequate sight distance for safety 
at intersections.
2. Minimum Setbacks. No manufactured home, 
carport or other structure shall be placed or erected 
closer to the pavement line or internal roadway than 
15 feet. No manufactured home shall be placed 
or erected closer than five feet to any side or rear 
manufactured home site line, and not closer than 50 
feet to any park property line.
3. Maximum Coverage. The total impervious 
coverage of a manufactured home site shall not 
exceed 40 percent of the area of the site.
4. HUD Code Compliance. Individual manufactured 
housing units shall comply with the construction and 
installation provisions of the National Manufactured 
Home Construction and Safety Standards Act (42 
U.S.C. Sec. 5401), commonly known as the HUD 
(United States Department of Housing and Urban 
Development) code, as well as all applicable city 
codes and ordinances. No additions shall be 
permitted to manufactured homes that are not in 
compliance with the HUD code.
5. Foundation System. Each manufactured 
housing unit shall be placed on a properly engineered 
foundation system that meets the manufacturer’s 
installation requirements and applicable city codes.

Manufactured Housing
A properly engineered foundation is one that 
provides adequate support of the home’s vertical 
and horizontal loads and transfers these and other 
imposed forces, without failure, from the home to the 
undisturbed ground below the frost line.
6. Parking. The number of off-street parking spaces 
for each home shall be that which is required 
by Table 7.2-A Off-Street Parking Requirements
under Manufactured Housing Park. The parking of 
recreational vehicles, boats and the like shall not be 
permitted within individual manufactured home sites. 
Such vehicles shall be parked in a central storage 
area designed and designated for such purpose. 
D. Accessory Uses and Buildings
The Planning Board may approve such accessory 
uses and structures that are determined to 
be accessory and clearly subordinate to the 
manufactured housing park where such uses 
are to be located on the same lot or parcel as the 
manufactured home park, and are not of a nature 
likely to attract visitors in larger numbers than would 
normally be expected in a single family residential 
neighborhood. The following are considered to be 
accessory uses:
1. Park recreation facilities including community 
room or center, courts for games, playgrounds, 
docks, boat launching area and the like but excluding 
facilities for boat repairs;
2. Park offices, maintenance facilities and laundry 
facilities;
3. Day care for tenants of park;
4. Recreational vehicle and boat storage areas;
5. Other uses determined by the Planning Board 
that provide services or convenience to the residents 
of the park which are found to be compatible with a 
residential development.
No accessory building housing such facilities shall 
be located closer than 100 feet to any public street. 
Any such building shall be accessible only from the 
private streets within the park.
E. Internal Private Streets and 
Circulation
All streets within a manufactured housing park shall 
be privately owned and maintained, and adequately 
drained. Access shall be designed for safe and 
convenient movement of traffic into and out of the 
park. The minimum pavement width for the private 
streets within a park shall be:
1. Internal collector street: 26 feet;
2. Divided roadway: 20 feet for each direction of travel, 
with a landscaped median not less than six feet in width; 
3. Internal minor streets: 22 feet for two way traffic, or 
20 feet for one way traffic.
F. Utilities
The minimum standards for the installation of utilities 
within a manufactured housing park shall be:
1. Lighting. Street lighting shall be installed which may 
be overhead or low level; the source of light shall not 
be visible beyond park boundaries and all light shall be 
reflected onto the internal private streets or pedestrian 
ways.
2. Water and Sewer. Each manufactured home site 
shall be connected to public water and sewer systems, 
or to state-approved central community water supply 
and sewage disposal systems. No individual water 
supply or sewage disposal system shall be permitted in 
a manufactured housing park.
3. Underground Placement. All utility distribution and 
collection systems, including those for water, sewer, 
electricity, telephone, and gas shall be underground.
G. Limitation on Signs
The following standards shall govern and limit the 
placement of all signs within a manufactured housing 
park:
1. One freestanding sign, which may have two faces, 
at each entrance of the manufactured housing park, to 
identify the park. Such sign shall contain only the name 
of the park and address and shall not exceed 18 square 
feet in area per face.
2. One wall sign per park accessory facility not to 
exceed 12 square feet.
3. No sign shall be erected within 20 feet of any adjacent 
property nor shall it be illuminated.
8.8.2 Manufactured Housing
Subdivisions
In order to provide reasonable opportunities for the 
placement of manufactured housing, in compliance with 
RSA 674:32, within parks and subdivisions dedicated 
exclusively to the placement of such homes, this 
section provides supplementary standards applicable 
to subdivisions to create lots reserved exclusively for 
the placement of manufactured homes to be owned

ARTICLE 8
individually by their occupants. Where authorized by 
Table 4.3-A, Principal Uses, manufactured housing 
subdivisions may be established, provided that such 
developments comply with all of the requirements 
normally pertaining to single family housing 
subdivisions in the same zoning district, and subject 
to the following additional requirements:
A. Minimum Tract Area
The minimum tract area for a manufactured housing 
subdivision shall be 20 acres.
B. HUD Code Compliance
Individual manufactured housing units shall comply 
with the construction and installation of manufactured 
housing units pursuant to the National Manufactured 
Home Construction and Safety Standards Act 
(42 U.S.C. Sec. 5401), commonly known as the 
HUD code, as well as all applicable city codes 
and ordinances. No additions shall be permitted to 
manufactured homes that are not in compliance with 
the HUD code.
C. Foundation System
Each manufactured housing unit shall be placed 
on a properly engineered foundation system that 
meets the manufacturer’s installation requirements 
and applicable city codes. A properly engineered 
foundation is one that provides adequate support 
of the home’s vertical and horizontal loads and 
transfers these and other imposed forces, without 
failure, from the home to the undisturbed ground 
below the frost line.
D. Restrictive Covenants
Restrictive deed covenants acceptable to the 
Planning Board shall be attached to the deeds of each 
lot in such a subdivision, the effect of which shall be 
to limit their use to the placement of manufactured 
housing units meeting the standards of this section. 
This requirement is intended to create a subdivision 
development of consistent structural types and 
compatible development limited to manufactured 
homes.
Section 8.9
EXCAVATION OF EARTH 
MATERIALS 
8.9.1 General Provisions
A. Authority
These regulations governing the excavation of 
earth materials are adopted in accordance with 
the provisions of RSA 155-E, Local Regulation 
Excavations. Pursuant to RSA 155-E, the Planning 
Board is designated as “regulator” and is authorized 
to administer and grant Conditional Use permits 
in accordance with Article 10: Administration, 
Procedures, and Enforcement, of this Ordinance.
B. Purpose
These regulations are adopted for the following 
purposes:
1. To provide reasonable opportunities for the 
excavation of earth materials;
2. To minimize safety hazards which can be created 
by open excavations;
3. To ensure that the public health and welfare will 
be safeguarded;
4. To protect the City’s natural resources and 
environmental quality; and
5. To maintain the aesthetic features of the City.
C. Excavation Permit 
Requirements
All excavations require the issuance of a Conditional 
Use permit from the Planning Board except those 
excavations that are specifically exempted from 
permit requirements pursuant to RSA 155-E. Any 
permit granted by the Planning Board pursuant 
to this Section shall be valid for a period not to 
exceed three years, and shall not be assignable or 
transferable without the approval of the Planning 
Board. The Conditional Use permit shall constitute 
the excavation permit required under RSA 155-E. All 
applications shall comply with the requirements of 
this Ordinance and RSA 155-E.
D. Exempt Excavations
Pursuant to RSA 155-E:2 and 155-E:2-a, no permit 
shall be required for the following types of excavation:
1. Existing Excavations and Stationary Manufacturing 
Plants, as set forth in RSA 155-E:2.

ARTICLE 8: SITE AND LANDSCAPING STANDARDS
196 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE
Excavation of Earth Materials
2. Excavations performed exclusively for construction 
of Class I, II, III, IV or V Highway, as set forth in RSA 
155-E:2. 
3. Excavation that is exclusively incidental to the 
construction or alteration of a building or structure 
or the construction or alteration of a parking lot or 
way including a driveway on a portion of the premises 
where the removal occurs; provided, however, that 
no such excavation shall be commenced without a 
permit under this chapter unless all state and local 
permits required for the construction or alteration of 
the building, structure, parking lot, or way have been 
issued.
4. Excavation that is incidental to agricultural or 
silvicultural activities, normal landscaping, or minor 
topographical adjustment.
5. Excavation from a granite quarry for the purpose 
of producing dimension stone, if such excavation 
requires a permit under RSA 12-E.
6. A person owning land abutting a site which 
was taken by eminent domain or by any other 
governmental taking upon which construction is 
taking place may stockpile earth taken from the 
construction site and may remove the earth at a later 
date after written notification to the appropriate local 
official.
E. Prohibited Excavations
The Planning Board shall not grant a permit for the 
following projects:
1. For excavations within 50 feet of the boundary of a 
disapproving abutter or within 10 feet of an approving 
abutter unless approval is requested by said abutter.
2. Where existing visual barriers to public highways 
would be removed, except to provide access to the 
excavation.
3. Where the issuance of the permit would be unduly 
hazardous or injurious to the public welfare due to 
such factors as noise, traffic, dust, fumes, or danger 
from operations.
4. Where the excavation would substantially damage 
a known aquifer, as designated by the United States 
Geological Survey.
5. When the excavation cannot receive necessary 
approvals from state or federal agencies, such as 
Alteration of Terrain or Wetlands permits.
6. Where the excavation is not permitted by zoning 
or other applicable ordinances, provided, however, 
that reasonable opportunities for excavation exist in 
town, as described in RSA 155-E:4,III.
7. Where the project cannot comply with the 
requirements of RSA 155-E:4-a, 155-E:5 and 
155-E:5-a.
F. Definition
Earth: sand, gravel, rock, soil or construction 
aggregate produced by quarrying, crushing or any 
other mining activity or such other naturally-occurring 
unconsolidated materials that normally mask the 
bedrock, per RSA 155-E:1, as amended.
Excavation: a land area which is used, or has been 
used, for the commercial taking of earth, including all 
slopes, per RSA 155-E:1, as amended.
Excavation Area: the surface area within an 
excavation site where excavation has occurred or is 
eligible to occur under the provisions of this chapter, 
per RSA 155-E:1, as amended.
Excavation Site: any area of contiguous land in 
common ownership upon which excavation takes 
place, per RSA 155-E:1, as amended.
8.9.2 Application for a
Conditional Use Permit for an
Excavation
An application for a Conditional Use permit for an 
excavation shall be filed with the Planning Board 
pursuant to Section 10.1.2 Application and Review 
Procedure, of this Ordinance. When the scope of 
an existing permitted excavation is proposed to be 
altered so as to affect the size or location of the 
excavation, the rate of removal of earth, or the plan 
for restoration, an application shall be submitted for 
amendment of the existing excavation permit. An 
application for amendment shall be subject to the 
same requirements and approval procedures as 
provided herein for a new excavation permit. 
A. Application Requirements
In addition to the requirements of Article 
10:Administration, Procedures, and Enforcement
of this Ordinance, and pursuant to RSA 155-E:3, all 
applications shall include the following:
1. An Excavation Plan, prepared by a Licensed Civil 
Engineer, including the following information:
a. The name and address of the owner of the land

198 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE
Excavation of Earth Materials
8.9.3 Operational Standards for
Excavations
A. Minimum Operational Standards 
In accordance with RSA 155-E:4-a, the following 
minimum operational standards shall apply to all 
excavations requiring a permit and all exempt 
excavations:
1. No excavation shall be permitted below road 
level within 50 feet of the right-of-way of any public 
highway as defined in RSA 229:1, unless such 
excavation is for the purpose of said highway. 
2. No excavation shall be permitted within:
a. 50 feet of the boundary of a disapproving 
abutter;
b. 150 feet of any dwelling which either existed or 
for which a building permit has been issued at the 
time the excavation is commenced; 
c. 75 feet of any great pond, navigable river, or any 
other standing body of water ten acres or more in 
area; or;
d. 25 feet of any other stream, river, or brook 
which normally flows throughout the year, or any 
naturally occurring standing body of water less 
than ten acres, prime wetland as designated in 
accordance with RSA 482-A:15, I., or any other 
wetland greater than five acres in area as defined 
by the NH Department of Environmental Services.
3. Vegetation shall be maintained or provided 
within the peripheral areas specified in Section
8.9.3.A.1 and 8.9.3.A.2.a and b.
4. Drainage shall be maintained so as to prevent 
the accumulation of free-standing water for 
prolonged periods. Excavation practices which 
result in continued siltation of surface waters or 
any degradation of water quality of any public or 
private water supplies are prohibited.
5. No fuels, lubricants, or other toxic or polluting 
materials shall be stored on-site unless in 
compliance with state laws or rules pertaining to 
such materials.
6. Where temporary slopes will exceed a grade 
of 1:1, a fence or other suitable barricade shall be 
erected to warn of danger or limit access to the 
site.
7. Prior to the removal of topsoil or other 
overburden material from any land area that has 
not yet been excavated, the excavator shall file a 
reclamation bond or other security as prescribed 
by the Planning Board, sufficient to secure the 
reclamation of the land area to be excavated.
8. Nothing in this Section shall be deemed to 
supersede or pre-empt applicable environmental 
standards or permit requirements contained in 
State laws, and no exemption under this regulation 
shall be construed as an exemption from any State 
statute.
B. Additional City Operational 
Standards
The following additional city standards shall apply 
only to those excavations requiring a permit: 
1. All property corners shall be staked and every 
property line shall be clearly marked at 100-
foot intervals to prevent encroachment of the 
excavation operations on abutting property;
2. All loam and topsoil to be stripped from the 
excavation site shall be stockpiled on the property to 
be replaced during reclamation;
3. No excavation shall exceed five acres at any 
one time;
4. No equipment or vehicles shall be operated 
prior to 7:00 AM or after 7:00 p.m. Monday 
through Saturday, or at any time on Sunday or 
holidays;
5. All vehicles transporting excavated material 
shall utilize dust covers and/or sideboards to 
prevent any spillage and dust;
6. Spilled material shall be cleaned from all 
streets on hauling routes at the end of each day;
7. No excavation shall be conducted within 100 
feet of a surface water body or watercourse, or a 
wetland and;
8. No excavation shall exceed a depth of four 
feet above the annual average water table, 
except that, pursuant to RSA 155-E:11, II., an 
exception to such prohibition shall be granted 
if the applicant demonstrates to the Planning 
Boards’s satisfaction that excavation below this 
height will not adversely affect water quality 
and quantity. Written notice of such exception 
shall be recorded at the HCRD at the applicant’s 
expense and one copy shall be filed with the NH 
Department of Environmental Services.

ARTICLE 8
8.9.4 Reclamation Standards for
Excavations
A. Minimum Reclamation 
Standards 
In accordance with RSA 155-E:5, the following 
minimum reclamation standards shall apply to all 
excavations requiring a permit, and all exempt 
excavations, and shall be met within 12 months after 
the expiration date of a permit issued under this 
Section, or within 12 months of the completion of any 
excavation: 
1. Except for exposed rock ledge, all areas which 
have been affected by the excavation or otherwise 
stripped of vegetation shall be spread with topsoil 
or strippings, if any, but in any case covered by 
soil capable of sustaining vegetation, and shall be 
planted with seedlings or grass suitable to prevent 
erosion. Areas visible from a public way, from 
which trees have been removed, shall be replanted 
with tree seedlings, set out in accordance with 
acceptable horticultural practices.
2. Earth and vegetative debris resulting from the 
excavation shall be removed or otherwise lawfully 
disposed of.
3. All slopes, except for exposed ledge, shall be 
graded to natural repose for the type of soil of which 
they are composed so as to control erosion or at a 
ratio of horizontal to vertical proposed by the owner 
and approved by the Planning Board. Changes of 
slope shall not be abrupt, but shall blend with the 
surrounding terrain.
4. The elimination of any standing bodies of water 
created in the excavation project as may constitute 
a hazard to health and safety.
5. The topography of the land shall be left so that 
water draining from the site leaves the property 
at the original, natural drainage points and in the 
natural proportions of flow. For excavation projects 
which require an Alteration of Terrain permit from 
the department of environmental services pursuant 
to RSA 485-A:17, the provisions of that statute, 
and rules adopted under it, shall supersede this 
paragraph as to areas of excavation sites covered 
thereby. The excavator shall file a copy of permits 
issued under RSA 485-A:17 with the Planning 
Board.
B. Additional City Reclamation 
Standards
The following additional city standards shall apply 
only to those excavations requiring a permit: 
1. Reclamation shall be initiated prior to the 
excavation of more than five acres of the site at any 
one time.
2. All debris shall be removed and all stumps 
shall be chipped or removed from the site, and 
disposed in accordance with applicable statutes 
and regulations. All rocks are to be removed, 
buried, or used for landscaping in accordance 
with the restoration plans.
3. No slope shall be left steeper than three feet 
horizontally for each one foot of vertical change 
unless it can be demonstrated by the applicant

B. Performance Guarantee 8.9.8 Abandoned Excavations
A permit shall not become effective until the applicant Pursuant to RSA 155-E, the Planning Board may
furnishes the City with a performance guarantee in initiate proceedings to secure the reclamation of an
a form satisfactory to the City Solicitor, and in an abandoned excavation.
amount based on the cost of restoration as estimated
by the Department of Public Works. The guarantee
shall have a term of one year in excess of the period
of validity of the permit, and shall remain in effect for
the full term unless exercised by the City or released
in writing by the Director.
8.9.6 Inspections and
Enforcement
A. Inspections
The Director shall have the right to enter upon the
property for a period beginning with the date of the
granting of the permit and ending one year after the
expiration of the permit to inspect the excavation and
reclamation operations and to ensure compliance
with the terms and conditions of the permit. The
Director may suspend operations found to be in
violation of a permit pending a hearing by the
Planning Board concerning any violation.
B. Compliance Hearing
Upon recommendation of the Director, or the receipt
of a valid complaint which in the opinion of the
Planning Board warrants investigation and a hearing,
the Planning Board may order a public hearing to
review the conditions of, or the extent of compliance
with, a permit. After a hearing, an excavation permit
may be modified or revoked by the Planning Board
if the Board finds that the operation is being carried
on in violation of any of the terms and conditions
of the permit. The modification or revocation of a
permit shall not relieve the applicant from any of their
obligations under the permit.
8.9.7 Appeal of Decision of the
Planning Board
Following the approval, disapproval, modification of
approval, or revocation of approval of an excavation
permit, any interested person may seek a rehearing
or appeal the decision of the Planning Board in
accordance with the provisions of RSA 155-E.

Section 9.1
GENERAL PROVISIONS
9.1.1 Purpose and Intent
The purpose of this Article is to regulate the display
of signs on privately owned property in a manner
that promotes the public interest in safety and
aesthetics, while maintaining neutrality as to the
content of speech. This Article is further intended to:
A. Communication and Navigation
Encourage the effective use of signs as a means of
communication and facilitate navigation from place
to place within the City;
B. Aesthetic Environment and
Economic Development
Maintain and enhance the aesthetic environment of
the City while retaining the City’s ability to attract and
encourage economic development;
C. Pedestrian and Traffic Safety
Improve pedestrian and traffic safety by eliminating
potential hazards;
D. Adverse Effects
Minimize possible adverse effects of signs on nearby
public and private property by eliminating excessive
and confusing sign displays;
E. Enforcement
Enable fair and consistent enforcement of these sign
regulations; and
F. Property Value
Safeguard property values by minimizing the possible
adverse effects of signs on nearby properties.
9.1.2 Permit Required
Except as otherwise provided in this Article, no sign
may be erected, placed, replaced, moved, enlarged,
illuminated, or substantially altered without a permit
in accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance.
A. Filing of Permit and Fee
A permit application and fee shall be submitted to
the Director and shall include a set of plans at an
appropriate scale showing the location, size, method

records.text:
ARTICLE 9: SIGN STANDARDS
A. Plot Plan
Where freestanding signs are proposed, an accurate
plan of the lot, to scale, showing the location of
buildings, parking areas, driveways, and landscaped
areas shall be submitted.
B. Inventory of Existing and
Proposed Signs
An accurate representation, by photograph or plan,
of the location of all existing and proposed signs.
Inventory information shall include sign type, size,
height above ground, materials, and method of
illumination.
C. Proposed Sign Measurements
and Features
An accurate representation of the sign type, size,
height above ground, materials and method of
illumination and attachment for all proposed signs.
9.1.4 Maintenance
All signs shall be maintained in good repair (e.g.,
without peeling paint or broken sign faces) and in
operable condition (e.g., if internally illuminated, all
light bulbs or tubes shall be operational) at all times.
The City may order the removal of any sign which
becomes a public hazard due to lack of maintenance
and repair.
9.1.5 Non-conforming Signs
A non-conforming sign that was lawfully established
and maintained in compliance with the provisions of
all applicable laws in effect at the time of original
installation, but that does not now comply with
the provisions of this Ordinance, may be repaired
subject to these additional regulations.
A. Compliance of Repairs
No non-conforming sign may be altered in any way
in structure or material, or re-located to a position,
that makes the sign less in compliance with the
requirements of this Ordinance than it was before
the alteration or relocation.
GENERAL PROVISIONS
B. Extent of Destruction
Should a nonconforming sign be destroyed by any
means to an extent of more than 75 percent of its
replacement cost at the time of its destruction, it
shall not be reconstructed except in conformity with
the provisions of this Ordinance.
9.1.6 Required Vegetation
Trees, shrubs, or other vegetation required by this
Ordinance shall not be destroyed or removed for
the purpose of installing, increasing, or enhancing
the visibility of any sign, unless replaced in-kind
elsewhere on the property.
9.1.7 Location
A. On the Principal Lot
A permanent sign, except for off-premises signs,
shall be located on the same site as the subject of
the sign.
B. Minimum Setbacks
The minimum setback for any freestanding sign shall
be five feet from any property line.
C. Signs on Public Property
No sign, other than signs placed by agencies of
government with appropriate jurisdiction, or a sign
whose placement is authorized by such agencies,
may be erected or placed on public property,
including rights-of-way.
D. Clear Sight Area
No sign may be installed in a way that obstructs free
and clear vision, clear sight area per Section 8.4,
Visibility at Intersections , or free use of any public
right-of-way, intersection, ingress or egress point,
transit stop, parking space, drive aisle, driveway,
building entrance, fire escape, or accessibility ramp.
E. Obstruction
No sign may obstruct or substantially interfere with
any window, door, fire escape, stairway, ladder, or
any other opening or structure intended to provide
ingress or egress to any building.

9.1.8 Illumination, Excluding
EMCs
Signs other than EMCs may be, but are not required
to be, illuminated unless otherwise specifically
stated for the particular sign type in Section 9.8,
Building Sign Types and Section 9.9, Freestanding
Sign Types .
A. External Illumination
External illumination shall be shielded so that it
illuminates only the sign surface and does not shine
on, cause glare to, or otherwise impair the vision of
the driver of any motor vehicle traveling on a public
right-of-way.
B. Internal Illumination
Internal illumination of a sign shall be equipped with
the ability to adjust the brightness of the sign and shall
not be operated at a brightness that is substantially
greater than other sources of illumination in the area.
C. Colored Lights
Colored lights shall not be used at a location or in a
manner so as to be confused with or construed as a
traffic control device.

EXEMPT SIGNS

requirements of Section 9.1.2 Permit Required , but
are subject to the standards contained herein. Any
failure to comply with these standards and any other
provisions of this Article shall be considered a violation

A sign that identifies the address of a lot, structure,
or establishment, provided it does not exceed two
square feet in area for a lot with only a residential
use or four square feet in area for a lot with non-
residential uses.

Signs
Signs erected by, or on behalf of, or pursuant to

1. Traffic, directional, or warning information;

danger;

in the performance of their public duty which aid E
L
service or safety;
C

T

A

by government order or regulations, provided that the
content and size thereof does not exceed that required

ARTICLE 9: SIGN STANDARDS
9.2.4 Flags
A flag shall be attached to a flag pole that is
permanently anchored to the ground. Within any
Residential (R) zoning district, the maximum
number of flags shall not exceed two flags, with the
maximum area of a flag not to exceed 15 square
feet. In all other districts, the maximum number of
flags shall not exceed three flags, with the maximum
area of a flag not to exceed 60 square feet.
9.2.5 Fuel Pump or EVC Signs
A sign that is attached or adhered to a fuel pump or
Electric Vehicle Charging Station (EVC). This sign
may not exceed two square feet in area per side
of the pump or station. Operational and payment
instructions on the face of the pump or charging
station are exempt from this limitation.
9.2.6 Drive-Through Signs
A drive-through sign is a permanently mounted sign
located proximate to a drive-through lane at a drive-
through facility, only as permitted as an accessory
use per Table 4.5-A, Accessory Uses .
A. Standards
1. Drive-through signs shall only be permitted in
conjunction with a permitted drive-through use.
2. A maximum of two drive-through signs are
permitted per drive-through lane.
3. A drive-through sign may not exceed 48 square
feet in area or eight feet in height above grade.
9.2.7 Parking, Directional, or
Informational Sign
Incidental parking signs that provide additional
direction or information, such as signs marking
entrances and exits, parking areas, circulation
direction, restroom, and pick-up or delivery areas,
may be on a building or freestanding provided they
comply with the following standards.
A. Standards
1. No more than two signs per driveway or one sign
per critical turning point (e.g., to direct vehicular traffic
to a drive-through window, loading area, etc);
2. Each sign shall not exceed four square feet in
surface area;
3. Freestanding parking lot directional and information
signs located within the clear sight area shall be limited
to three feet in height; and
EXEMPT SIGNS
4. All signs within the R and MX districts shall be non-
illuminated.
9.2.8 Construction Signs
Signs posted on the fencing surrounding active
construction sites. These signs shall be related to
on-premises activities only and shall be removed
after construction has ended.
9.2.9 Temporary Signs
A sign that is used in connection with a circumstance,
situation, or event that is designed, intended, or
expected to take place or to be completed within
a reasonably short or definite period of time after
the erection of the sign; or a sign that is intended to
remain on the location where it is erected or placed
for a reasonably short or definite period of time after
the erection of the sign. If the sign display area is
permanent but the message displayed is subject to
periodic changes, that sign shall not be regarded as
a temporary sign. Temporary signs are allowed in all
districts and may be either a freestanding or building
sign.
A. Standards
1. Not more than four such signs may be located on
any lot;
2. No such sign may exceed four square feet in
surface area;
3. Such a sign may not be displayed for longer
than 10 days after the expiration of the temporary
circumstance, situation, or event; and
4. The signs shall not be illuminated.
9.2.10 Murals
A mural is any pictorial image or graphic, not including
letters or numbers, directly painted to an integral
surface of an exterior wall of a building. A mural shall
not include images or graphics that are applied to a
separate material that is affixed to a wall and is not
an integral part of a wall. Murals are only permitted in
the BC, Millyard, DT, ID, and IND Districts. If a mural
contains letters or numbers, those letters or numbers
shall be considered a wall sign and added to the total
sign surface area pursuant to Section 9.6.1 Building
Sign Surface Area . Sign area of letters and numbers
shall be calculated as the total area of a rectangle that
encompasses each series of letters and numbers.
Letters or numbers printed at a size smaller than four
inches in height shall be considered de minimis and
not included in total sign surface area.

PROHIBITED OR LIMITED SIGNS
Section 9.3
PROHIBITED OR LIMITED
SIGNS
These signs are either expressly prohibited city-wide
or prohibited unless they adhere to specific standards
and are erected in limited commercial areas within
the City. Any sign type not expressly allowed by this
Ordinance is prohibited.
9.3.1 Types of Prohibited Signs
A. Prohibited City-Wide
1. Signs which interfere with, obstruct the view of,
imitate, copy, purport to be, or may be confused with
any authorized official sign, traffic sign, traffic signal, or
traffic control device;
2. Beacons, rotating beams, intermittent light, lights
of changing colors or degrees of intensity, or flashing
illumination, or any light with one or more beams
directed into the atmosphere or one or more points not
on the same property as the light source, except as
part of an electronic message center sign;
3. Inflated signs and tethered balloons;
4. On corner lots, signs which obscure the vision of
drivers and create a potential safety hazard;
5. Signs attached to a tree, street light, utility pole,
rock, or fence, except as permitted by Section 9.2.8
Construction Signs ; and
6. Signs on a building blocking windows.
9.3.2 Types of Signs with Limited
Applications
A. Electronic Message Centers
(EMCs)
Any sign that uses computer-generated messages
or some other electronic means of changing copy.
These signs include displays using incandescent
lamps, LEDs, LCDs, or a flipper matrix. EMCs are
prohibited unless they comply with the following
regulations:
1. EMCs are permitted in all districts for Civic principal
uses, pursuant to Table 4.3-A, Principal Uses. Such
EMCs shall not exceed 32 square feet in area, shall
not engage in off-premise advertising, and shall be
limited to the sign types permitted in the district.
ARTICLE 9: SIGN STANDARDS
2. EMCs are otherwise only permitted within the BC-2
and IND districts;
3. EMCs located within any Residential (R) District
or Mixed-Use (MX) District shall not be illuminated
between the hours of 10 pm and 7 am ;
4. All EMCs shall be equipped with a sensor or other
device that automatically determines the ambient
illumination and programmed to automatically dim
according to ambient light conditions;
5. No EMC shall exceed 0.3 foot-candles above
ambient lighting conditions as measured at a distance
that is equal to the square root of the product of the
area of the EMC multiplied by 100;
6. All messages shall be static and displayed for a
minimum of eight seconds;
7. Any change in an electronic message shall be
instantaneous without fading in, dropping in, spinning,
rotating, or similar moving copy changes;
8. Full-motion video display is prohibited;
9. Any EMC that is malfunctioning shall be turned off
until such time that it is functioning properly;
10. An EMC is prohibited from being displayed on a
motorized vehicle parked on a lot; and
11. The total surface area of an EMC shall be counted
towards the total sign allotment for the property.
B. Off-Premises Signs
9
Any sign erected, maintained, or used for the
E
purpose of the display of messages relating to an
L
activity, business, or product sold at a location other
C
than the premises on which the sign is located. Off- I
T
premises signs are prohibited unless they comply
R
with the following regulations:
A
1. Off-premises signs shall only be permitted in the
BC-2 District;
2. Off-premises signs shall be limited to freestanding
signs; and
3. The total surface area of an off-premise sign shall
be counted towards the total sign allotment for the
property on which it is located.
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 207

not engage in off-premise advertising, and shall be 
limited to the sign types permitted in the district.
2. EMCs are otherwise only permitted within the BC-2 
and IND districts;
3. EMCs located within any Residential (R) District 
or Mixed-Use (MX) District shall not be illuminated 
between the hours of 10 pm and 7 am;

device that automatically determines the ambient 
illumination and programmed to automatically dim 
according to ambient light conditions;

ambient lighting conditions as measured at a distance 
that is equal to the square root of the product of the 
area of the EMC multiplied by 100;

minimum of eight seconds;
7. Any change in an electronic message shall be 
instantaneous without fading in, dropping in, spinning, 
rotating, or similar moving copy changes;

until such time that it is functioning properly;
10. An EMC is prohibited from being displayed on a 
motorized vehicle parked on a lot; and
11. The total surface area of an EMC shall be counted 
towards the total sign allotment for the property. 
B. Off-Premises Signs
Any sign erected, maintained, or used for the 
purpose of the display of messages relating to an 
activity, business, or product sold at a location other 
than the premises on which the sign is located. Off-premises signs are prohibited unless they comply 
with the following regulations:
1. Off-premises signs shall only be permitted in the 
BC-2 District;
2. Off-premises signs shall be limited to freestanding 
signs; and
3. The total surface area of an off-premise sign shall 
be counted towards the total sign allotment for the 
property on which it is located.

or prohibited unless they adhere to specific standards
and are erected in limited commercial areas within
the City. Any sign type not expressly allowed by this

A. Prohibited City-Wide

imitate, copy, purport to be, or may be confused with
any authorized official sign, traffic sign, traffic signal, or
traffic control device;

of changing colors or degrees of intensity, or flashing
illumination, or any light with one or more beams

on the same property as the light source, except as
part of an electronic message center sign;

drivers and create a potential safety hazard;

Construction Signs ; and

ARTICLE 9: SIGN STANDARDS
SIGN MEASUREMENTS
[IMAGE]
Section 9.4
SIGN MEASUREMENTS
9.4.1 Surface Area
Unless otherwise stated, sign surface area is
calculated as the height of the sign multiplied by
the width of the sign. Sign surface area shall be
measured as follows:
A. Signs on a Background
The entire area of the framework or background of
the sign is calculated as sign area, including any
material or color forming the sign face or background
[IMAGE]
used to differentiate the sign from the structure
against which it is placed.
B. Signs with a Base
The base of a monument sign does not count as
sign area if it is less than three feet in height and is
constructed of masonry or a material that matches
the primary building façade material.
C. Individually Mounted Letters or
Features
The sign area is calculated as the total area of each
rectangle that encompasses each word or graphic
[IMAGE]
element. Sign area does not include any supporting
framework or bracing, unless such framework is part
of the message or sign face.
D. Signs on an Awning
The area of awning sign is calculated by drawing the
smallest possible rectangle that encompasses each
word or graphic element on the awning.
E. Two or More Faces
If the sign has two or more faces, the area of all
[IMAGE]
faces is included in determining the area of the sign.
However, if two sign faces are placed back to back,
or at an angle where both faces cannot be viewed
from any point at the same time, and are separated
by a maximum dimension of 42 inches measured
from the furthest points of each of the sign faces,
the sign surface area shall be computed by the
measurement of only one of the sign faces.
208 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE

ARTICLE 9: SIGN STANDARDS
SIGN MEASUREMENTS
9.4.4 Façade Area Calculations
When calculating the area of a façade upon which a
building sign may be placed, the area of the façade
shall be the actual surface area of the façade of the
building or tenant space located above grade and
beneath the top of the wall, not including the roof.
Façade area shall include any two-dimensional area
of the building elevation from which the façade, or
portion thereof, may be viewed. The calculation of
façade area is determined independently for each
façade.

freestanding sign. The sign shall not exceed 20
square feet in surface area or six feet in height, and
shall not be illuminated. Multifamily buildings in all
other districts shall comply with Section 9.6, Non-
Residential Sign Standards.

E
Developments

Any solely residential planned development that C

consists of eight or more dwelling units, including T
manufactured housing parks, is permitted one R

freestanding sign per street frontage. The sign shall
not exceed 20 square feet in surface area or six
feet in height, and shall not be internally illuminated.
Mixed-use planned developments shall comply with
Section 9.6, Non-Residential Sign Standards.

Section 9.6
NON-RESIDENTIAL SIGN 
STANDARDS
The number, height, and total sign surface area per 
street frontage of all signs on a lot designated as 
mixed-use or for any nonresidential use may not 
exceed the maximums allowed within the applicable 
zoning district, as shown in Tables 9.6-A and 9.6-B.
9.6.1 Building Sign Surface Area
The total sign surface area allowed for building signs is 
the sum of the surface areas of all building signs on a 
façade. The total sign surface area shall not exceed the 
maximum allotted percentage of the façade area or total 
square footage of allotted signage per façade, whichever 
is less.

adjacent lots is required.

ARTICLE 9: SIGN STANDARDS
BUILDING SIGN TYPES
Section 9.8
BUILDING SIGN TYPES
A building sign is any sign attached to or supported by
a building. Building signs include, but are not limited to
awning or canopy signs, projecting signs, roof signs,
suspended signs, wall signs, and window signs,
unless otherwise stated. The number of building signs
are unlimited per façade; however, the combined area
of all building signs per street frontage shall comply
with Table 9.6-A: Non-Residential Building Sign
Standards , and meet any of the following standards
specific to the applicable sign type.

records.text:
ARTICLE 9: SIGN STANDARDS
BUILDING SIGN TYPES
[IMAGE]
9.8.3 Roof Signs
A sign mounted on the roof or the uppermost
architectural band of a building.
A. Standards
1. Roof signs are only permitted in the DT and
Millyard districts and shall only be installed on a
building with a flat roof.
2. A maximum of one roof sign is permitted per
building.
3. Roof signs shall not be more than 75 percent
of the building width at the roof level or 15 feet in
height.
4. Roof signs shall not extend below the upper
lintel of windows of the highest story of a building.
5. Roof signs may be internally illuminated.
External illumination is prohibited.
6. Roof signs shall consist of individual
alphanumeric characters or graphic elements.
[IMAGE]
9.8.4 Suspended Signs
A sign that is suspended, hung, or connected to the
underside of a horizontal surface and intended to be
viewed from the sidewalk at close range.
A. Standards
1. A maximum of one suspended sign is permitted
per ground floor establishment, per frontage.
2. Suspended signs shall have a maximum sign
surface area of six square feet.
3. Suspended signs shall have a vertical clearance
of at least eight feet above the finished grade below.
4. Suspended signs may be internally illuminated
within all districts except an R or MX District.
Suspended signs may be externally illuminated.
216 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE

ARTICLE 9: SIGN STANDARDS
BUILDING SIGN TYPES
[IMAGE]
9.8.5 Wall Signs
Any sign attached to, applied to, or mounted on
the wall of a building or structure except murals as
defined in Section 9.2.10 Murals , with the face of the
sign parallel to that of the wall.
A. Standards
1. Wall signs shall not project more than 18 inches
from the wall.
2. Wall signs shall not be more than 80 percent of
the building façade width.
3. No wall sign may extend above the window
sills of the second story, unless the establishment
extends to the second story or above. No portion
of a wall sign may extend above the roofline or
parapet wall of a building with a flat roof or above
the lower eave of a building with a pitched roof.
4. Wall signs may be internally or externally
illuminated.
[IMAGE]
9.8.6 Window Signs
A sign that is attached to, placed upon, printed
on the interior or exterior of a window or door of a
building, or displayed within the interior and clearly 9
intended for public recognition outside the building. E
L
C
A. Standards I
T
R
1. Window signs shall not exceed 25 percent of the
A
area of the window or 12 square feet, whichever is
less.
2. In the case of multi-pane windows, the surface
area of the window shall be the combined surface
area of the individual panes.
3. Window signs may be internally illuminated.
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 217

ARTICLE 9: SIGN STANDARDS
FREESTANDING SIGN TYPES
Section 9.9
FREESTANDING SIGN TYPES
A freestanding sign is a sign that is attached to,
erected on, or supported by a structure that is not
itself an integral part of or attached to a building.
Freestanding signs include, but are not limited to:
post, pylon, pole, pole with cladding, monument, and
yard signs. The number, surface area, and height of
freestanding signs on a lot shall comply with Table
9.6-B: Non-Residential Freestanding Sign Standards,
and meet any of the following standards specific to the
applicable sign type.
[IMAGE]

ARTICLE 9: SIGN STANDARDS
FREESTANDING SIGN TYPES
[IMAGE]
[IMAGE]
9.9.3 Pole Signs
A sign that is supported by one or more poles that
are anchored in the ground, and intended to be
viewed at a distance.
A. Location
Pole signs are permitted only on lots where the front
building façade is located more than 25 feet away
from the front lot line
B. Vertical Clearance
The lowest portion of the sign display shall have a
vertical clearance of at least seven feet above the
grade below.
C. Illumination
A pole sign may be internally or externally
illuminated.
[IMAGE]
9.9.4 Freestanding Canopy Signs
A freestanding canopy sign is a sign that is applied
to, painted on, or mounted to a canopy structure that
is not attached to a building. Freestanding canopies
are typically associated with the accessory drive-
through services of a Vehicle Fueling Station, Car
Wash, Bank, or Restaurant.
A. Sign Area
Freestanding canopy signs shall not exceed 25
percent of the surface area of the façade of the
canopy.
B. Number and Area
The number and sign surface area of freestanding
canopy signs do not count toward the maximum
standards for the other signage on the premises.
C. Projection
Freestanding canopy signs shall have a maximum
projection of 12 inches above the canopy.
D. Illumination
A freestanding canopy sign may be internally or
externally illuminated.

ARTICLE 10: ADMINISTRATION, PROCEDURES, AND ENFORCEMENT
222 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE
Conditional Use Permits
Section 10.1
CONDITIONAL USE PERMITS
10.1.1 Planning Board to
Administer
Wherever a Conditional Use is authorized by this 
Ordinance, the authority to administer or grant 
Conditional Use permits shall be vested in the 
Planning Board. The duration of a Conditional Use 
permit shall be defined by the provisions of Section
10.3.4 Expiration of Permits and Approvals.
10.1.2 Application and Review
Procedure
An application for a Conditional Use shall be initiated 
by filing with the Planning Board for an application for 
a Conditional Use permit. The following procedures 
shall apply to the processing of such application:
A. Procedure if Subdivision or Site 
Plan Approval Also Required
Where other required development approvals for 
a Conditional Use include subdivision or site plan 
approval by the Planning Board, the application 
and review procedure for a Conditional Use permit 
shall be made concurrently and in accordance with 
the procedures specified in the Subdivision and 
Site Plan Review Regulations as applicable to the 
particular development.
B. Procedure if Subdivision or Site 
Plan Approval Not Required
Where no subdivision or site plan approval would 
otherwise be required for the Conditional Use, the 
application and procedural requirements of the Site 
Plan Regulations shall be applied to the application 
and processing of Conditional Use permits with 
respect to content of applications, requirements for 
public notice, hearings and timing of decisions by the 
Planning Board.
10.1.3 Burden of Persuasion
The applicant shall bear the burden of persuasion, 
through the introduction of sufficient evidence by 
testimony or otherwise, that the development, if 
completed as proposed, will comply with this Article 
and will satisfy the specific requirements for the use 
contained in the Ordinance.
10.1.4 Standards of Review
In reviewing an application for a Conditional 
Use permit, the Planning Board shall consider 
the following information in its deliberations, as 
applicable to the case:
A. Authorization
Specific authorization for the Conditional Use in 
Article 4, Table 4.3-A Principal Uses and Table 4.5-A 
Accessory Uses;
B. Compliance
Compliance of the development plan with the specific 
standards for such use contained in this Ordinance;
C. Special Investigation or 
Scientific Study
The results of any special investigative or scientific 
studies prepared in association with the proposed 
development;
D. Special Report or Analysis
Special reports or analysis of the project or its 
impacts, prepared by the City or consultants;
E. City Objectives and Goals
The findings, goals and objectives of the City Master 
Plan;
F. Public Improvement Schedule
The relationship of the development to the timing, 
location and cost of public improvements scheduled 
in the Capital Improvements Program; and
G. Public Hearings
Testimony and evidence introduced at the public 
hearing on the application.
10.1.5 Hearing and Decision
Following a public hearing on the proposed use, the 
Planning Board shall issue a Conditional Use permit, 
if it finds, based on the information and testimony 
submitted with respect to the application, that:
A. Authorization
The use is specifically authorized by Article 4, Table 
4.3-A, Principal Uses and Table 4.5-A Accessory 
Uses;

ARTICLE 10: ADMINISTRATION, PROCEDURES, AND ENFORCEMENT
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 223
Conditional Use Permits
ARTICLE 10
B. Compliance
If completed, the development in its proposed 
location will comply with all requirements of this 
Article, and with specific conditions or standards 
established in this Ordinance for the particular use;
C. Health and Safety
The use will not materially endanger the public 
health or safety;
D. Abutting Properties
The use will not substantially de-value abutting 
property;
E. Compatibility
The use will be compatible with the neighborhood 
and with adjoining or abutting uses in the area in 
which it is to be located;
F. Adverse Impacts on Safety
The use will not have a substantial adverse impact 
on highway or pedestrian safety;
G. Adverse Impacts on the 
Environment
The use will not have a substantial adverse impact 
on the natural and environmental resources of the 
City; and
H. Public Utilities and Community 
Facilities
Adequate public utilities and community facilities 
are available to the property to ensure that the 
proposed use will not necessitate excessive public 
expenditures in providing public services.
10.1.6 Stipulations of Approval
In granting a Conditional Use permit, the Planning 
Board may attach reasonable conditions to its 
approval, including but not limited to the phasing of 
a development, where such conditions are shown 
to be necessary to further the objectives of this 
Ordinance and the master plan, or which would 
otherwise allow the general conditions of this Article 
to be satisfied. Representations made at a public 
hearing, or in material submitted to the Planning 
Board by an applicant, to obtain a Conditional Use 
permit shall be deemed conditions for the issuance 
of the permit. All conditions of approval shall be 
stated in writing in the issuance of a permit. The 
Planning Board may require that such conditions 
be annotated on a site plan or subdivision plan, 
or otherwise recorded at the Hillsborough County 
Registry of Deeds.
10.1.7 Appeals
Any persons aggrieved by a Planning Board 
decision on a Conditional Use permit may appeal 
that decision to the Superior Court, as provided for 
in RSA 677:15. A Planning Board decision on the 
issuance of a Conditional Use permit cannot be 
appealed to the Zoning Board of Adjustment. (RSA 
676:5, III)

ARTICLE 10: ADMINISTRATION, PROCEDURES, AND ENFORCEMENT
224 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE
Appeals to the zoning board of adjustment
Section 10.2
APPEALS TO THE ZONING 
BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT
10.2.1 Zoning Board of
Adjustment (ZBA)
A. Appointment and Terms
Pursuant to RSA 673, Local Land Use Boards, a 
ZBA shall be established, consisting of five members 
and up to five alternate members, all appointed by 
the Mayor subject to confirmation by the Board of 
Mayor and Aldermen for three year terms. Alternate 
members may fulfill the duties and responsibilities 
of a regular member when a regular member is 
disqualified from consideration of a particular 
application.
B. Organization and Rules of 
Procedure
On an annual basis, the ZBA shall elect a chairman 
and other officers from among its membership. 
The ZBA shall adopt, and from time to time amend, 
rules of procedure for the conduct of business. The 
rules of procedure shall establish a regular meeting 
schedule for the consideration of appeals.
10.2.2 Powers and Duties of the
ZBA
A. Interpretation of the Ordinance
The ZBA Shall:
1. Hear and decide appeals where it has been alleged 
that there is an error in any order, requirement, decision, 
or determination by the Director in the administration 
of this Ordinance. The ZBA may affirm or reverse 
such order, requirement, decision, or determination, in 
whole or in part, or may modify the same;
2. Hear and render determinations on any questions 
relative to the meaning of the text of this Ordinance; 
and
3. Hear and render determinations on any questions 
relative to the exact location of any district boundary 
shown on the zoning map.
B. Authorization of Variances
1. Upon appeal, the ZBA may authorize a Variance 
from the terms of this Ordinance for a particular use, 
a parcel of land, an existing structure, or a proposed 
structure only when it determines that all of the following 
five criteria have been satisfied:
a. The Variance will not be contrary to the public 
interest;
b. The spirit of the Ordinance is observed;
c. Substantial justice is done;
d. The values of surrounding properties are not 
diminished; and
e. Literal enforcement of the provisions of the 
Ordinance would result in an unnecessary hardship.
2. Unnecessary Hardship
a. The meaning of “unnecessary hardship,” as used 
in Subsection 1 above, shall be that, owing to special 
conditions of the property that distinguish it from 
other properties in the area:
(1) No fair and substantial relationship exists 
between the general public purposes of the 
Ordinance provision and the specific application of 
that provision to the property; and
(2) The proposed use is a reasonable one.
b. If the criteria in paragraph (a) are not established, 
an unnecessary hardship will be deemed to exist if, 
and only if, owing to special conditions of the property 
that distinguish it from other properties in the area, 
the property cannot be reasonably used in strict 
conformance with the Ordinance, and a Variance is 
therefore necessary to enable a reasonable use of it.
c. The definition of “unnecessary hardship” set forth 
in paragraphs (a) and (b) shall apply whether the 
provision of the Ordinance from which a Variance 
is sought is a restriction on use, a dimensional or 
other limitation on a permitted use, or any other 
requirement of the Ordinance. 
3. The applicant bears the burden of presenting 
evidence sufficient to allow the ZBA to reach conclusions 
and make findings to support the authorization of a 
Variance.
4. In authorizing a Variance, the ZBA may impose such 
conditions and stipulations as it deems necessary and 
proper in order to fulfill the purpose and intent of this 
Ordinance.

ARTICLE 10
5. Variances authorized under Section 10.2.2.B shall be 
valid if exercised within two years from the date of final 
approval, or as further extended by local ordinance or by 
the ZBA for good cause, provided that no such Variance 
shall expire within six months after the resolution of a 
planning application filed in reliance upon the Variance.
6. If after commencement of construction, the property 
is abandoned for a period of two years, then the 
Variance shall be deemed to have expired and cannot 
be re-established without a new application process and 
affirmative decision of the ZBA.
7. Any proposed non-residential Variance request 
located within the Lake Massabesic Protection Overlay 
District shall be forwarded to the Manchester Water 
Works for comment prior to the hearing on the Variance. 
8. The ZBA may grant a Variance from the terms of this 
Ordinance without finding a hardship arising from the 
condition of a premises subject to this Ordinance, and 
thus not comply with Section 10.2.2.B.1.e above, when 
reasonable accommodations are necessary to allow a 
person or persons with a recognized disability to reside 
in or regularly use the premises, provided that:
a. Any Variance granted under this paragraph shall 
be in harmony with the general purpose and intent of 
this Ordinance, and
b. In granting any Variance pursuant to this 
subsection, the ZBA may provide, in a finding 
included in the Variance, that the Variance shall 
survive only so long as the particular person has a 
continuing need to use the premises.
C. Granting of Special Exceptions
1. The ZBA shall hear and decide requests for Special 
Exceptions that are specifically authorized in Article 
4:Uses or otherwise in this Ordinance.
2. The ZBA shall grant a request for a Special Exception 
only where it makes each of the following findings:
a. The use requested is specifically authorized in the 
Ordinance;
b. The requested use will not create undue traffic 
congestion or unduly impair pedestrian safety;
c. The requested use will not overload the public 
utility systems (e.g. sewer and water);
d. The requested use will not create excessive 
demand for municipal police, fire protection, schools, 
or solid waste disposal services;
e. Any requirements and standards for the use as 
set forth in Article 4: Uses, of this Ordinance are 
fulfilled;
f. The requested use will not create hazards to 
the health, safety, or general welfare of the public, 
nor be detrimental to the character of the adjacent 
neighborhood;
g. The proposed location is appropriate for the 
requested use; and
h. The requested use is consistent with the spirit 
and intent of this Ordinance and the Master Plan.
3. The applicant bears the burden of presenting 
evidence sufficient to allow the ZBA to make findings 
required to support the granting of a Special Exception.
4. In granting a Special Exception, the ZBA may attach 
conditions as it deems necessary to assure compliance 
with the purposes of this Ordinance. Such conditions 
may include but are not limited to the following:
a. Increasing the lot size or yard dimensions;
b. Limiting the lot coverage or building height;
c. Specifying the location and the number of 
vehicular curb-cuts to the property;
d. Requiring additional on-site parking or loading 
spaces;
e. Requiring additional landscaping and screening;
f. Limiting the number of occupants of a building, 
and the methods and times of operation of a use;
g. Restricting the number, size, and illumination of 
signs;
h. Modifying the exterior appearance of a building; 
and
i. Providing for specific locations or layout of facilities 
on the property.
5. Special Exceptions authorized under Section
10.2.2.C shall be valid if exercised within two years 
from the date of final approval, or as further extended by 
local ordinance or by the ZBA for good cause, provided 
that no such Special Exception shall expire within six 
months after the resolution of a planning application 
filed in reliance upon the Special Exception. 
6. If, after commencement, a Special Exception is 
abandoned or discontinued for a period of two years, 
then the Special Exception shall be deemed to have 
expired and cannot be re-established without a new 
application process and the affirmative decision of the 
ZBA.

with the purposes of this Ordinance. Such conditions

a. Increasing the lot size or yard dimensions;

c. Specifying the location and the number of

d. Requiring additional on-site parking or loading

f. Limiting the number of occupants of a building,

g. Restricting the number, size, and illumination of 
signs;
h. Modifying the exterior appearance of a building; 
and
i. Providing for specific locations or layout of facilities 
on the property.
5. Special Exceptions authorized under Section
10.2.2.C shall be valid if exercised within two years 
from the date of final approval, or as further extended by 
local ordinance or by the ZBA for good cause, provided 
that no such Special Exception shall expire within six 
months after the resolution of a planning application 
filed in reliance upon the Special Exception.

abandoned or discontinued for a period of two years, 
then the Special Exception shall be deemed to have 
expired and cannot be re-established without a new 
application process and the affirmative decision of the 
ZBA.

ARTICLE 10: ADMINISTRATION, PROCEDURES, AND ENFORCEMENT
226 CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE
Appeals to the zoning board of adjustment
D. Granting of Equitable Waivers
1. When a lot or other division of land, or structure 
thereupon, is discovered to be in violation of a physical 
layout or dimensional requirement imposed by a zoning 
ordinance enacted pursuant to RSA 674:16, the zoning 
board of adjustment shall, upon application by and with 
the burden of proof on the property owner, grant an 
equitable waiver from the requirement, if and only if the 
board makes all of the following findings:
a. That the violation was not noticed or discovered 
by any owner, former owner, owner’s agent or 
representative, or municipal official, until after 
a structure in violation had been substantially 
completed, or until after a lot or other division of land 
in violation had been subdivided by conveyance to a 
bona fide purchaser for value;
b. That the violation was not an outcome of 
ignorance of the law or ordinance, failure to inquire, 
obfuscation, misrepresentation, or bad faith on the 
part of any owner, owner’s agent or representative, 
but was instead caused by either a good faith 
error in measurement or calculation made by an 
owner or owner’s agent, or by an error in ordinance 
interpretation or applicability made by a municipal 
official in the process of issuing a permit over which 
that official had authority;
c. That the physical or dimensional violation does not 
constitute a public or private nuisance, nor diminish 
the value of other property in the area, nor interfere 
with or adversely affect any present or permissible 
future uses of any such property; and
d. That due to the degree of past construction 
or investment made in ignorance of the facts 
constituting the violation, the cost of correction so 
far outweighs any public benefit to be gained, that 
it would be inequitable to require the violation to be 
corrected.
2. In lieu of the findings required by the board 
under Section 10.2.2.D.1(a) and (b), the owner may 
demonstrate to the satisfaction of the board that the 
violation has existed for 10 years or more, and that no 
enforcement action, including written notice of violation, 
has been commenced against the violation during that 
time by the municipality or any person directly affected.
3. Application and hearing procedures for equitable 
waivers under this section shall be governed by Section
10.2.3. 
4. Equitable waivers shall be granted under this section 
only from physical layout, mathematical or dimensional 
requirements, and not from use restrictions. An equitable 
waiver granted under this section shall not be construed 
as a nonconforming use, and shall not exempt future 
use, construction, reconstruction, or additions on the 
property from full compliance with the Ordinance. This 
section shall not be construed to alter the principle that 
owners of land are bound by constructive knowledge 
of all applicable requirements. This section shall not be 
construed to impose upon municipal officials any duty to 
guarantee the correctness of plans reviewed by them or 
property inspected by them.
10.2.3 Application Procedure for
the ZBA
A. Application Fees
A non-refundable fee shall be submitted together with 
an application to cover the costs of the advertising, 
notification, and processing of the application as well 
as any special investigative studies deemed necessary 
by the ZBA.
B. Submission Materials
An application to the ZBA shall include a completed 
application form, plans, and supplemental information 
as may be required for the specific type of appeal. 
The application shall be filed at least 30 days before a 
regularly scheduled meeting of the ZBA.
C. Notification
A notice of a public hearing on an application shall 
be sent to the applicant and to all abutters by verified 
mail, as defined by RSA 451-C:1,VII, not less than 
five days before the date of the hearing. Notice shall 
also be given to the Alderman of the Ward in which the 
application is located. A public notice shall be placed 
in a newspaper of general circulation in the City of 
Manchester, not less than five days before the date of 
the hearing.
D. Public Hearing
At the public hearing, the ZBA shall hear or receive oral 
or written testimony from the applicant, all abutters, and 
any non-abutter who can demonstrate they are directly 
affected. Representations made at the public hearing 
or material submitted to the ZBA shall be deemed to be 
conditions of any decision of the ZBA. The ZBA may 
convene or reconvene the public hearing at the site 
of the proposed use in order to permit observations 
concerning the site to become part of the record of the 
hearing and decision.

ARTICLE 10: ADMINISTRATION, PROCEDURES, AND ENFORCEMENT
CITY OF MANCHESTER, NEW HAMPSHIRE | ZONING ORDINANCE 227
Administration and Enforcement
ARTICLE 10
E. Action on the Application
The ZBA shall approve, deny, or approve with 
conditions, each complete application upon which a 
hearing has been held within the time period required 
by RSA 676:5. Action on an application may be tabled 
from the public hearing to another meeting of the ZBA. 
A concurring vote of three members of the ZBA shall 
be necessary for a decision on an application. 
F. Issuance of a Decision
Within five business days after a vote on an application, 
a written record of the decision shall be available for 
public inspection at the Manchester Planning and 
Community Development Department. The record 
of decision shall state whether the application 
was approved or denied, include any conditions if 
approved, state the reasons for any denial, and be 
accompanied by written findings of fact to support the 
decision. A copy of the record of decision shall be sent 
to the applicant by first class mail, and copies shall 
be made available to the Planning and Community 
Development Department, and the Chairman of the 
Board of Assessors.
G. Rehearing
Within 30 days after a decision of the ZBA, any party 
to the action or any person directly affected thereby 
may apply for a rehearing in respect to any matter 
determined in the decision, and must specify such 
grounds in the motion for rehearing. The ZBA may 
grant a rehearing if, in the opinion of the ZBA, the 
original decision was based on legal or factual error, 
or if new evidence material to the decision has been 
found since the decision.
H. Subsequent Applications
Once an application has been denied by the ZBA, 
the same application may be considered as a new
